lawyer:
Dr. Md. Eunus Ali Akond Advocate ------ Petitioner in person.
Mr. A. Baset Majumder, Senior Advocate with Mr. M. Sayed Ahmed, Advocate and Mr. Sajed Ahammad Sami, Advocate ------- For the Respondent.
parties:
DR. MD. EUNUS ALI AKOND ADVOCATE, ADVOCATE, BANGLADESH SUPREME COURT, BANGLADESH SUPREME COURT BAR ASSOCIATION, POLICE STATION-SHAHBAG, DHAKA.
Vs.
Mr. Md. Mofazzal Hossain Chowdhury Maya, Member of Parliament (M.P) and Minister for Disaster Management and Relief, Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh, Secretariat, Dhaka.
full_judgment:
Syed Refaat Ahmed, J: This Application under Article 102(2)(b)(ii) of the Constitution has sought inter alia the issuance of a Rule Nisi calling upon the sole Respondent to show cause as to under what authority he claims to hold the Offices of a Member of Parliament and of Minister of the Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh in violation of the provisions of Articles 66(2)(d) and 67(1)(d) of the Constitution. There is also an accompanying prayer for an Order of injunction restraining the sole Respondent from functioning as a Member of Parliament and Minister till disposal of any Rule Nisi as may be issued.

2. The said Application as initially placed before a regularly constituted Bench of this Court attracted a split Order of 17.8.2015. That merited, therefore, the subsequent reference of the Matter to this specially constituted Bench by an Order of 10.11.2015 signed by the Hon'ble Judge performing the functions of the Hon'ble Chief Justice of Bangladesh.

<u>3. A consideration of the Application with two Supplementary Affidavits filed and of facts and issues preliminarily presented reveals that the sole Respondent was convicted for offence involving moral turpitude on 14.2.2008. Criminal Appeal No. 3536 of 2009 arising from such conviction secured to the Respondent a bail pending hearing of that Appeal from the High Court Division on 4.6.2009. This, however not having the effect of suspension of the conviction per se the Respondent is noted, thereafter, to have obtained another Order in the said Criminal Appeal Case from the High Court Division on 16.2.2010. By this Order the High Court Division stayed the operation of the Respondent's conviction and sentence allowing his application under Section 426(1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure albeit in a modified form. It is noted that such stay was granted till disposal of the underlying Appeal.</u>

<u>4. It is against the backdrop of the above two Orders in Criminal Appeal No. 3536 of 2009 that the Respondent came to be acquitted of the charge levelled against him and discharged from his bail bond by the Judgment and Order of the High Court Division on 27.10.2010. This gave rise to Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 107 of 2011 that eventually came to be disposed of by the Appellate Division on 14.6.2015 setting aside the Impugned Judgment of 27.10.2010 and sending the case back to the High Court Division on remand for disposal afresh on merit expeditiously.</u>

5. Noted further is the filing of Criminal Review Petition No. 49 of 2015 by the Respondent arising out of CPLA No. 107 of 2.011 under an Affidavit affirmed on 2.8.2015. The learned Advocates for the Respondent Mr. M. Sayed Ahmed and Mr. Sajed Ahammad Sami submit that significantly an accompanying application for permission to swear such Affidavit to the Review Petition without surrender has been filed and permitted.

6. In the above facts. and circumstances, and upon a consideration of the ratio decidendi, in particular, of two Judgments cited by the Petitioner i.e. H M Ershad Vs. A. M. Chowdhury and another reported in 10 BLT (HCD) 2002, 163 and Husssain Mohammad Ershad v. Zahedul Islam Khan reported in 21 BLD (AD) 2001, 142, the core issue for this Court's consideration has been the date until which the Order of the Respondent's conviction and sentence of 14.2.2008 remained operative. That date, in the facts and circumstances, appears to be 16.2.2010 on which date the Order of Stay was granted by the High Court Division in Criminal Appeal No. 3536 of 2009 pursuant to an application under Section 426(1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure. The resultant moot question is whether, therefore, the Respondent suffered any constitutional disability under Article 66(2)(d) at any time after 14.2.2008 and, more significantly, on the date that his nomination paper for election to legislative office was placed under scrutiny. Both the Respondent and the Petitioner himself, Dr. Akond confirm that it is only upon the Respondent's conviction and sentence of 14.2.2008 being made inoperative on 16.2.2010 and followed by the acquittal. Order of 27.10.2010 as above noted, did the Respondent come to first contest the Parliamentary Elections held on 5.1.2014. The Respondent so contested the Election during pendency of CPLA No. 107 of 2011. It is further affirmed by the learned Advocates for the Respondent that the last date of submission of nomination paper for the said Election was 2.12.2013 and the dates of scrutiny of the same were 5.12.2013 and 6.12.2013. It is found, therefore, that on the latter sets of dates in December 2013 i.e. at the time of scrutiny of nomination paper, there was no Order of conviction and sentence operative against the Respondent by virtue of the Order of the High Court Division issued under Section 426(1) in the Code of Criminal Procedure on 16.2.2010.

7. By reason of the above, this Court finds no prima facie ground to issue a Rule Nisi and remains disinclined to a favourable consideration of the prayers in this Application.

8. In the result, the Application stands summarily rejected.

End.

lawyer:
Mr. Mohammad Saifullah Mamun with Mr. Abdullah Al Hady, Advocates ----- For the Petitioner. 
Mr. Kamal-Ul- Alam, Senior Advocate with Mr. Md. Mizanul Hoque Chowdhury with Mr. Md. Masud Alam, Advocates ------ For the opposite party No.1.
parties:
STX CORPORATION, STX NAMSAN TOWER, 631 NAMDAEMUNNO 5-GA, 
JUNG-GU, SEOUL, REPUBLIC OF KOREA 100-503.
Vs.
MR. MOSTAFA KAMAL AND ANOTHER
full_judgment:
Md. Nuruzzaman, J. On an application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure the instant Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party No. 1 to show cause as to why the impugned order No. 11 dated 10.7.2014 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka rejecting an application under order 7 Rule 11(d) of the Code of Civil Procedure for rejection of the plaint should not be set aside.

2. The material facts, relevant for disposal of the instant Rule, in short, are that, the opposite party No. 1 as plaintiff instituted the Title Suit No. 264 of 2014 against the defendants praying for following reliefs.

a. For a declaration that the purported proforma invoice dated 09.06.2008 is manufactured, concocted and fabricated as afterthought and, as such, the said pro-forma invoice dated 09.06.2008 is illegal, unlawful and void.

b. For a declaration that there is no arbitration agreement in between the plaintiff and defendant No. I and, as such, the defendant No. 1 initiated the said arbitration being Arbitration No. ARB021/11/AG before Singapore International Arbitration Centre illegally, unlawfully and the said initiation of the said arbitration and subsequent proceeding thereof including the awards given therein are void and do not have any binding effect upon the plaintiff.

c. For a declaration that the Preliminary Award dated 05.04.2012 and Final Award dated 23.10.2013 passed in the Arbitration No. ARB02/11/AG before Singapore International Arbitration Centre against the plaintiff are illegal, unlawful, unenforceable, ineffective and void and the said Preliminary Award dated 05.042012 and Final Award dated 23.10.2013 do not have any binding effect upon the plaintiff.

d. For a permanent injunction restraining the defendant No. 1 from making any claim and /or taking any prejudicial step against the plaintiff on the basis of /pursuant to the final award dated 23.10.2013 passed in the Arbitration No. ARB021/11/AG by the Singapore International Arbitration Centre.

e. For any other relief or relies as the court may deem fit and proper.

3. The suit while was so pending, the defendant No. 1 filed an application under order-7 Rule 11(d) read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for rejection of the plaint of the instant suit.

4. The plaintiff as opposite party filed a written objection against the application for rejection of the plaint. The learned Joint District Judge upon hearing both the sides by his judgment and order dated 10.07.2014 rejected the application for rejection of the plaint.

5. The defendants as petitioner feeling aggrieved invoked the revisional jurisdiction under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure and there by preferred the instant revision and obtained the instant Rule with an order of stay.

6. The petitioner in support of his revisional application filed two supplementary affidavits in Court one dated 13.01.2015 and 2nd one dated 05.11.2017. In both the supplementary affidavit he annexed the plaint of title Suit No. 264 of 2014 and another judgment of Arbitration passed by the SISE in Arbitration No. 21/2011 (ARB- 021/11 AG).

7. Mr. Md. Saifullah Mamun the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner has submitted that the Court below committed an error law resulting an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice in not considering that the Title suit No. 264 of 2014 is directly barred by the provision of the Section 7 read with Section 45 of the Arbitration Act, 2001 and in pursuance of Order VII Rule 11(d) of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 the plaint of the suit shall be rejected and, as such, the impugned order is not tenable under law and calls for interference by this Hon'ble Court.

8. He has also submitted that the Court below committed an error of law resulting an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice in not considering that the Opposite Party filed the Title Suit 264 of 2014 intending to frustrate the clear right of the petitioner to execute the Final Award filed in the Court of the District Judge, Dhaka under Section 45 of the Arbitration Act 2001 because they had accepted the jurisdiction of the Arbitral Tribunal at the Singapore Courts and contested the arbitration and challenged it, and, as such, the impugned order is not tenable under law and calls for interference by this Hon'ble Court.

9. He has further submitted that the Court below committed an error of law resulting an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice in not considering that the Title Suit No. 264/2014 and the impugned order arises out of an arbitration agreement governed by Singapore laws requiring arbitration under the International Arbitration Act of Singapore and which had been invoked by the petitioner leading to the preliminary Award on Jurisdiction declaring the Opposite Party to be the contracting party which declaration was challenged by the Opposite party unsuccessfully in proceedings between the same parties in respect of the same subject matter in the Singapore High Court and therefore the Opposite Party cannot re-litigate the same issues before the learned Court below, however the learned Court below upon misreading the facts of case passed the impugned order and, as such, the impugned order is misconceived, illegal and is not tenable under law and calls for interference by this Hon'ble Court and liable to be set aside.

10. Ile argued that the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka gave a findings in the impugned order that section 7 of the Arbitration Act, 2001 will not attract in the Title Suit No. 264 of 2014, which is vague, improper and not true. The opposite party in the written objection gave submission that as per section 3 of the Arbitration Act and as per unreported case M/S Uzbekistan Airways vs. M/S Air Span Ltd. In Civil petition for leave to appeal No. 1112 of 2005 and 2(two) other cases cited in 10 BLC 617 and 64 DLR550, only sections 45,46 and 47 shall apply to the foreign arbitration award and Court below on the basis of such submission stated that section 7 will not attract in the Title Suit No. 264 of 2014. But it is enacted in Section 7 which is as follows:

৭। সালিশ চুক্তির আওতাভূক্ত বিষয়ে আদালতের এখতিয়ার।– সালিশ চুক্তির কোন পক্ষ অপর কোন পক্ষের বিরুদ্ধে উক্ত চুক্তির অধীনে সালিসে অর্পণে সম্মত কোন বিষয়ে আইনগত কার্যধারা রুজু করিলে, বর্তমানে প্রচলিত অন্য কোন আইনে যাহাই থাকুক না কেন, এই আইনের বিধান ব্যতীত অন্য কোন আইনগত কার্যধারার শুনানীর এখতিয়ার আদালতের থাকিবে না।” which clearly indicates that no other section of this Act or any other provision of any Act shall be applicable or override the provision of section 7 of this Act. Therefore, section 3 has no effect upon the provision of section 7 and for this reason as per provision of section 7 the Title Suit No. 264 of 2014 is barred by law. Therefore, the learned Court below committed error of law in passing the impugned Order which resulted failure of justice and, as such, the impugned order is needed to be interfered by this Hon'ble Court and liable to set aside.

11. He has further argued that the learned Court below committed an error of law resulting an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice in not considering that the Final Award was made after contest and not being challenged at all for which the petitioner is entitled to enforce as an award of an international commercial Arbitration under section 45 of the Arbitration Act 2001 for which the impugned order passed in Title Suit No. 264 of 2014 seeks to prevent the legal and lawful proceeding of earlier with malafide intention and, as such, the suit is nothing but vexatious litigation and an outright abuse of the process of law. Thus, passing the impugned order resulted in an error of law occasioning failure of justice and, as such, the impugned order is not tenable under law and calls for interference by this Hon'ble Court.

12. He has also argued that the Hon'ble Court below committed an error of law resulting an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice in not considering that the issue of multiple proceedings in respect of the same subject matter between the same parties cannot be decided twice which does not permissible with the rule of law as envisaged in our constitution and hence, the impugned order is liable to be set aside.

13. He has submitted in a same breath that the Hon'ble Court below committed an error

of law resulting an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice in not considering that the vexatious proceeding has been started instituting Title Suit No. 264 of 2014 and the impugned order is adversely affecting and tainting the legitimate expectation of the petitioner which was disposed of earlier in accordance with law and is an illegal obstruction to enforce the Final Award passed by foreign Arbitrator in Bangladesh in accordance with law and, as such, the impugned order is liable to be set aside.

14. Mr. Mamun in support of his contentions cited the unreported judgment passed in Civil Petition for leave to appeal No. 43 of 15, to the case of HRC Shipping Limited Vs. MV X-Press Manaslu and others reported in 12 MLR (FICD) 265, to the case of ECOM Agro industrial Corp. Ltd Vs. Mosharaf Composite Textile Mils Ltd reported in 13 BLT (HCD) 42, to the case of Chief Engineer Roads & Highways Department Vs. Concord Engineers & Construction Ltd. reported in 48 DLR (FICD) 243.

l5. In view of his submissions and facts and circumstances of the case he prays for making the Rule absolute allowing the application under order 7 Rule 11 (d) of the Code of Civil Procedure.

16. The opposite party No. 1 and 2 contested the Rule by filing counter affidavit. It has been stated in counter affidavit, inter-alia that in view of the provision of section-3 of the Arbitration Act, 2001 the provision of Section 7 of the Arbitration Act, 2001, have no manner of application in the case of foreign Arbitration. The Court below committed no error of law in passing the impugned judgment and order rejecting the application under order 7 Rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure 1908 holding the section 7 of the Arbitration Act has no manner of application in the instant case.

17. Mr. Kamal-ul-Alam, the learned Advocate has submitted that the application filed under order 7 Rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure has no manner of application in the instant suit because under the provision of section 7 and 10 of the Arbitration Act, 2001 the Court cannot reject the plaint of a suit. However, he concede that according to the aforesaid provision any suit file without invoking the Arbitration clause as stipulated in the agreement in that case the suit may be stayed unless Arbitration clause exhausted. However, the plaint of the suit cannot be rejected. Mr. Alam has further submitted that the plaint has disclosed the cause of action and the relief sought by the plaintiffs can only address after appreciation of the evidence. Therefore, an application for rejection of the plaint is not maintainable in the present case as the defendant is non but the petitioner as per the judgment and proceedings of a foreign Arbitration.

l8. Mr. Alam in support of his contentions referred the section 3 of the Arbitration Act and submitted that the foreign judgment passed in a Arbitration proceedings would not be enforceable save an accept following the provision of Sections 45, 46 and 47 of the Arbitration Act of 2001. Therefore, the application for rejection of the plaint is misconceived. Mr. Alam has further argued that the plaintiff opposite party was not the party to the agreement and, as such, any stipulation including the Arbitration as set forth in the agreement is not binding upon the plaintiff. Therefore, in reference the proceedings of Arbitration the plaint of the suit cannot be rejected. However, in support of his contentions he has cited some decisions which are to the case of STX Corporation Ltd. Vs. Meghna Group of Industries Limited and others reported in 64 DLR 550, to the case of Unicol Bangladesh Blocks Thirteen and Fourteen Limited (formerly named Occidental of Bangladesh Limited) and another Vs. Max well Engineering Works Ltd. reported in 13 BLT (AD) 106, to the case of Maico Jute and Bag Corporation Vs. Bangladesh Jute Mills Corporation and others reported in 55 DLR(AD)23.

19. We have gone through the revision application, the impugned order dated 10.07.2014, the plaint of title suit No. 264 of 2014. The judgment passed by SIA Arbitrator in the Arbitration Case No. 21.21(ARB-021/11/AG) which is the Annexure A.A of the supplementary affidavit dated 13.01.2015.

20. On perusal the annexure DD the plaint of Title suit No. 264 of 2014 it appears that the plaintiff sought for declaration that the purported pro-forma invoice dated 09.06.2008 is manufactured concocted, fabricated, illegal, unlawful and void. He has further prayed for a declaration that there is no Arbitration agreement between the plaintiff and defendant No. 1 and, as such, the defendant No. 1 initiated Arbitration being Arbitration No. ARB 021/ 11/ AG before Singapore International Arbitration Centre is illegal, unlawful and the said initiation of the said Arbitration and subsequent proceedings thereof including the award given therein are void and do not have any binding effect upon the plaintiffs. He has further also prayed for preliminary award dated 5.4.2012 and final Award dated 23.10.2013 passed in the aforesaid Arbitration is illegal, unlawful, unenforceable, ineffective and not binding upon the plaintiff He has also prayed for permanent injunction against the defendant No. 1 for making any claim in pursuance of the final Award dated 23.1.2013 passed in the Arbitration No. ARB 021/11/ AG by Singapore International Arbitration Centre.

<u>21. On perusal of the prayer of the plaint it is clearly divulged that the plaintiff in the suit claim that he is not the party to the agreement. However, on the other hand he prayed for several relief against the judgment of Arbitration which arose from the aforesaid agreement. On perusal of the judgment of Singapore International Arbitration Centre dated 23.10.2013 passed in Arbitration No. ARB 021/11/AG the plaintiff as a party contested the aforesaid proceedings and the same point was raised by the plaintiff before the Arbitration in Singapore. Thereafter the Singapore International Arbitration Centre passed the preliminary Award against the plaintiffs including others which was produced before the learned District Judge, Dhaka to enforce the same. The learned District Judge dismissed the said execution case being No. 22 of 2014 against which the present petitioner preferred the Civil Revision No. 3338 of 2014. Thereafter the petitioner herein filed an application to convert the Civil Revision to F.A. as the impugned order dated 23.07.201.4 passed by the learned District Judge, Dhaka was not revisable rather it was appealable. The said revisional application was converted to an appeal by competent bench of this Court which is till now pending for decision.</u>

22. We have gone through the decision cited by the learned Advocates of the respective parties. We have also considered the judgment passed in civil petition for leave to Appeal No. 43 of 2015 to the case of Mosharaf Composite Textile Mills Ltd --vs-ECOM Agro Industrial Corp Ltd and others. On perusal the same it is revealed that in the similar occasion the High Court Division stayed the proceedings of the suit and which was also upheld by the Appellate Division. We do not find any point and facts to distinguish in the present case from the facts and circumstances of the referred case. Therefore, we cannot but to obey the dictum enunciated by the Hon'ble Appellate Division in Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 43 of 2015.

<u>23. However, on perusal the decisions referred by the learned Advocate for the opposite parties except the decision reported in 55 DLR (AD) 23 it appears that the facts and question of law as decided by the Hon'ble Appellate Division in two other cases are quite distinguishable from the facts and question of law of the present case. Therefore, though we are not disagreeing with that dictum however, we are unable to make those dictum acceptable in the present case.</u>

<u>24. On perusal the decision of 55 DLR(AD)23 we are of the view that it is not helpful for the opposite parties, rather, in favour of the petitioner. Therefore, we also relied upon the decision of Maico Jute and Bag Corporation reported 55 DLR (AD) 23 which is squarely applicable in the case in hand as facts and law are quite similar.</u>

25. In that view of the matter we are of the considered view that justice would be best served if the proceedings of title Suit No. 264 of 2014 is stayed until disposal of the F.M.A.T. No. 112 of 2016 now pending before this Division. Accordingly, the further proceeding of Title Suit No. 264 of 2014 is hereby stayed until disposal of the First Miscellaneous Appeal No. 112 of 2016.

26. Therefore, the instant revisional application is disposed of with the above observation and direction.

27. The office is directed to communicate the order at once.

End.

lawyer:
Mr. A.J. Mohammad Ali with Mr. Subrata Saha, Advocates ------- For the petitioners. 
Mr. M.M. Haque Siddique Rana, Advocate ------- For the opposite parties.
parties:
AKBAR ALI @ MD. AKBAR ALI AND OTHERS
Vs.
REASUDDIN BEING DEAD HIS LEGAL HEIRS 1(A) 
MD. ANWAR HOSSAIN AND OTHERS
full_judgment:
Khizir Ahmed Choudhury, J: This rule has been issued calling upon the opposite parties to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 02.8.2001 passed by learned Subordinate Judge and Artha Rin Adalat, Mymensingh in Other Class Appeal No.86 of 1999 affirming the order dated 26.1.1999 passed by learned Assistant Judge, Bhaluka, Mymensingh in Partition Suit No.47 of 1990 should not be set aside and or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may deem fit and proper.

2. The opposite party No. 1 as plaintiff instituted Partition Suit being Partition Suit No.83 of 1981, being renumbered as Partition Suit No.47 of 1990. The present petitioners were defendant Nos. 57(gha) and 59 in the aforesaid suit. The suit was decreed ex-parte in preliminary form on 15.5.1996. The petitioner and another filed a written objection on 19.09.1995 against the report of the advocate Commissioner. Learned Senior Assistant Judge, Bhaluka by order dated 26.1.1999 rejected the written objection filed by the petitioner, accepted the reports submitted by advocate commissioner and subsequently drawn final decree on 08.3.1999.

3. The petitioner preferred Other Class Appeal No. 86 of 1999 before the District Judge, Maymensingh against the final decree and after hearing learned Subordinate Judge and Aurtho Rin Adalat, Maymensingh dismissed the appeal by judgment and order dated 02.8.2001 against which the instant rule.

4. Mr. A.J. Mohammad Ali along with Mr. Subrata Saha, learned advocates appeared for the petitioner. Mr. A.J. Mohammad Ali learned advocate submits that admittedly the petitioners are co-sharers in the suit land and the total quantum of suit land is 48.43 acres which plaintiffs claim is only 0.55 acres of land for which he got decree in preliminary form. He next submits that after allotting the share to the plaintiff vast tract of land remained as residuary shares and out of that some other defendants namely defendant Nos.94, 189, 190, 199, 73, 113, 111 obtained saham regarding 27.64 acres of land by filing an application, even though they did not submit any sorts of documents in support of their claim, but in spite of filing of relevant documents by the petitioner, the Court below did not consider the documents and objection and without adverting the same rejected the objection which caused failure of justice. He next submits that the appellate Court dismissed the appeal citing some technical ground regarding particular date being erroneously mentioned in the memo of appeal which is technical in nature. He next submits that before drawing up final decree the petitioner filed objection and as such it was incumbent upon the trial Court to consider the contents of the written objection and to direct the advocate commissioner to cause inquiry whether the petitioner is entitled to get his claimed saham from the residuary property, but the trial Court without any consideration rejected the same and drew final decree which caused failure of justice. Apart from this petitioner Nos. 2(a) 2(i) filed an application for allotment of saham in respect of 4.04 acres of land in favour of them.

5. Mr. M.M. Haque Siddique Rana, learned advocate appearing for the opposite party submits that after preliminary decree, the opposite party filed an application for appointment of advocate commissioner for demarcating his land and accordingly advocate commissioner went to the locality and thereafter allotted specific saham to the plaintiff opposite party and consequently the trial Court has drawn final decree in pursuance of the commissioner's report and as such the present approach of the petitioner for allotting saham to them from residuary property is not sustainable. He next submits that since the petitioner did not contest the suit in spite of service of summons, their share has not been allotted by the Court and as such they are not entitled to get any share by filing belated application.

6. Mr. Rana in support of his contention referred the case of Alekjan Bewa and others vs. Alefa Bewa and others reported in 7 ADC 593, Aziz Ahmed and another vs. Khorsheda Begum alias Monwara Begum and others reported in 7 MLR Al) 25, Md. Atar Ali Sheikh and others vs. Md. Karam Ali Sheikh and others reported in 11 BLT 444 and Syeda Khatoon Vs Abdur Rahaman being dead his heirs 1(a) Abdus Salam and others reported in 6 MLR AD 234.

7. It appears from the findings of the learned Assistant Judge that the petitioner did not raise objection against the ex-parte judgment and decree and specifically did not raise any particular objection regarding the commissioner's report and the petitioner also took no step against the ex-parte judgment and decree whereby suit land has been ordered to be partitioned, consequently learned Assistant Judge by the same order drawn final decree. The appellate Court held that the any infirmity in the trial Court's judgment regarding preliminary decree cannot be considered at the time of hearing of objection regarding the report filed by the commissioner. The appellate Court also held that in the memo of appeal order dated 13.1.1999 has been challenged but in fact the impugned order has been passed on 26.1.1999 and as such from that count also the appeal is not maintainable.

8. After preferring the instant revisional application the petitioners by filing an application with annexing certain documents prayed for allotment of saham regarding 4.04 acres of land to petitioner No.1 and 11.75 acres of land for petitioner 2(a)-2(i). In the application the ownership in the suit land and other related documents have been placed and urged to allot saham in respect of the land as mentioned therein.

9. Mr. Subrata Saha urged that due to inadvertence supporting documents of title of the petitioner could not be filed and as such the shares regarding 11.75 acres of land should be allotted to the petitioners contending that out of 48.43 acres of land plaintiffs have got .55 acres of land while other defendants have got 27.94 acres of land and even after allotment of saham to the petitioners still Other lands will remain as residuary property.

10. It appears that the petitioner-defendant did not raise any specific plea regarding their claimed share and the infirmity in doing commission work by the Advocate Commissioner, so the trial Courts findings regarding the objection cannot be termed as perverse and the appellate Court also concurred with that findings. The appellate Courts finding regarding not mentioning actual date of impugned order is not tenable as because certified copy having filed by the petitioner reveals actual date of the impugned order.

<u>11. On perusal of the decisions as referred by the learned advocate of the opposite party it appears that before final decree any share can be allotted to the co-sharer in spite of his not having contested to the original suit, if he can prove his title and possession over any residuary shares of any partible property but after pronouncement of final decree there is little scope to consider any co-sharer's claim regarding allotment of share out of residuary ejmali property. In the case of Alekjan Bewa and others vs. Alefa Bewa and others reported in 7 ADC 593, Aziz Ahmed and another vs. Khorsheda Begum alias Monwara Begum and others reported in 7 MLR AD 25, Md. Atar Ali Sheikh and others vs. Md. Karam Ali Sheikh and others reported in 11 BLT 44 similar views are reiterated by our apex Court.</u>

12. Total partible land is 48.43 acres out of which plaintiffs claim is only 0.55 acres which has been allotted to him by the Advocate Commissioner and accordingly, final decree has been drawn up. Another 27.94 acres of land has been allotted to other defendant from residuary shares. Apart from the allotted shares still there remained residuary property wherefrom the present petitioners are claiming 15.79 acres of land. In the application for allotting saham the petitioner submitted certain photoset copies of the document in support of their claim. On perusal of the documents it appears that those are old and ancient one but its veracity cannot be ascertained because of having not formally proved. But since residuary shares still remains, the genuineness of the documents and other aspects should be investigated without upsetting the share and possession allotted to the plaintiff opposite party as well as the defendant opposite parties to whom specific shares have been allotted as per showing of the Advocate Commissioner. The trial Court can depute the said Advocate who held investigation regarding the suit land allotting the shares to the plaintiff and other defendants and if, the said advocate commissioner is not available or found absent another advocate commissioner can be deputed for considering petitioners claim out of residuary properties. But before that the petitioners are required to submit all title deeds and other required papers in original or in absence of originals by producing certified copies with due explanation thereof, for making proper inquiry regarding the claim of the petitioner and as such final decree passed by the trial Court is required to be set aside as because keeping the final decree intact inquiry cannot be held regarding the title and other aspect of the petitioners claim.

13. In the above context, the final decree dated 26.01.1999 passed by learned Assistant Judge, Bhaluka, Maymensingh and the judgment and decree dated 02.8.2001 passed by erstwhile Subordinate Judge and Artha Rin Adalat, Mymensingh are hereby set aside. The shares allotted to the plaintiff-opposite parties and the defendant-opposite parties by the Advocate Commissioners report as well as possession will remain intact. If any further commission is held and after examining and scrutinizing the documents submitted by the petitioners if the petitioners are entitled to get any share from residuary properties it cannot anyway affect the plaintiff opposite parties share and possession as well as the defendant opposite parties share and possession which they have got meanwhile.

14. The trial Court is directed to cause inquiry about the documents of the present petitioner as expeditiously as possible preferably within 4(four) months from the receipt of the order and also to procure commission report within that period without granting any adjournment to the parties concerned.

15. Accordingly, the rule is made absolute without any order as to cost.

16. The order of stay granted at the time of issuance of the rule is hereby re-called and vacated.

17. Send down the lower Courts records.

18. Communicate the order.

End.

lawyer:
Sarwar Hasan Faruque, Advocate ------- For the Petitioners.

parties:
Abul Hashem Chowdhury and others -------- Petitioners
Vs
Md Jobaid Iqbal and others ---------- Opposite-Parties
full_judgment:
Ahmed Sohel, J: Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party Nos. 1-5 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and order dated 26-6-2005 passed in other suit No. 191 of 2000 by the Joint District Judge, 3rd Court, Chittagong should not be set aside.

2. The short facts necessary for disposal of the rule are that the plaintiff opposite party Nos. 1-5 filed the suit in the Court of the 3rd Subordinate Judge, Chittagong praying for decree for declaration of title simplicitor and for declaration that the BS Khatian is wrong. Earlier they also filed another suit being other Suit No. 108 of 1999 in the Court of 5th Assistant Judge, Chittagong for the self same land and that was withdrawn on 17-10-2000 with permission to sue afresh subject to payment of costs. Thereafter, the plaintiff filed the present suit on 30-10-2000.

3. That during pendency of the present suit the plaintiff opposite party on 12-8-2004 filed an application under Order VI, rule 17 of the Code of Civil Procedure for amendment of plaint (Annexure C to the Civil Revision) by adding a new paragraph after paragraph No. 13 of the plaint i.e. a new paragraph No. 14 stating that during preparation of the plaint certain important provisions of law and relevant necessary facts could not be stated which was a bonafide mistake on the part of the plaintiff. Their contention is that the proposed amendment would not change the nature and character of the suit rather it is necessary to resolve the real controversy between the parties.

4. Against this backdrop, the defendant petitioners also filed a written objection (Annexure D to the civil revision) against the application for amendment of the plaint and prayed for rejection of amendment of the plaint stating mainly that it would change the nature and character of the suit. The proposed amendment is actually a substitution of plaint and, as such, the application for amendment is liable to be rejected.

5. That after hearing both the parties the learned Joint District Judge vide order No. 33 dated 26-6-2005 allowed the application for amendment.

6. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid impugned order No. 33 dated 26-6-2005 passed in other class suit No. 191 of 2000 by the Joint District Judge, 3rd Court, Chittagong, the present petitioners preferred the revisional application and obtained the instant Rule.

7. Mr Sarwar Hasan Faruque the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that the proposed amendment is allowed without considering the fact that it is 33 typed pages of amendment which is actually a substitution plaint with new claim of the plaintiff. The Court below acted illegally in allowing the amendment application in particular it is introduction of new causes of actions and it would change the nature and character of the suit and also it is not at all aimed for adjudicating the real controversy between the parties. In support of his submissions, he relied upon the decision of Norendra Chandra Dash vs Md Solaiman Chowdhury reported in 51 DLR 81 and Shamsul Haque alias Rain Mia vs Shaukat Ali alias Babul Bhuiyan reported in BCR 1985 (AD) 45 and accordingly, he prayed for making the rule absolute.

8. On the other hand Mr Khurshid Alam Khan the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite party along with Mr Zainul Abedin, Advocate contested the rule and submits that by allowing the amendment in particular by adding paragraph No. 14 in the plaint, it would not at all change the nature and character of the suit and he further submits that the learned court below on proper consideration of plaint, application for amendment of plaint and other documents, rightly allowed the application for amendment of plaint as it is necessary to determine the real question in controversy. Further, he submits that it will not prejudice to the other party's right to submit their written statement. Accordingly he prayed for discharging the Rule.

9. We have heard the learned counsels for both the parties with profound attention and considered the above submissions and also gone through the revisional application, application for amendment, written objection, impugned order and other materials on record and decisions of our Apex court relating to amendment of plaint, very carefully.

10. In a case of South Korean Distilleries vs Pravakar Gajanon Naik reported in AIR 2009 SC 1177, it has been held by the Indian Supreme Court that "It is well settled that court will be liberal in allowing amendment if the court is of the view that party seeking amendment would suffer irreparable loss and injury if the amendment is not allowed."

11. Further, it was held in the case of Managing Committee, NMC Model High School vs Obaidur Rahman reported in 31 DLR (AD) 133 that "The other object of the rule is to avoid multiplicity of proceedings and in a proper case the pleading should be allowed to be amended."

12. Similar view has been expressed in the Indian Jurisdiction in the case of Nichha bhai vs Jeswantlal reported in AIR 1966 SC 997.

13. For better understanding, Order VI, rule 17 of the Code of Civil Procedure is quoted below:

R17—Amendment of pleadings—"The Court may at any stage of the proceedings allow either party to alter or amend his pleadings in such manner and on such terms as may be just, and all such amendments shall be made as may be necessary for the purpose of determining the real questions in controversy between the parties"

14. Now the Judicial Committee of the Privy Council in the Case of Ma Shwe Mya vs Maung Mo Hnaung reported in AIR 1922 PC 249 wherein it has been slated how the Court should exercise its power under the rule and what are the limitations in the exercise of such power. The observations are as follows;

"All rules of the Court are nothing but provisions intended to secure the proper administration of justice, and it is therefore essential that they should be made to serve and be subordinate to that purpose, so that full powers of amendment must be enjoyed and should always be liberally exercised, but nonetheless no power has yet been given to enable one distinct cause of action to be substituted for another, nor to change by means of amendment the subject matter of the suit."

15. It is now well settled that under Order VI, rule 17 of the Code of Civil Procedure that an amendment of pleading can be allowed at any stage of the proceedings by any court from the lower tier up to the Apex Court if such amendment is necessary to determine the real controversy in between the parties provided it would not change the nature and character of the suit and also it would not prejudice to the other party.

16. Further, it is also settled principle of law that when the conditions for allowing amendment are fulfilled, the court is required to allow it, even though the court thinks that party seeking amendment will not be able to establish the necessary facts.

17. Furthermore, truth or falsity of the case put in the amendment need not be considered while considering whether amendment should be allowed. Merits of a proposed amendment need not to be gone into at the stage of allowing the amendment, decided in the case of Rajesh Kumar Agarwal vs KK Modi reported in AIR 2006 SC 1647.

18. Now keeping in mind, all these principles relating to amendment of plaint, we have thoroughly gone through the amendment application and found that by adding paragraph No. 14 (Annexure-C to the civil revision) in the plaint in our opinion, the proposed amendments do not introduce a new cause of action or a new case but amounts no more than a different or additional approach to the facts already on record. Although it is a lengthy amendment however in our view nature and character of the present suit does not change as the fundamental character of the suit remains the same, i.e. no fundamental or radical change has occurred to the suit. On the contrary, it would help to determine the real controversy between the parties and also would avoid multiplicity of proceedings.

19. In the case of Abdul Motaleb vs Ershad Ali 1998 BLD (AD) 121 = 4 BLC (AD) 150 it has been held that "the nature and character of a suit do not change so long as the fundamental character of the suit remains the same."

20. Similar view has been expressed in the case of Md Sirajuddin vs Mohibunessa reported in 12 BLT (AD) 138 "merely because an amendment brings something new from what has been stated in the plaint, it cannot be disallowed unless it changes the character of the suit."

21. Furthermore, by allowing this amendment the defendant petitioners would not be prejudiced as because if necessary they would also have the opportunity to file additional/ further written statement on their behalf.

22. It has been decided in the case of Monjur Morshed vs Monjur Hasan reported in 7 BLT (AD) 21 that even if the court does not direct filing of written statement, the defendant will have the right to file it after amendment of plaint.

23. Therefore, in any view of the matter the opposite parties would not be prejudiced by allowing this amendment.

24. Now coming to the decisions cited by the learned Advocate for the petitioners, reported in BCR 1985 (AD) 45 and 51 DLR 81 we are of the view that the above decisions are not relevant in the facts and circumstances of the present case inasmuch as by adding paragraph No. 14 in the plaint, the plaintiffs are not inserting any new cause of action or any new claim and it would also not change the nature and character of the suit rather it is an additional approach to the facts already on record.

25. Further, in the case of Jai Jai Ram Monohar Lai vs National Building Material Supply Gurgaon reported in AIR 1969 SC 1267 it has been held that "A party cannot be refused just relief merely because of some mistake, negligence, inadvertence or even infraction of the rules of procedure. The court always gives leave to amend the pleading of a party, unless it is satisfied that the party applying was acting malafide or that by his blunder he had caused injury to his opponent which may not be compensated for by an order of costs. However, negligent or careless may have been the first omission and however late the proposed amendment, the amendment may be allowed if it can be made without injustice to the other side."

<u>26. From the above discussions and after examining the decisions of our Apex Court as well as of the Indian Supreme Court, we can safely come to a conclusion that the proposed amendments do not show of any fact totally inconsistent with the original pleadings and furthermore it would not cause injustice to the opposite parties.</u>

27. In such view of the matter, we find no error committed by the court below in allowing the application of amendment by the impugned order dated 26-6-2005.

<u>28. Further it appears from the impugned order dated 26-6-2005 that an application for time submitted by defendant No. 12 to file written statement was rejected by the court below. Although defendant No. 12 did not prefer any revision against this rejection order for application of time to file written statement before the Hon'ble High Court Division, however in the interest of justice, the rejection of application for time to file written statement is hereby set aside and we are inclined to give liberty to the defendant No. 12 to submit the written statement within 30 days from the date of receipt of this judgment.</u>

29. Since it is a suit of the year 2000, the trial court is hereby directed to dispose of the suit as early as possible preferably within 6 (six) months from the date of receipt of this judgment.

30. In the result, the rule is disposed of with the above direction.

31. However, there will be no order as to costs.

32. The order of stay granted earlier by this court stands vacated.

Communicate the order to the court below at once.

End.

Mahbubey Alam, Senior Advocate, instructed by Sufia Khatun, Advocate-on-Record -----For the Appellant/ Petitioners (In all the cases).
