full_judgment:
Gobinda Chandra Tagore J: On an application under Article 102 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh, the Rule Nisi was issued calling upon respondents to show cause as to why the order dated 11-1-2015 passed by the respondent No. 5 under Memo No. 161- ১৬১-পাউবো/শৃং/শাঃ১/অভি(ক)-৪/২০১৪ dismissing the petitioner from his service and to recover proportionate amount of money from the petitioner (Annexure-M) and the order under Memo No. ৪২.০৩১.০২৭.০০.০০.০১২.২০১২.২০১২-৪১৪ dated 17-5-2015 issued under the signature of the respondent No. 2, Deputy Secretary, Ministry of Water Resources (Annexure-O) on behalf of the respondent No. 1 dismissing the appeal by affirming the order of dismissal should not be declared to have been issued without lawful authority and is of no legal effect and as to why the respondents should not be directed to reinstate the petitioner in the service with all attending salary and benefits and/or why such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper, shall not be passed.

2. Pending hearing of the Rule, the operation of the order dated 11-1-2015 passed by the respondent No.5 under Memo No. ১৬১-পাউবো/শৃং/শাঃ১/অভি(ক)-৪/২০১৪ so far as it relates  to recovery of proportionate amount of money from the petitioner (Annexure-M) was stayed initially for a period of 6 (six) months. Subsequently, the order of stay was extended from time to time.

3. The petitioner in his Writ Petition made the following averments:

The petitioner was an Executive Engineer, Office of the Chief Monitoring, Bangladesh Water Development Board, Dhaka until the impugned order was passed dismissing him along with order to recover money proportionately. The petitioner after completion of his degree of Bachelor of Science in Civil Engineering from Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology (BUET), Dhaka applied to the Bangladesh Water Development Board for employment and got appointment letter on 14-3-1989 and accordingly joined in the Design Circle-2, Bangladesh Water Development Board, Dhaka on 22-3-1989 as an Assistant Engineer and served in the said post for about 4 years. Thereafter the petitioner was promoted as Sub-Divisional Engineer and served with satisfaction of the concerned authority about 4 years in Derai O&M (Operation and Maintenance), Sub-Division, Sunamganj in Haor Projects; Sylhet O&M Sub-Division-I, about 2.4 years in different Projects and Haor Projects; about 2 years in Rajshahi Town Protection Project and other Projects; 1 years in Bhola Town Protection Project and other Projects; 1.6 years in Chandpur Town Protection Project and other Projects. Thereafter the petitioner was further promoted as an Executive Engineer on 6-2-2006 and served about 1.5 years in the field of planning as an Executive Engineer in Planning-I, Bangladesh Water Development Board, Dhaka and thereafter he served about 6 years and 7 months as an Executive Engineer in Chandpur O&M Division and successfully prevented the river erosion of the river Meghna by implementing different projects. Thus, the petitioner served in the post of Assistant Engineer for 4 years and as Sub-Divisional Engineer for about 12.10 years under different offices of Bangladesh Water Development Board, with utmost sincerity and honesty and also with full satisfaction of the authority. During the period at Chandpur O&M Division as an Executive Engineer, the petitioner success-fully maintained Chandpur Irrigation Project, an area of 57,000 hectare, situated in 6 Upazilas of Chandpur and Laxmipur Districts with minor maintenance cost and saved crops of about Taka 600.00 crores every year. He also implemented 10.60 km revetment works (River Bank Protection works) under Haimchar 1st and 2nd phase projects at the cost of about Taka 183.00 crores and till that date the said projects were working very well and prevents the river erosion in the said locality/area. He also effectively formulated and implemented 5.68 km. revetment works (River Bank Protection works) under Ibrahimpur-Sakhua Project at the cost of about Taka 170.00 crore which was also serving very well till that date and saved the river erosion at Ibrahimpur-Sakhua area. He successfully formulated and implemented Chandpur Town Protection Project (3rd phase) by which he maintained and strengthened Chandpur Town Protection Project of length 3.360 km. revetment works (River Bank Protection works) at Nutan and Puran Bazar of Chandpur Town at the cost of about Taka 25.00 crore and this work also serving very well and prevents the Chandpur Town Area from the river erosion at junction point of three mighty rivers- Padma, Meghna and Dakatia. The petitioner was transferred to the office of Chandpur O&M Division, Water Development Board, Chandpur from the Office of Planning-I, Water Development Board, Dhaka vide Memo No. ৩৫১-পাউবো(সচি)/প্রশাসন-৩/বিবিধ-৩৩৫/৯৭(অংশ-২)dated 7-8-2007 and accordingly he joined on 12-8-2007 and served with honesty and sincerity and also with full satisfaction of the authority. Then, the petitioner was transferred vide Memo No. পাউবো(সচি)/প্রশাসন-৩/বিবিধ-৩৩৫/৯৯(অংশ-৩)/১৯৫ dated 26-2-2014 issued under the signature of respondent No. 9 from the Office of Chandpur O&M Division, Bangladesh Water Development Board, Chandpur to the Office of the Chief Monitoring, Bangladesh Water Development Board, Dhaka and accordingly he joined there on 12-3-2014 and since then also served there with honesty and sincerity. The daily news paper namely "Dainik Jugantor" published a report on 24-3-2014 alleging irregularities in different projects at Chandpur, which were formulated and implemented under the control of the petitioner while he was serving as an Executive Engineer at Chandpur O&M (Operation and Maintenance) Division, Bangladesh Water Development Board, Chandpur which led temporary suspension of the petitioner with effect from 25-3-2014 on the basis of vague allegations vide Memo No. পাউবো(সচি)/প্রশাসন-৩/২ পি-২৬৮/২০০৬/২৭৮ dated 25-3-2014 issued under the signature of respondent No. 9, Deputy Secretary (Administration) with recommendation of respondent No. 3, Director General, Bangladesh Water Development Board, Dhaka. The respondent No. 5, Director, Discipline, Bangladesh Water Development Board, Dhaka framed 21 (twenty one) charges against the petitioner on the allegations of various irregularities in respect of Non-Development Revenue Works and Sachar Khal which were implemented under the control of the petitioner. He was asked for reply to the charges within 10 (ten) days from the date of receipt of the charges, Annexure-F. The petitioner replied vide letter of reply dated 9-7-2014, Annexure-G against the charges to the respondent No. 5, Director, Discipline, Bangladesh Water Development Board, Dhaka stating clearly, amongst other, that he did not commit any irregularity in performing his duties. But the authority did not consider the written reply of the petitioner, rather, formed an inquiry committee consisting of 1 (one) member namely, Md Abdur Rahman Akanda, Director, Planning-I, Bangladesh Water Development Board, Dhaka, respondent No. 7 vide Memo No. ৭৮-পাউবো/শৃং/শাঃ১/অভি(ক)-০৪/২০১৪ dated 4-8-2014, Annexure- H for holding an inquiry into the alleged charges against the petitioner. The inquiry officer issued Notice vide Memo No. বাপাউবো/পরি-১/৫৬৮(১০) dated 10-8-2014 Annexure-I on the petitioner for his personal appearance and hearing of the alleged charges brought against him. After completion of the inquiry, the inquiry officer, respondent No.7 submitted a report on 15-11-2014 finding prima facie allegations against the petitioner with recommendation to award punishments to the petitioner, while, regulation 54(8) of the বাংলাদেশ পানি উন্নয়ন বোর্ড চাকুরী প্রবিধানমালা (hereinafter referred to as the Service Regulations) categorically prohibits that the Inquiry Officer shall not recommend any punishment except giving his findings whether one is guilty or not guilty. The authority issued a 2nd Show Cause Notice vide Memo No. ১৩৮-পাউবো/শৃং/শাঃ১/অভি(ক)-৪/২০১৪ dated 15-12-2014, Annexure-K to the petitioner, enclosing therewith an incomplete inquiry report directing him to show cause as to why the petitioner should not be dismissed from service under Clause 49(1)(L)(D) of the said Service Regulations. The petitioner submitted a written reply dated 28-12-2014, Annexure-L to the 2nd Show Cause stating in detail that the allegations brought against him are not true and he did not commit any offence and the inquiry officer without following the provisions of the said Service Regulations submitted his inquiry report malafide and intentionally against him. In fact, the petitioner was not connected in any way with the said occurrence and, as such, he is entitled to be released from the charges leveled against him. The authority without considering the reply of the petitioner, dismissed him from the service and also imposed punishment against him to recover money proportionately vide the impugned Memo No. ১৬১-পাউবো/শৃং/শাঃ১/অভি(ক)-৪/২০১৪ dated 11-1-2015, Annexure-M. Thereafter, the petitioner filed an appeal before the respondent No. 1, Secretary, Ministry of Water Resources on 30-3-2015, Annexure-N stating in detail as to his innocence against the alleged charges, violations of the said Service Regulations by the inquiry officer and praying for his release from the punishment. The respondent No. 2, Deputy Secretary, Ministry of Water Resources without considering the appeal of the petitioner rejected the appeal vide Memo No.  ৪২.০৩১.০২৭.০০.০০.০১২.২০১২-৪১৪ dated 17-5-2015, Annexure-O which he cannot do, as the said appeal and the decision of appeal ought to have been given by the respondent No. 1 and not by the respondent No. 2 and thus, the affirmation of punishment by the respondent No.2 by rejecting the appeal is ex facie illegal and the rejection order is not a proper disposal of the appeal in the eye of law. In June 2013, a mid-term post work was taken up by the field officers under the petitioner and on the basis of that measurement 79.84% bill was paid to the Contractors in August 2013. After 9 months including a flood season, Task-Force of BWDB took measurement on 30-3-2014 to 3-4-2014 in the absence of the petitioner. In reply to the charges, the petitioner denied all the charges and measurements taken by the Task-Force. The petitioner requested the authority to take a fresh measurement in his reply to the 1st Show Cause Notice and also to the inquiry officer. He also said in his reply to the 2nd Show Cause Notice that the calculation of earth of Sachar Khal by task force was not realistic. The actual progress of Sachar Khal would be 94.87%. The 9th meeting of the Steering Committee of Projects Implemented by the Bangladesh Water Development Board under the finance of the Climate Change Trust Fund was held on 15-6-2015 at the Ministry of Water Resources and in that meeting, the respondent No. 6, Chief Engineer, Eastern Zone, Comilla, who was the complainant against the petitioner informed the meeting that the progress of the respective project Sachar Khal was 81% and due to rainy season the scheduled work could not be completed in due time i.e. within the period of January 2013 to June 2014 and the schedule period of the work was required to be extended till June, 2015 and the minutes of the said meeting dated 15-6-2014 was issued on 23-6-2014 under the signatures of the respondent Nos.1 and 2, Annexure-P. The Ministry of Food and Disaster Management issued a letter vide Memo No. ধাদ্যব্যম/প্রাক-১/৫(১)/২০০৫-২০০৬/০০ dated 22-8-2005, Annexure-Q directing the concerned authority to measure the excavation of earth upon deducting the depression/damage of the earth at the rate of completion of the projects of 15% within 2(two) months of the next year and upon the deducting further 10% for every next year, even, the excavation of earth in the জলাভূমি or হাওর এলাকা shall be calculated upon deduction of further 5%. Moreover, the respondent No. 7, the inquiry officer unlawfully co-opted 3 (three) task-force members for checking Sachar Khal measurements. These 3 (three) complainants, who were illegally co-opted checked Randomly Selected Post-Works of Sachar Khal which were taken by them by the order of the inquiry officer, but the inquiry officer did not enclose any earth calculation sheet with the inquiry report. In such facts and circumstances, the petitioner having no other equally efficacious remedy filed the instant Writ Petition and obtained the Rule and the order of stay.

4. Respondent No. 3 namely, Director General, Bangladesh Water Development Board contested the Rule by filing an Affidavit-in-Opposition denying the material allegations made in the Writ Petition and contending, inter alia, that the Writ Petition is not maintainable as no illegality was committed by the respondents inasmuch as the Writ Petition so far it relates to the allegation brought by the petitioner involved serious disputed question of facts, which cannot be resolved under this summary jurisdiction. Moreover, the Writ Petition is not maintainable in view of the law enunciated in the case of Government of Bangladesh vs Sontosh Kumar Saha, reported in 21 BLC (AD) 94, Bangladesh Water Development Board being a public statutory body, the petitioner ought to have sought remedy before the Administrative Tribunal. The Chandpur Irrigation Project Area (Haimchar) Protection Project 2009-2010 and 2010-2011 was under construction to prevent the Meghna river erosion. Another project Ibrahimpur-Sakhua Project was also under construction for the fiscal years 2009-2010, 2010-2011, 2011-2012 and 2012-2013. An inquiry was initiated against the petitioner by the BWDB vide Memo No. 100 dated 13-10-2014 to inquire into the irregularities committed by the petitioner according to Clause 52 of the Service Regulations, 2013. Accordingly, a complaint was filed as per the Clause 48(L)(M) (0)(P) and (Q) of the said Service Regulations. Subsequently, an Inquiry Officer was appointed vide Memo No. 134 dated 7-12-2014. The claim of the petitioner that he successfully completed the projects during his tenure is not true. During 2013-2014 the petitioner paid 100% bills by showing completion of 100% works in 11 flood prevention/re-construction/re-pair projects and ring dying repair and re-construction works without, completing the projects. Moreover, Chandpur O&M Division has dismissed him from his duties vide Memo No. 161 dated 11-1-2015 as he paid an extra Taka 513.88 lac to the concerned Contractor for Sachar Khal (Boyaljuri Khal) Re-excavating Project in Kachua Upazila, Chandpur showing progress of 100% work in 10 package specifications without completing the works. The petitioner was suspended as per Clause 55(1) of the said Service Regulations following which an Inquiry Officer was appointed and an inquiry was held. Therefore, the claim that his temporary suspension is based on newspaper report containing vague allegation is hot true. Upon inquiry the Chief Engineer, North and East Division, BWDB, Comilla submitted a report dated 21-4-2014 with the finding that the petitioner was responsible for the irregularities along with other concerned officers. According to the office order No. 159 dated 20-4-2014, the Additional Director General (East Region) visited the site and also submitted an inquiry report with the similar findings. Following the said report, 7 officers with the rank of Sub-Divisional Engineer and Branch Officers were temporary suspended vide Memo No.40 dated 7-5-2014. The Inquiry Officer submitted the inquiry report with the comment and findings on the prima facie allegations against the petitioner with the recommendation for awarding punishment to the petitioner as per Clause 54(8) of the said Service Regulations. The inquiry report was submitted with attachments consisting 50 pages. According to the posts work measurement conducted by the task force committee of BWDB between 30-3-2014 to 3-4-2014, a total amount of re-excavated earth was 564079.80 Cubic Meter which was 60.86% of the total estimated 9,26,843.48 Cubic Meter. According to the plan Circle-2, BWDB the vetted value of the re-excavated earth was Taka 679.21 lakh (taka 120.41/Cubic Meter) and the Contractors were paid a total of Taka 11,93,09 lakh. Thus, an extra Taka 51388 lakh was paid to the Contractors and, as such, having drawn the departmental proceeding properly, the petitioner was dismissed from his service and therefore, there being no legal infirmity in the order of dismissal, the Rule is liable to be discharged.

5. Having placed the Writ Petition, Mr Shafique Ahmed along with Mr Mahbub Shafique, Mr Leo Saha Kenedey and Mr Md Enayeat Ullah Nadim, learned Advocate for the petitioner submits that the departmental proceeding suffers from the non-application of the relevant provision of the said Service Regulations, which has seriously prejudiced the petitioner in defending himself resulting the illegal dismissal of the petitioner from his service and, as such, the impugned order of dismissal, including the entire proceeding being issued or drawn by violation of the relevant provision of law as well as without jurisdiction, the same is liable to be declared to have been made or drawn without lawful authority and is of no legal effect.

6. The learned Advocate for the petitioner elaborately makes the following submission:

(a) The petitioner was suspended by the order dated 25-3-2014 but he was not communicated the charges on which he was suspended even within 52 (fifty two) working days while, Regulations 55(2) of the said Service Regulations provides that such suspension shall be deemed to be cancelled unless the charges are communicated to the delinquent within 30 (thirty) working days from which it appears that even up to issuance of the order of suspension, there was no allegation against the petitioner and the suspension order was deemed to be cancelled.

(b) Regulations 52(4) of the said Service Regulations provides for initiation of the inquiry within 10 (ten) days from the date of appointment of the Inquiry Officer, who shall have to submit an inquiry report within the time fixed by the authority, but the Inquiry Officer did not submit his report within 100(one hundred) working days while, the authority directed the Inquiry Officer to submit the report only within 30(thirty) working days and, as such, the 'Inquiry Officer acted in violation of the provision of Regulations 52(4) of the said Service Regulations inasmuch as the Inquiry Officer did not allow the petitioner to examine the complainant and to go through the relevant documents relating to the alleged charges with an ulterior motive by which the petitioner also was also deprived of his legal right as ensured by Regulations 54(2)(ka) of the said Service Regulations and thereby, the petitioner was seriously prejudiced in defending himself.

(c) The petitioner was also not allowed to cross examine the witnesses of the authorities in violation of the provision of Regulation 54(2)(ka) of the said Service Regulations inasmuch as he was also deprived of his right ensured by and under the Principle of Natural Justice.

(d) Regulation 54(8) of the said Service Regulations empowers only the Enquiry Officer to make any finding as to the guilty or not guilty but he has" no juris-diction to make any comment or propose any punishment which may influence the concerned authority to award punishment, but in the present case, the Inquiry Officer specifically made proposal for awarding punishment against the petitioner and thereby, the impugned order of dismissal is also defective due to the violation of the said Regulations 54(8).

(e) At the time of issuance of the 2nd Show Cause Notice, the respondents did not serve the petitioner the entire inquiry report but only the summary thereof without attaching thereto any relevant documents which has further prejudiced the petitioner in defending himself as well as to make a proper, elaborate and effective defence.

(f) By the 2nd Show Cause Notice, only one punishment i.e. dismissal from his service was proposed but by the impugned order the another punishment as to realization of the proportionate money disbursed to the Contractors allegedly in excess and thereby the respondents further violated the provision under Regulations 52(6) of the said Service Regulations.

(g) The appellate authority dismissed the appeal without assigning any reason but by a non-speaking order, which is also contradictory to the provision of Regulations 58(3) of the said Service Regulations.

(h) The appeal was disposed of by way of dismissal by a Deputy Secretary of the Ministry of Water Resources, who was holding the post and rank equivalent to those of the petitioner and thus, the appeal was disposed of without any jurisdiction.

(i) The complainant on 23-6-2014 informed the 9th meeting of the Steering Committee of the project implemented by the BWDB that there was a progress of Sachar Khal project was up to 81% and realized an amount of Taka 1197.39 lakhs equivalent to 79.84% i.e. the expenditure was lower than the implemented work and thus, the allegations brought against the petitioner are contrary to the report submitted by the complainant himself and, as such, the entire proceeding is malafide and to have been drawn with an ulterior motive, to have been done without jurisdiction only to harass and humiliate the petitioner.

7. In support of his contention, the learned Advocate for the petitioner relied upon the decision in the case of (1) Tapashi Bhattacharjee vs Bangladesh, reported in 9 BLC 613, (2) Ayub Ali Chowdhwy vs Government of Bangladesh, reported in 57 DLR 578, (3) Md Shafiqul Islam vs Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education, Comilla, reported in 15 MLR 345, (4) Nurun Nabir Sarker (Md) vs Secretary, Ministry of Education, reported in 68 DLR 125, (5) Md Golam Mostafa Miah vs Bangladesh, represented by the Secretary, Ministry of Establishment, reported in 7 BLT 127 = 51 DLR 248, (6) Pradeep Kumar Biswas vs Indian Institute of Chemical Biology, reported in (202) 5 SCC 111, (7) Ajay Hasia vs Khalid Mujib Sehravardi, reported in (1981) 1 SCC 722, (8) Ratan Chandra Dey vs Jinnator Nahar, reported in 13 MLR (AD) 168 = 61 DLR (AD) 116, (9) Md Jashimuddin (Kanchan) vs Md Ali Ashraf, reported in 11 BLD (AD) 101 = 42 DLR (AD) 289 and (10) Bangladesh Agricultural Development Corporation vs Mr Saidul Huq Bhuiyan, reported in 11 BLT (AD) 164 = 8 BLC (AD) 49.

8. On the other hand, Mr Sk. Shaifuzzaman, learned Advocate appearing for the respondent No. 3 submits that Bangladesh Water Development Board being a public statutory body as per the law enunciated by the Appellate Division in the case of Government of Bangladesh vs Sontosh Kumar Saha, reported in 21 BLC (AD) 94, the Writ Petition is not maintainable as the petitioner ought to have sought for remedy before the Administrative Tribunal.

9. The learned Advocate for the respondent No. 3 further submits that since the Writ Petition is not maintainable, there is no legal scope for considering the case on merit. At this stage, the learned Advocate was also invited to make other submission but he repeatedly stresses on his earlier submission that the Writ Petition is not maintainable and there is no scope for entering into the merit of the case.

10. In support of his contention, the learned Advocate for the respondent No. 3 relied upon the decision in the case of (1) Delwar Hossain Mia (Md) vs Bangladesh, represented by the Secretary, Ministry of Home Affairs, reported in 52 DLR (AD) 120, (2) Bangladesh, represented by the Secretary, Ministry of Home Affairs vs Sontosh Kumar Saha and 24 others, reported in 21 BLC (AD) 94 and (3) Junnur Rahman vs Bangladesh Shilpa Rin Sangstha (BSRS), reported in 51 DLR (AD) 166.

11. We have perused the Writ Petition along with the Supplementary Affidavit filed by the petitioner and the Affidavit-in-Opposition along with the Supplementary Affidavit-in-Opposition filed by the respondent No.3 and heard the learned Advocates from both the sides.

12. The petitioner is an Executive Engineer of Bangladesh Water Development Board (BWDB). Vide the Memo dated 7-8-2007 the petitioner was transferred to the office of Chand-pur Operation and Maintenance Division, BWDB and he joined the post on 12-8-2007 and functioned there up to 4-3-2014. During this time, amongst other, the petitioner maintained Chand-pur Irrigation Project consisting an area of 57000 hectors situated in 6 Upazilas of Chandpur and Laxmipur Districts and also implemented 10.60 km Revetment Works (river bank protection work) under Haimchar, 1st and 2nd Phase Project; 5.68 km Revetment Works under Ibrahimpur-Sakhua Project; Chandpur Town Protection Project (3rd phase) consisting the land of 3.360 km at Natun and Puran Bazar of Chandpur Town in the 2013-2014 fiscal years. On 24-3-2014, a news was published in the "Dainik Jugantor" alleging some irregularities on different projects at Chandpur, which was formulated and implemented under the control of the petitioner. On the basis of the news report, the petitioner was put under suspension vide Memo dated 25-3-2014. Regulations 55(2) of the বাংলাদেশ পানি উন্নয়ন বোর্ড চাকুরী প্রবিধানমালা (hereinafter referred to as the said Service Regulations) provides that if any order of suspension is imposed of any employee, the order of suspension shall be deemed to be cancelled after expiry of 30 working days unless by this time, the delinquent employee is communicated with the charges. Admittedly, no charges were communicated to the petitioner even within 52 working days. However, on the 53rd working days on 12-6.2014, the petitioner was served with Memo dated 12-6-2013 containing some charges of various irregularities in respect of non-development of revenue work including Sachar Khal. The allegations covered only 2013-2014 fiscal years i.e. up to 30-6-2014, but the petitioner was functioning as the Executive Engineer up to 4-3-2014. The petitioner replied to the charges vide a letter dated 9-7-2014 stating, amongst other, that he did not commit any irregularity in performing his functions. His reply being not satisfactory to the authority vide Memo dated 4-8-2014, a 01 Member Inquiry Committee was formed with Md Abdur Rahman Akanda for holding inquiry into the charges. The Inquiry Officer vide Memo dated 10-8-2014, directed the petitioner and others to remain present in the office of the Inquiry Officer on 11-9-2014 at 10-30 am and with a direction to remain present when the Inquiry Officer would inspect the sites on 14-9-2014 and 15-9-2014. The Inquiry Officer after completion of the inquiry submitted a report on 15-11-2014. It is a summary report consisting of 50 pages and there were some annexures as were mentioned therein. It appears from the inquiry report that it is based on mainly the report submitted by the Task Force Committee with regard to the implementation of the work. There is only one irregularity as to that two level books in two package were not available and there is no other statement as to the irregularities, but in his opinion, the Inquiry Officer only made the following findings:

“চাঁদপুর সেচ প্রকল্পটির ক্ষেত্রে পরিচালনা ও রক্ষণাবেক্ষণ খাতে প্রাপ্ত বরাদ্দ যথাযথভাবে ব্যয় করা হইয়াছে বলিয়া প্রতীয়মান হয় না। তাহা ছাড়া কাজের প্রাক্কলিত পরিমাণ ও বাস্তবায়িত পরিমাণের মধ্যে বিস্তর পার্থক্য বিদ্যমান বলিয়া সাইট পরিদর্শনের সময় তদন্ত কর্মকর্তার নিকট প্রতীয়মান হইয়াছে।”

13. Therefore, from the said findings, it appears that there was no elaborate statement of the works and the irregularities, if any there. Accordingly, it may be said that it is nothing but a summary and non-speaking report (with regard to the summary package). Having concluded the inquiry, the Inquiry Officer made a proposal for taking administrative measures against the officers and employees involved in the irregularities and with regard to the Sachar Khal Project, the similar proposal were made. The Inquiry Officer also found that Taka 513.88 lakhs were disbursed in excess to the works implemented and accordingly, he also proposed for realization of money proportionately from the officers and employees responsible for such disbursement. Therefore, we find substance in the submission made by the learned Advocate for the petitioner that the Inquiry Officer in his inquiry report instead of making any finding as to whether the delinquent officers and employees are guilty or not, he made proposal for taking punitive measures while, under Regulations 54.8, there is a specific bar as to making any such recommendation for any punishment. However, it does not appear from the report that the delinquent officers and employees misappropriated any money or they enjoyed any unlawful gain but there is only the allegation that they have disbursed the bill in excess to the work implemented. Therefore, such proposal for punishment might have influenced the concerned executive authority in proceeding with departmental proceeding and warding punishment against the petitioner.

14. It is the further contention of the petitioner that only an incomplete inquiry report was given to him with the 2nd Show Cause Notice. It has already been found that the inquiry report is summery and non-speaking one, which does not contain any elaborate discussion, but there were some annexures attached with the inquiry report. The contention of the petitioner that those annexures were not supplied to him. However, in the Affidavit-in-Opposition, this contention of the petitioner has not been materially denied. The contesting respondents even in his Affidavit-in-Opposition or Supplementary Affidavit-in-Opposition did not annex those annexures; and, when the respondent No.3 was asked for producing those documents, his learned Advocate replied that no such documents can be submitted before this Court without any order. Since the respondent No.3 himself is present and those documents are supposed to be lying with him, we do not find any reason to pass any order to submit those documents. Moreover, in this regard, the learned Advocate further submits that only the inquiry report is to be supplied with those documents with the 2nd Show Cause Notice. But it appears from the report that those annexures are part of the inquiry report.

15. Regulations 52(5) of the said Service Regulations specifically provides that upon receiving the inquiry report, the authority shall take decision thereon and shall inform the decision along with the inquiry report and shall inform the delinquent officer of the inquiry report along with the 2nd Show Cause Notice. Therefore, the inquiry report as has been supplied to the petitioner was not a complete one. It has already been found that the inquiry report was a summary and non-speaking one. Therefore, the partial inquiry report was not sufficient for the petitioner to defend himself effectively. There is no doubt, in such facts and circumstances that the petitioner was prejudiced in defending himself and, as such, prejudicial activities were also made by violation of Regulations 52(5) of the said Service Regulations.

16. It has also been alleged by the petitioner that he was not given any chance to cross-examine the complainant and other witnesses deposed on behalf of the authorities which is mandatorily required under Regulations 52(2)(ka) & (kha) of the said Service Regulations. This material allegations have not been materially denied by the contesting respondent No.3. Therefore, he was further deprived of proper defence and thereby, the petitioner was further prejudiced in defending himself before the Inquiry Officer.

17. It appears that in the 2nd Show Cause Notice, only one punishment namely dismissal from service was proposed but it appears from the order of dismissal that an additional punishment was imposed on him for realization of money proportionately from the petitioner. But Regulations 52(c) stipulates that in the 2nd Show Cause Notice, there must be a proposal for the punishment to be imposed on the delinquent. Therefore, the order of dismissal also suffers from violation of Regulations 52(c) of the said Service Regulations.

18. It appears from the discussions made above that the entire proceeding was drawn and concluded in violation of Regulations 52(2); Regulations 52(4); Regulations 54(2)(ka), (kha); Regulations 54(8) and Regulations 52(6) of the said Service Regulations.

19. Against the order of dismissal the petitioner filed an appeal to the concerned authority within time. It is the contention of the petitioner that the appeal was disposed of by a Deputy Secretary. The petitioner being an Executive Engineer is equivalent to Deputy Secretary. But it is the settled principle of law that no Inquiry Officer or Appellate Authority can be an Officer holding a post lower to the post of the delinquent or even any post equivalent to the delinquent. This contention of the petitioner was denied by the respondent No.3 contending that the Deputy Secretary only communicated the order of dismissal as he was ordered. But even on asking for, the respondent No.3 could not show any document that the appeal was disposed of by any other superior officer. Therefore, such evasive denial is not a denial at all in the eye of law. Accordingly, we find substance in the submission of the learned Advocate for the petitioner made in this regard. Thus, it transpires that the appeal was disposed of without jurisdiction.

20. Moreover, Regulations 58(3) of the said Service Regulations provides that in deciding the appeal, the appellate authority must examine whether the procedure as required under the Regulations have been observed or not. But from the appellate order, Annexure-O, it appears that there was no such finding in the appellate order. Accordingly, the appeal was not disposed of in accordance with Regulations 58(3) of the said Service Regulations. The discussion as have been made above relates to the merit of the matter.

21. At the very outset of hearing of the Writ Petition, Mr Murad Reza along with Mr Sk. Shaifuzzaman, learned Advocate for the respondent No. 3 having referred to the case of Government of Bangladesh vs Sontosh Kumar Saha, reported in 21 BLC (AD) 94 submits that Bangladesh Water Development Board being a public statutory body, the petitioner was to go to the Administrative Tribunal for relief, if any. In this regard, the learned Advocate for the respondent No. 3 referred to the relevant portion of paragraph No. 148 which is quoted below:

"We have held earlier that a public servant or an employee of the Statutory Corporation can maintain a writ petition if he challenges the vires of a statute or if his fundamental rights are violated and not otherwise."

22. Referring the above quoted observation made in the said judgment, the learned. Advocate for the respondent No. 3 submits that the Writ Petition is not maintainable under writ juris-diction. In this regard, Mr Shafique Ahmed, learned Advocate having referred to section 2(aa) of the Administrative Tribunal Act, 1980 submits that in the judgment referred to by the learned Advocate for the respondent No. 3, the statutory corporation corresponds and contemplates the `statutory public authority' as has been defined in section 2(aa) of the said Act, while, in the said judgment, the schedule to the said Act has not been discussed or has not been extended by any means. We have gone through the relevant portion of the judgment referred to. It appears from the said judgment that only 8 (eight) determining points were selected and decided by the said judgment. The question of public statutory body or the extension of the schedule to the Public Administration Act, 1980 was not within the said 8(eight) determining points. Therefore, the schedule to the Public Administration Act, 1980 was not discussed and decided in the said case, but the statutory corporation has been referred to there. Section 2(aa) of the Administrative Tribunal Act reads as follows:

"2. In this Act, unless there is anything repugnant in the subject or context,—

(aa) 'statutory public authority' means an authority, corporation, or body specified in the Schedule to this Act"

23. Therefore, since the schedule to the Act was not discussed in the judgment, we find substance in the submission of the learned Advocate for the petitioner that the statutory corporation as has been referred to in the judgment corresponds the statutory corporation or statutory public authority as has been defined under section 2(aa) of the Administrative Tribunal Act. But the learned advocate for the respondent No. 3 even after being invited to make his submission elaborate on the merit in the Writ Petition confined himself within the point of maintainability of the Writ Petition and nothing else.

<u>24. Upon such discussion, we find that Bangladesh Water Development Board being not included in the schedule to the Administrative Tribunal Act, 1980 as a public statutory authority, the officers and employees of the Board have no remedy under the Administrative Tribunal Act. Therefore, the petitioner has no other equally efficacious remedy other than the remedies as have been sought for in the writ petition and accordingly, the writ petition is very much maintainable.</u>

25. It has already been found that the learned Advocate for the respondent No.3 has not pressed any other facts or issue which were stated or raised in their Affidavit-in-Opposition. Though we invited him to take multiple defence; even then he restricted himself within the point of maintainability only. Thus, it appears that the questions relating to the merit of the matter as have been discussed above remain to be uncontroverted. Accordingly, we find substance in the Rule.

26. Hence, the Rule is made absolute.

27. Accordingly, the order dated 11-1-2015 passed by the respondent No. 5 under Memo No. ১৬১-পাউবো/শৃং/শাঃ১/অভি(ক)-৪/২০১৪ dismissing the petitioner from his service and to  recover proportionate amount of money from the petitioner (Annexure-M) and the order under Memo No. ৪২.০৩১.০২৭.০০.০০.০১২.২০১২-৪১৪ dated 17-5-2015 issued under the signature of the respondent No. 2, Deputy Secretary, Ministry of Water Resources (Annexure-O) on behalf of the respondent No. 1 dismissing the appeal by affirming the order of dismissal is hereby declared to have been issued without lawful authority and are of no legal effect.

28. Therefore, the petitioner is deemed to be have all through been in service and he is entitled to his arrears of salaries.

29. The respondents are hereby directed to allow petitioner to function within 30 (thirty) days from the receipt of a copy of this judgment.

However, there would be no order as to costs.

End.

full_judgment:
Md Shohrowardi J: This Rule Nisi was issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why they should not be directed to take appropriate measures for settling a dispute between the petitioner and the Managing Committee in terms of the findings of the Enquiry Report contained in memo no. Umashiau/Ambar/ 13/Tandanta/22dated 18-2-2013 submitted by the respondent No. 3 to respondent No. 2 (Annexure-L) wherein dismissal of the petitioner was found unlawful and/or such other or further order or orders be passed as to this court may deem fit and proper.

2. Short facts for disposal of the Rule are that the petitioner was appointed on 30-12-2010 in the vacant post of Headmaster of Mofiz Uddin Girls Pilot High School, Amtali, Barguna by the Managing Committee of the school and he joined in his service as Headmaster on 1-1-2011. After appointment of the petitioner, the term of the Managing Committee had expired and he filed an application on 30-7-2012 to the respondent No. 1, Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education, Barisal, for approval of the Ad-hoc Committee of the school and the respondent No. 1 by office order dated 29-8-2012 contained in memo No. বশিবো/বিঅ/৪০/২০১২/২২৬৯ approved the Ad-hoc Committee of the said school for a period of 6 (six) months from the date of issuance of the order. Thereafter, the President of the Ad-hoc Managing Committee of the school on 18-9-2012 issued show cause notice upon the petitioner to show cause within 7 (seven) days as to why he should not be suspended from the school for misappropriation of the fund of the school and other allegations. After that, on 24-9-2012 the petitioner had given reply to the show cause notice dated 18-9-2012 denying all the allegations made in the show cause notice and on 30-9-2012 the petitioner also lodged a General Diary being No. 1029 with Amtali Police Station, Barguna against the President of the Ad-hoc Managing Committee and teachers of the school and subsequently he also filed an application on 22-11-2012 to the respondent No. 1 regarding false allegations brought against him by the President of the Ad-hoc Committee of the school. Thereafter the President of the Ad-hoc Managing Committee of the school on 26-11-2012 dismissed the petitioner from service. After that, he filed an application on 5-12-2012 to the respondent No. 1 praying for taking step against the illegal action of the respondent No. 4 and the respondent No. 1 by office order dated 6-1-2013(Annexure K) instructed the Upazila Secondary Education Officer, Amtali, Barguna to inquire into the allegations brought against the petitioner by the President of the Ad-hoc Managing Committee of the school and by office order dated 6-1-2013 contained in Memo No. বশিবো/বিঅ/বরগুনা-৪০/২০১৩/৩৩৬০ (Annexure K1) directed the President of the Ad-hoc Managing Committee to sent all relevant documents regarding dismissal of the petitioner to the respondent No. 1. Thereafter, Md Golam Mostafa, Upazila Secondary Education Officer, Amtali, Barguna issued notice to both the parties to appear on 18-2-2013 at 10-00 am in the office of the Headmaster of Mofiz Uddin Girls Pilot High School, Amtali, Barguna for the purpose of holding inquiry and after hearing both parties and completing inquiry submitted his report on 18-2-213 (Annexure L) to the respondent No. 2, Inspector of the School, Secondary and Higher Secondary Education Board, Barisal finding no truth of the allegations brought against the petitioner by the Ad-hoc Managing Committee of the school.

3. The petitioner further stated that after issuance of the Rule, stay and direction dated 15-5-2013 passed by this Court, he joined in his service on 19-5-2013 and the Upazila Secondary Education Office, Amtali, Borguna by letter dated 20-5-2013 (Annexure- S) also informed Md Delwar Hossain, Headmaster (in-charge) that the petitioner joined in his service on 19-5-2013 and instructed him to take necessary steps in accordance with law. After expiry of the term of the Ad-hoc Managing Committee of the school, the petitioner as Headmaster filed an application on 29-5-2013(Annexure) to the respondent No. 2 for giving permission to form an Ad-hoc Managing Committee and accordingly the respondent No. 1 by office order dated 4-6- 2013(Annexure T-1) allowed him to form an Ad-hoc Managing Committee of the school and after forming the Ad-hoc Managing Committee, the petitioner filed an application on 6-6-2013 (Annexure U) to the respondent No. 2 for approval of the said Committee and accordingly the respondent No. 2 approved the Ad-hoc Managing Committee on 16-6-2013 (Annexure-V) including the name of the petitioner as Member Secretary (ex-officio Headmaster) for a period of 4 (four) months. In the meantime on 11-6-2013 Mesbah Uddin, former President of the Ad-hoc Managing Committee filed Civil Petition For Leave to Appeal No. 1325 of 2013 before the Hon'ble Appellate Division and the Hon'ble Appellate Division by order dated 11-6-2013 was pleased to stay the operation of the order dated 15-5-2013 passed by this Court and was further pleased to pass an order directing the parties to maintain statuesque in respect of the office of the Headmaster of the school in question.

4. Thereafter, the Ad-hoc Managing Committee in its meeting held on 18-6-2013 (Annexure W) decided that as per order of the statues quo passed by the Hon'ble Appellate Division in Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 1325 of 2013, the petitioner will continue in his service as Headmaster of the school and subsequently the said Ad-hoc Managing Committee in its meeting held on 25-9-2013 (Annexure Z-2) unanimously confirmed the service of the petitioner as Headmaster of the school with effect from 1-1-2013. In the meantime, on 26-6-2013 the petitioner as Headmaster along with other teachers of the school obtained MPO. After expiry of the term of the Ad-hoc Managing Committee, the election of the Managing Committee was duly held and the newly elected Managing Committee of the school in its' meeting held on 9-11-2013 (Annexure Z-4) unanimously had withdrawn the order of dismissal dated 26-11-2012 holding that the Ad-hoc Managing Committee has no authority to dismiss the Headmaster as per Rules and further decided not to contest in the instant Rule against the petitioner.

5. In the meantime, the Hon'ble Appellate Division after hearing Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 1325 of 2013 by order dated 25-11-2013 disposed of the leave petition and was further pleased to extend the order of statuesque till disposal of the instant Rule. Thereafter, the term of the elected Managing Committee has expired and before expiry of the term of the Managing Committee, the petitioner as Headmaster conducted the election of the Managing Committee and one Ms. Zakia Alice, sister of Mesbah Uddin Ahmed, former President of the Ad-hoc Committee who dismissed the petitioner from service, was elected President of the Managing Committee and the respondent No. 1 on 16-2-2017 again approved the newly elected Managing Committee of the school including the name of the petitioner as Member Secretary (ex-officio Headmaster) and the newly elected Managing Committee headed by Ms Zakia Alice also allowed the petitioner to continue as Headmaster of the School. Thereafter, all of a sudden, the Managing Committee of the school by order dated 27-5-2017 contained in memo No. এমইউব/আম/বর/দায়িত্ব/২০১৭/৯০ (Annexure-Q) instructed Md Delwar Hossain, Senior Assistant Teacher to take over the charge of the Headmaster holding that since the order of stay granted by the Hon'ble High Court Division has been declared void by the Hon'ble Appellate Division and the order of statuesque passed by the Appellate Division is in force, the petitioner is not legally entitled to perform the duty as Headmaster of the school and sent the Monthly Payment Order of the teachers and employees of the school excluding the name of the petitioner (Annexure-P). Thereafter on 2-8-2017 the petitioner obtained the Supplementary Rule Nisi in the following term;

Let a supplementary Rule Nisi issue calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the striking out petitioner's name from salary sheet from the month of April, 2017 (Annexure-P) and letter dated 27-5-2017 (Annexure-Q) issued by the respondent No. 4 to the respondent No. 5 despite pendency of the rule in Writ Petition No. 4554 of 2013 before the High Court Division and in violation of the order of Appellate Division dated 11-6-2013 and 25-11-2013 passed in Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 1325 of 2013 shall not be declared to have been issued without lawful authority and is of no legal effect and /or such other or further order or orders be passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper.

6. The respondent No. 4 contested the Rule by filing affidavit-in-opposition stating that before dismissing the petitioner from service, a three members inquiry committee headed by Sukumar Chandra Hawlader, guardian member of the Ad-hoc Managing Committee, after examining the records and the witnesses found truth of the allegations brought against him and submitted its report on 20-10-2012 and on the basis of the said inquiry report, the Ad-hoc Managing Committee by order dated 26-11-2012 dismissed the petitioner from service and against the order of dismissal , he filed Title Suit No. 323 of 2012 in the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Amtali, Barguna who by order dated 15-1-2013 dismissed the suit against which the petitioner filed Title Appeal No. 6 of 2013 before the District Judge, Barguna and after filing the appeal, again he filed the instance Writ Petition before this Hon'ble Court and subsequently had withdrawn the Title Appeal No. 6 of 2013. The respondent No. 4 also stated that after passing the order of stay and direction dated 15-5-2013, the respondent No. 4 filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 1325 of 2013 before the Hon'ble Appellate Division and the Hon'ble Appellate Division by order dated 11-6-2013 was pleased to stay the order of stay and direction dated 15-5-2013 passed by the High Court Division and also directed the parties to maintain statuesque in respect of the office of the Headmaster of the school and at the time of filing the Writ Petition, the petitioner was not in service and in view of the order of statuesque passed by the Hon'ble Appellate Division, Mr Md Delwar Hossain, Senior Teacher of the school had already taken over the charge of the Headmaster of the school and after passing the order of statuesque by the Hon'ble Appellate Division, the petitioner joined in his service on 26-6-2013 and the letter dated 20-5-2013 (Annexure-S) has been issued by the Upazila Secondary Education Officer, Amtali, Barguna at the instance of the petitioner.

7. The learned Advocate Mr ABM Siddiqur Rahman Khan appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that inquiry committee headed by Sukumar Chandra Hawlader without hearing the petitioner at the instance of the President of the Ad-hoc Managing Committee had given an ex parte and false report without any basis of materials and the Ad-hoc Managing Committee of the school had no authority to dismiss any teacher of the school and the dismissal order of the petitioner has not been sent to the Appeal and Arbitration Committee for its examination and approval of the Board as per Rule 12 of the Recognized Non-government Secondary School Teachers (Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education, Jessore) Terms and Conditions of Service Regulations, 1979. He further submits that the inquiry committee formed by the respondent No. 1 found the allegations brought against the petitioner untrue and subsequently the Ad-hoc Managing Committee of the school after expiry of two years by resolution dated 25-9-2013 confirmed the service of the petitioner with effect from 1-10-2013 and thereafter, elected Managing Committee also by the resolution dated 9-11-2013 had withdrawn the order of dismissal dated 26-11-2012 and further decided not to contest in the Rule against the petitioner. He also submits that after issuance of the Rule, stay and direction dated 15-5-2013 passed by this Court, the petitioner joined in his service on 19-5-2013 and thereafter he continued in his service till 27-5-2017, on which date the Managing Committee of the school most illegally, arbitrarily and mala-fide violating the order of statuesque passed by the Hon'ble Appellate Division issued the impugned Annexure P and Q and as such the impugned Annexure P and Q are liable to be declared to have been issued without lawful authority and is of no legal effect.

8. The learned Advocate Mr Lutfor Rahman appearing on behalf of the respondent No.4 submits that the petitioner was dismissed from service on the basis of a report of an inquiry committee duly formed by the Ad-hoc Managing Committee and at the time of dismissal, he was a probationer and the Title Suit No. 323 of 2012 filed by the petitioner was dismissed as being not maintainable and the Title Appeal No. 6 of 2013 filed by the petitioner against the order of dismissal of Title Suit No. 323 of 2012 has been withdrawn and thereafter petitioner malafide filed the instant Writ Petition. He further submits that since the service of the petitioner was not confirmed by the Managing Committee, approval by the Board is not required. He candidly submits that the impugned Annexure P and Q have been issued by the Managing Committee of a Non-Government High school and any decision of the Managing Committee of the Non-Government High School is not amenable to writ jurisdiction.

9. We have heard the learned Advocate Mr ABM Sidduqur Rahman Khan who appeared on behalf of the petitioner and the learned Advocate Mr Lutfor Rahman who appeared on behalf of the respondent No. 4 and meticulously examined the Writ Petition, and the affidavit-in-opposition filed by the respondent No. 4.

10. The issue involved in the instant Rule as to whether the Ad-hoc Managing Committee of a Non-government High School has any authority to impose a penalty upon any teacher of a Non-Government High School violating the ad interim order passed by the Apex Court or not.

11. In this regard, it is required to reproduce the verbatim of the provision of Regulation 12 of The Recognized Non-Government Secondary School Teachers (Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education, Jessore) Terms and Condition of Service Regulation, 1979 which is as under;

12. Regulation 12: Power to impose penalty:-The power to impose penalty upon a teacher under Regulation 11 shall vest in the authority competent to make appointment; provided that the penalties of dismissal or removal from service shall not be imposed unless the proposal for such penalty is examined by the Appeal and Arbitration Committee and approved by the Board.

13. In this regard the Ministry of Education published a notification on 12-4-2011 pursuant to Regulation 54 of “বেসরকারী শিক্ষা প্রতিষ্ঠানের ম্যানেজিং কমিটি/গর্ভনিং বডি সংক্রান্ত প্রবিধানমালা, ২০০৯ restraining the Ad-hoc Managing Committee not to appoint any teacher or employee of a Non-Government High School and the contents of the notification dated 12-4-2011 is reproduced below:

“বেসরকারী শিক্ষা প্রতিষ্ঠানের ম্যানেজিং কমিটি/গভর্নিং বডি সংক্রান্ত প্রবিধানমালা ২০০৯ এর ৪১(২)(খ)৪ অনুযায়ী ম্যানেজিং কমিটি গভর্নিং বডিকে শিক্ষক-কর্মচারী নিয়োগের যে ক্ষমতা দেয়া হয়েছে তা কেবলমাত্র নিয়মিত ম্যানেজিং কমিটি/গভর্নিং বডির মাধ্যমে সম্পন্ন করতে হবে। কোন ক্রমেই এডহক বা বিশেষ ধরনের কমিটি/গভর্নিং বডির মাধ্যমে নিয়োগ প্রক্রিয়া সম্পন্ন করা যাবে না।

২। আলোচ্য প্রবিধানমালার ৫৪নং প্রতিবিধিতে বর্ণিত ক্ষমতাবলে বিষয়টি স্পস্ট করা হল। জনস্বার্থে এ আদেশ জারি করা হল এবং তা অবিলম্বে কার্যাকর করা হবে।

স্বাক্ষরিতঃ

১১-৪-২০১১

(ডঃ কামাল আবদুল নাসের চৌধুরী)

সচিব।

<u>14. On a careful reading of the Regulation 2(a) and 12 of the Recognized Non-government Secondary School Teachers (Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education, Jessore) Terms and Conditions of Service Regulations, 1979 and notification dated 12-4-2011 issued by the government pursuant to Regulation 54 of  “বেসরকারী শিক্ষা প্রতিষ্ঠানের ম্যানেজিং কমিটি/গর্ভনিং বডি সংক্রান্ত প্রবিধানমালা, ২০০৯ it reveals that an elected Managing Committee of a Non-Government High School is the only appointing authority of any teacher and an Ad-hoc Managing Committee is not competent to appoint any teacher of Non-government High School. As appointing authority, an elected Managing Committee is only legally authorized to impose any penalty upon a teacher under regulation 11 subject to examination of the Appeal and Arbitration Committee and approval by the Board. In the instant case, before dismissing the petitioner from service, the Ad-hoc Managing Committee of the school did not send the proposal for dismissal to the Appeal and Arbitration Committee for examination and approval of the Board. An order of dismissal of any teacher of Non-government High School by Ad-hoc Managing Committee is without jurisdiction and a nullity.</u>

15. The above view of this Court also gets support from the decision made in the case of Akhil Krishna Chakraborti vs Bharati Rani, reported in 3 CLR (AD) 30, Pam 10, 22 DLR (1970) 669, Para 14 made in the case of Abdul Rashid vs Hari Pada Sarkar, 2012 BLT (AD) 239: Zulfikar Mahmud vs National University.

<u>16. In Regulation 12 of the Recognized Non-government Secondary School, (Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education, Jessore) Terms and Conditions of Service Regulations, 1979, the legislature also laid down the procedure of imposing a penalty of dismissal or removal of any teacher of Non-government High School. Under Regulation 12, before dismissing or removing any teacher of Non-Government High School, an elected Managing Committee is duty bound to send the proposal for dismissal or removal from service to the Appeal and Arbitration Committee for examination and approval of the Board. There is no scope to send the order of dismissal to the Appeal and Arbitration Committee for examination and approval of the Board. Subsequent approval of the order of dismissal or removal of any Teacher of Non-Government High School by the Board is illegal and not sustainable in law.</u>

17. On careful scrutiny of the records it transpires that the petitioner filed representation to respondent No. 1, the Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education Board, Barisal against the allegation brought against him by the Ad-hoc Managing Committee and the respondent No. 1 directed the respondent No. 3, Upazila Secondary Education Officer, Amtali, Barguna, to inquire into the allegations brought against the petitioner by the Ad-hoc Managing Committee of the school and respondent No. 3 after inquiry found the allegations brought against the petitioner untrue and submitted report on 18-2-2013 (Annexure-K) to the respondent No. 2. It also transpires that Ad-hoc Managing Committee of the school before dismissing the petitioner although formed an inquiry committee to inquire into the allegations brought against the petitioner, but said inquiry committee without hearing the petitioner submitted an ex parte report against him and on the basis of a biased report, the Ad-hoc Managing Committee of the school dismissed the petitioner from service without sending the proposal for dismissal to the Appeal and Arbitration Committee for examination and approval of the Board as required under Regulation 12 of the aforesaid Regulations.

18. On perusal of the records it appears that the Managing Committee in its meeting held on 25-9-2013 (Annexure-Z-2) unanimously confirmed the service of the petitioner as Headmaster of the school and after confirmation of the service of the petitioner, the election of the Managing Committee was held and Mr Md Motiur Rahman was elected as the President of the Managing Committee and the elected Managing Committee in its meeting held on 9-11-2013(Annexure Z-4) had withdrawn the order of dismissal dated 26-11-2012 holding that the Ad-hoc Managing Committee is not legally authorized to dismiss the Headmaster of the school and also decided not to contest in the instant Rule against the petitioner, but the respondent No. 4 without any further decision of the Managing Committee at her sweet- will contest the Rule and during pendency of the Rule with an ill motive showing disrespect to the authority of this Court and violating the order of statuesque passed by the Hon'ble Appellate Division in Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 1325 of 2013 malafide by order dated 27-5-2017 (Annexure Q) directed Md Delwar Hossain, a senior teacher of the said school to take over the charge of the Headmaster.

19. It further transpires that after the dismissal of the petitioner, both the Managing Committee allowed him to discharge his duty as Headmaster of the school and in the meantime, the petitioner and other teachers of the school obtained the MPO from the concerned authority and he performed all function as Headmaster. After expiry of the term of the previous elected Managing Committee of the school, he also conducted the election of the present Managing Committee which has been approved on 16-2-2017 by the Board including the petitioner as Member Secretary (ex-officio Headmaster) and Zakia Alice, respondent No. 4, as President of the Managing Committee and after due approval of the Managing Committee the respondent No. 4 also allowed the petitioner to discharge his duty as Headmaster till 27-5-2017 but the respondent No. 4 suddenly and surprisingly without any basis mala fide issuing Annexure-Q on 27-5-2017 directed Md Delwar Hossain, Senior teacher of the school to hold the charge of the Headmaster holding that at the time of filing the writ petition, the petitioner was not in service suppressing the fact that after passing the order of stay and direction dated 15-5-2013 passed by this Court, the petitioner joined in service on 19-5-2013 which is evident from the Annexure S, letter dated 20-5-2013 (Annexure S) issued by the Upazila Secondary Education Officer, Amtali, Barguna.

20. Although the Annexure P and Q have been issued by the Managing Committee of a Non-government High School and the said decision is not amenable to writ jurisdiction, but those Annexure have been issued violating the ad-interim order, passed by no less a Court but the Appellate Division during pendency of the instant Rule and as such the same is void ab initio and have no force of law. The above view of this Court lends support from the decision made in the case of MA Bari vs Uttara Sarkari Officers Quarter Kallayan Samity, reported in 55 DLR 289 wherein it has been observed in the following terms:

"While the order of stay was in force the Department of Social Welfare accorded registration in favour of the samity of the writ petitioners. Hence the registration is invalid and a nullity."

<u>21. It is found that the Ad-hoc Managing Committee of the School on the basis of an ex parte and biased report mala fide dismissed the petitioner from service without prior approval of the Board. Mala fide is of two kinds, Malice in law and Malice in fact. Malice-in-fact is an act done with ill will or motive against a person. Malice-in-law is a wrongful act intentionally done to cause injury. In Bromage vs Prosser (1825) IC & P; 673:4 B & C it is opined that "Malice in law means the doing of a wrongful act intentionally without just cause or excuse" It depends upon knowledge and deliberately done in disregard to the right of others. The concept of Malice-in law and Malice-in fact, has been succinctly expressed by Lord Haldane in Shearer vs Shields (1914) AC 808 page 813-814 in the following language.</u>

<u>"Between" malice-in- fact and malice in-law" there is a board distinction which is not peculiar to any system of jurisprudence. The person who inflicts a wrong or an injury upon any person in contravention of the law is not allowed to say that he did so with an innocent mind. He is taken to know the law and can only act within the law. He may be, therefore, be guilty of 'malice-in-law' although, so far as the state of his mind was concerned he acted intentionally, and in that sense innocently. Malice-in-fact is a different thing. It means an actual malicious intention on the part of the person who has done the wrongful act."</u>

22. In the case of SR Venkatareunan vs the Union of India, reported in (1979) 2 SCC 491, their Lordships observed in the following language:

"Malice in its legal sense means malice such as may be assumed from the doing of a wrongful act intentionally but without just cause or excuse, or want of reasonable or probable cause."

23. It reveals that the before dismissing the petitioner from service, proposal for dismissal of the petitioner was not sent to the Appeal and Arbitration Council for examination and approval of the Board in accordance with Regulation 12 of the Recognized Non-government Secondary School Teachers (Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education, Jessore) Terms and Conditions of Service Regulations, 1979, and the service of the petitioner has been confirmed by the subsequent Ad-hoc Managing Committee with effect from 1-1-2013 and thereafter elected Managing Committee had withdrawn the dismissal order by resolution dated 9-11-2013 (Annexure Z-4). Therefore, there was nothing left for the subsequent Managing Committee to take any action against the petitioner on the same cause of action. After passing the order dated 15-5-2013 by this Court, the petitioner joined in his service on 19-5-2013 and discharged his duty as Headmaster till 17-5-2017 and the respondent No. 4 also allowed the petitioner to continue in his service from 16-2-2017 to 17-5-2017, but for reasons best known to the respondent No. 4 without any reasonable cause maliciously issued Annexure P and Q violating the order passed by the Apex Court. It is a settled principle that any act done in disobedience of the interim order of the Court is a nullity. Therefore, there is no doubt in our mind that Annexure P and Q are a nullity and no order in the eye of law.

24. The doctrine of approbate and reprobate which is fairly attracted in the case which found eloquent expression in the case of Ambu Nair, reported in AIR 1933 PC 167 in the following language:

"It is a well-accepted principle that a party cannot both approbate and reprobate. He cannot, to use the words of Honyman, J. in Smith vs Baker (1878) LR 8 CP 350 at p. 357 at the same time blow hot and cold. He cannot say at one time that the transaction is valid and thereby obtain some advantage to which he could only be entitled on the footing that it is valid, and at another time say it is void for the purpose of securing some further advantage."

25. In the Case of Nurul Haque (Md) vs the Government of Bangladesh reported in 51 DLR (AD) 140, Para 6 our Apex Court also endorsed the same view wherein Latifur Rahman, J as his Lordship then was, observed in the following language;

"The petitioner having accepted the benefit cannot now term the same as illegal. The High Court Division in exercising Writ jurisdiction rightly refused to exercise discretion in favour of the petitioner as it is unconscionable to blow hot and cold in the same breath."

26. The decision of the Indian Supreme Court made in RN Goswami vs Yashpal Dhir

reported in AIR 1993 SC 352, speaks out the same principle in a different language:

"Law does not permit a person to both approbate and reprobate. This principle is based on the doctrine of election which postulates that no party can accept and reject the same instrument and that a person cannot say at one time that a transaction is valid and thereby obtain some advantage, to which he could only be entitled on the footing that it is valid, and then turn round and say it is void for the purpose of securing some other advantage."

27. The above view of the Indian Supreme Court has been reiterated in the subsequent case like City Montessori School vs State of Uttar Pradesh, 14 SCC 253, and New. Bihar Biri Leaves Co vs The State of Bihar reported in 1981 (I) SCC 537. In New Bihar case it has been held that;

"It is a fundamental principle of general application that if a person of his own accord, accepts a contract on certain terms and works out the contract, he cannot be allowed to adhere to and abide by some of the terms of the contract which proved advantageous to him and repudiate the other terms of the contract which might be disadvantageous to him. The maxim is qui approbate non-reprobate (one who approbates cannot reprobate). This principle, though originally borrowed from Scots Law, is now firmly embodied in English Common law. According to it, a party to an instrument or transaction cannot take advantage of one part of a document or transaction and reject the rest. That is to say, no party can accept and reject the same instrument or transaction (Per Scrutton, Verschueren Creameries Ltd. vs Hull & Netherlands Steamship Co.)"

28. On scrutiny of the records, it appears that the respondent No. 1 approved the Ad-hoc Managing Committee of the Mofiz Uddin Girls Pilot High School by order dated 29-8-2012 (Annexure C) for a period of 6 (six) months and the term of the said committee expired on 29-2-2013 and thereafter on 11-6-2013 Mesbah Uddin, President of the former Ad-hoc Managing Committee filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 1325 of 2013 and on the same day obtained the order of stay and status quo from the Hon'ble Appellate Division.

29. While the petitioner was discharging his duty as Headmaster, Zakia Alice, respondent No. 4, was elected President of the Managing Committee of the school and she also allowed the petitioner to discharge his duty as Headmaster from 16-2-2017 to 27-5-2017. Therefore, the respondent No. 4 cannot be allowed to blow hot and blow cold at the same time in disregard to his right to continue as Headmaster of the school unless there is fresh cause of action for dismissal.

30. Since after issuance of the Rule, stay and direction dated 15-5-2013, the petitioner joined in his service on 19-5-2013 as Headmaster of Mofiz Uddin Girls Pilot High School, Amtali, Barguna and discharged his duty till 27-5-2017 and the letter dated 27-5-2017 (Annexure-Q) and striking out the name of the petitioner from the salary sheet from month of April 2017 (Annexure-P) have no force of law, there is nothing left for the respondents to take appropriate measures for settling the disputes between the petitioner and the respondent No. 4. In view of the above, the petitioner is entitled to continue in his service as Headmaster of the school and respondents are hereby directed to allow the petitioner to discharge his duty as Headmaster of Mofiz Uddin Girls Pilot High School, Amtali, Barguna.

31. Both the Rules are thus disposed of with observation and direction as above.

However, there will be no order as to cost.

End.
