full_judgment:
Mr. Surendra Kumar Sinha, CJ. :- A cryptic law point is involved in this appeal —it is whether in view of the amendment of the Code of Civil Procedure by gazette notification dated 24th September, 2012 adding two provisos to rule 17 of order 6 after the word 'parties' by substituting colon mark (;) for the full stop, an amendment to the plaint can be allowed at the appellate stage. The added provisos read as under: 
"Provided that no application for amendment shall be allowed after the trial has commenced, unless the Court is of opinion that in spite of due diligence, the party could not have raised the matter before the commencement of trial. 
Provided further that if an application for amendment is made after the trial has commenced and the Court is of opinion that the application is made to delay the proceedings, the Court shall make an order for the payment to the objector such cost by way of compensation as it thinks fit." 

2. To resolve the point in controversy short facts are narrated as under. Respondents instituted Title Suit No.94 of 2011 against the appellant seeking enforcement of power of attorney dated 4th August, 1999 empowering him to do all acts, deeds and things in the said power, and to declare the deed of revocation of the power of attorney dated 29th July, 2010 void with some other reliefs. During the pendency of the suit the plaintiffs made some amendments to the plaint and ultimately the suit was dismissed by the trial Court. Plaintiffs then preferred an appeal in the High Court Division and in the appellate forum they prayed for amendment of the plaint as under: 
a) After full stop (.) in paragraph 9, the following sentences be added 'for the same reasons, the Deed of Revocation of Power of Attorney being Deed No.8427 registered on 29.7.2010 is also liable to be cancelled. Hence, the plaintiffs also seek cancellation of the Deed of Revocation of the Power of Attorney being Deed No.8427 registered on 29.7.2010. 
b) In prayer (b) after the words 'and without any effect' the words 'and to cancel the said Deed of Revocation of the Power of Attorney being Deed No.8427 registered on 29.7.2010 be added. 
c) At the end of paragraph 2 after the full stop (.), the following sentence be added `the plaintiffs also seek consequential relief in the suit by way of cancellation of the Deed of Revocation of the Power of Attorney being Deed No.8427 dated 29.7.2010 and maximum Court fees are paid thereon. 

The High Court Division allowed the prayer for amendment.

3. Mr. Rokauddin Mahmud, learned Counsel argues that the High Court Division fell in an error in failing to consider that the plaintiffs have exhausted all avenues of amending the plaint on 10th February, 2013, 24th March, 2013 and 9th November, 2014 and those amendments having been made after framing issues, the last amendment made in the appellate forum is to fill up the lacuna and as such is not permissible in law, inasmuch as, they could have amended the plaint prior to the trial of the suit. Secondly, it is argued that though amendment of pleadings is discretionary power, it should not be exercised on mere asking by the plaintiffs and the power of the Court should not be exercised arbitrarily. Thirdly, it is argued that after the amendment of the Code of Civil Procedure, no amendment can be made unless it is proved by sufficient materials that the party seeking amendment was diligent in prosecuting with the proceeding, and the Court cannot take away the right accrued in favour of the appellants under the amended provision of the Code in the absence of sufficient explanation that there was no neglect and latches in not seeking proper amendment in time and that the prayer for amendment was made bonafide. 

4. On the question of amendment of the pleadings the opinions the superior Courts of this sub-continent are almost identical. It is that an amendment to the pleadings can be made at any stage of the proceedings but such amendment cannot be made if the nature and character of the suit is changed; that the amendment is barred on the date of institution of the suit; that the amendment should be allowed with a view to resolving all controversies over the same subject matter between the parties and this will prevent the multi-furiousness of proceedings; that all reliefs ancillary to the main relief which is in the nature of additional relief should be allowed as general rule. The averments in the plaint and written statements are pleadings, but in respect of amendment of the written statement the Code is a bit more liberal, inasmuch as, there is also a provision in the Code to file additional written statement under Order 8, Rule 9 of the Code. Secondly, as regards the question of limitation both the plaintiffs and defendants are not standing on the same footing, inasmuch as, the question of limitation does not arise in case of the amendment of the written statement. 

5. The Judicial Committee of the Privy Council in Md. Zahoor Ali Khan V. Mst. Thakooranee Rutta Koer, 11 MIA 468 and Charan Das V. Amir Khan, AIR 1921 PC 50 consistently maintained that the Court has undoubtedly full power to allow such amendment even where a legal right had accrued by lapse of time if the special circumstances of the case outweigh such' considerations. In Keramat Ali V. Muhammad Yunus Haji, 15 DLR (SC) 120, Hamoodur Rahman, J. speaking for the Court observed that in exercising the power of amendment 'no doubt', this Court would be reluctant to allow an amendment which would have the effect of totally altering the nature of the suit or of taking away a valuable right accrued by lapse of time, but where in the circumstances of a particular case it would be plainly inequitable to refuse such relief this Court will not hesitate to do what the judicial committee did -----,, 

6. In Managing Committee V. O.R. Chowdhury, 31 DLR (AD) 133, this Court has observed that 'the amendment of the pleadings could be allowed at any stage of the proceedings for the purpose of determining the real question of controversy between the parties but it could not be allowed, if, it changed the nature and character of the suit, or if the prayer for amendment had become barred by lapse of time and a right had accrued to other side. In Akitullah V. Zafala Begum, 10 BLT (AD) 132, this Court held that before allowing any amendment to the plaint the Court must come to a finding that such amendment is necessary for determining the real question in controversy between the parties and that the same shall not change the nature and character of the suit. In Abdul Motaleb V. Ed. Ershad Ali, 18 BLD (AD) 121, this Court again reiterated the views of the Privy Council. 

7. In Abdul Karim Meah Vs. Arch Bishop Christian, 36 DLR (AD) 38 this Court observed that amendment of the plaint may be allowed at any stage of a proceeding according to the established rules and practices governing amendment. If amendment does not prejudice the right of the other party nor does it change the character of a suit, there is no reason why amendment should not be allowed if it is found necessary to determine the real issues between the parties. In another case of the same issue in Radha Krishna V. Dwarka Das at page 253(258) this Court approved the dictum of the Judicial Committee and Supreme Court of Pakistan. This Court posed a question as to whether the Court will allow amendment of the plaint or refuse to do so would depend upon the question whether the nature of the suit would be altered thereby. Then the Court quoting an observation of the Judicial Committee that "the Court had undoubtly full power to allow such amendment even where a legal right had accrued by lapse of time if the special circumstances of the case outweighed such consideration" approved the above views observing that we did not find anything therein which is against allowing the prayer for amendment ....." 

8. In Indian Jurisdiction similar views have been taken in Leach V. Jardine Skinner, AIR 1957 SC 357. It has been observed in Para 16 that 'Courts would, as a rule, decline to allow amendments, if a fresh suit on the amended claim would be barred by limitation on the date of the application. But that is a factor to be taken into account in exercise of the discretion as to whether amendment should be ordered and does not affect the power of the Court to order it, if that is required in the interest of justice'. In another case of the same issue, in Pirgonda Hongonda Patil V. Kalgonda Shidgonda Patil, AIR 1957 SC 363, the question was whether the addition of a relief or reliefs in a suit would change the nature and character of the suit. It was observed that it is not feasible nor advisable to encase a discretionary power within the strait jacket on an inflexible formula. In that case there was defect in the plaint that stood in the way of the plaintiff in getting the relief and despite pointing out the defect by the defendant no amendment was made in the trial Court and the suit was dismissed on the ground of such defect. In the High Court the prayer for amendment was allowed at the appellate stage. The respondent objected to the amendment on the ground that the amendment was barred by limitation on the date of the prayer since the appellant by filing petition raised the defect at the trial stage. The Court observed that the quality and quantity of the reliefs sought remain the same; whether the relief should be granted or not is a different matter as to which Court is not called upon to express any opinion at the stage of amendment. The Court then with approval of the views taken by Batchelor, J. in 32 Bomb 644 observed as under: 

"All amendments ought to be allowed which satisfy the two conditions (a) of not working injustice to the other side, and (b) of being necessary for the purpose of determining the real questions in controversy between the parties .... But I refrain from citing further authorities, as, in my opinion, they all lay down precisely the same doctrine. That doctrine, as I understand it, is that amendment should be refused only where the other party cannot be placed in the same position as if the pleading had been originally correct, but the amendment would cause him an injury which could not be compensated in costs. It is merely a particular case of this general rule that where a plaintiff seeks to amend by setting up a fresh claim in respect of a cause of action which since the institution of the suit has become barred by limitation, the amendment must be refused; to allow it would be to cause the defendant an injury which could not be compensated in costs by depriving him of a good defence to the claim. The ultimate test therefore still remains the same; can the amendment be allowed without injustice to the other side, or can it not ?" 

9. This Court along with Indian and Pakistan Supreme Court observed that in amending a plaint, the nature and character of the suit cannot be changed by amendment and that the addition of one or more reliefs will not change the nature and character of the suit, inasmuch as, adding of a relief may become necessary when there appears other complication in getting the full relief and that by reason of this change the suit property rests on the same foundation. More so, all reliefs ancillary to main relief and those are in the nature of additional should be allowed as general rule. Finally the disclosure in written statement requires amendment to the plaint, such prayer should be allowed. 

10. If we read the language used in rule 17 of Order 6, the power of the Court to allow amendment is wide. The first sentence is cast in affirmative, that is to say, the Court may at any stage of the proceedings allow either party to alter or amend his pleadings. It has been enacted with no object other than to facilitate the task of administration of justice. The language used in it is used very wide terms that the Courts power to allow amendment has been considerably enlarged. In the alternative, the Court should adopt a liberal approach in allowing the amendment and it should not disallow on hypothetical grounds. The second limb of the rule is that the amendment of the pleadings may be allowed on such terms 'as may be just'. So the Court is required to see whether the amendment is necessary for just and proper adjudication of the case. So, the Court is left with no discretion but to allow the amendment if the proposed amendment is just for proper adjudication of the suit. The other condition is that the Court is required to see that amendment is necessary 'for the purpose of determining the real question in controversy between the parties'. So, the amendment of the pleadings should be allowed which are necessary for determination of the real controversy in the suit. 

11. The Court on close reading of the language of the rule added conditions as to when an amendment should be allowed. It observed that if the proposed amendment does not alter or substitute any cause of action on the basis of which the original lis was raised; that no amendment should be allowed which amounts to defeating a legal right accrued to the opposite party on account of lapse of time and that if the amendment takes away a legal right of the defendant by lapse of time or in the alternative, amendment ought to be allowed if the amended plaint would not be barred on the date of filing the suit. 

12. In Craies on 'Statute Law', Seventh Edn., it is stated, statutes passed for the purpose of enabling something to be done are usually expressed in permissive language, that is to say, it is enacted that `it shall be lawful' etc., or that 'such and such a thing may be done'. 'Prima-facie' these words import a discretion, and they must be construed as discretionary unless there be anything in the subject-matter to which they are applied, or in any other part of the statute, to show that they are meant to be inoperative.' (Fleming & Farguson Ltd. V. Burgh of Paisley, 1948 S.C. 547). 

13. The words it shall be lawful are words said Lord Cairns in Julius V. Bishop of Exford, (1880) 5 A.C. 214(222) `making that legal and possible which would otherwise be no right or authority to do. They confer a faculty or power, and they do not of themselves do more than confer a faculty or power. But there may be something in the nature of the thing empowered to be done, something in the object for which it is to be done, something in the conditions under which it is to be done, something in the title of the persons for whose benefit the power is to be exercised, which may couple the power with a duty, and make the duty of the persons in whom the power is reposed to exercise that power when called upon to do so. These words being, according to their natural meaning, permissive or enabling words only, it lies upon those who contend that an obligation exists to exercise this power to show in the circumstances of the case something which, according to the principles I have mentioned, creates an obligation.' 

14. Coleridge, J. speaking for the Court in Queen V. Tith Commissioners for England and Wales, (1849) 14 QB 459 observed, `It has been so often decided as to have become an axiom, that in public statutes words only directory, promissory, or enabling, may have a compulsory force where the thing to be done is for the public benefit or an advancement of public justice'. Where the power is coupled with a duty of the person to whom it is given to exercise it, then it is imperative (Re Bake (1890) 44 Ch D 262). In Indian Council of Legal Aid V. Bar Council, AIR 1995 S.C. 691, Ahmadi, C.J. speaking for the Court in paragraph 9 observed, 'where a provision is couched in positive language and is in the nature of an enabling provision, there is no canon of construction which says that by necessary implication the rule making authority can make a provision disentling admission or enrolment to the profession.'

15. It is now settled that an appeal is the continuation of the original proceeding because of the fact that all rules and procedures applicable to the trial Court are equally applicable to the appellate Court in view of Section 107 read with Order 41 of the Code. In the first proviso the legislature has attached condition that the Court shall not allow amendment after the trial has commenced if the litigant is negligent in pursuing the matter properly. It is in conflict with rule 17, inasmuch as, the pleadings are normally prepared by the lawyers of the parties. A litigant has no knowledge about the intricacies of pleadings. On perusal of the pleadings and the documents, if the lawyer finds defect in the pleadings, he advices his client to amend the pleadings. This defect may be detected at the appellate forum when a senior lawyer conducting the appeal finds the defect. Now under such circumstances how the Court will form opinion that in spite of due diligence, the plaintiff or the defendant has not rectified the defect before the commencement of trial? If the lawyer is competent one, he will make proper amendment at the preliminary stage of the suit after the filing of the written statement. Even if no such advice to amendment is given due to oversight or mistake, he may suggest to his client to make amendment showing reasons that his client has not brought the amendment despite his due diligence in prosecuting the matter, but if a lawyer is weak in drafting pleadings naturally it is not expected of him to explain the reasons for the delay properly. 

On plain reading of this proviso it suggests that the amendment incorporating facts which are within the knowledge of the party seeking amendment at the earliest opportunity would not be allowed after the commencement of the trial if no proper explanation is given regarding delay, but it is difficult to prove the same. The question is whether the amendment will be rejected if it is found relevant for the purpose of determining the real questions in controversy between the parties. The answer to the question is emphatically in negative. If the defect remains, there will arise multi-fariousness of proceedings and to obviate it from doing justice this rule 17 has been inserted. 

In the second proviso the legislature has given power to award cost if the Court finds that the amendment is made with a view to delaying the proceedings. This second proviso conflicts with the first proviso, inasmuch as, if the Court can allow the amendment with costs if it is satisfied that the litigant has made the amendment after the commencement of the trial with a view to delaying the matter, then it is not necessary to attach condition in the first proviso. Secondly, in rule 17 it is especially provided that amendment may be made at any stage 'on such terms' that is, the Court can allow amendment with costs. The expression 'on such terms' means if the Court allows amendment it has discretionary power to award a cost. The terms may be imposed in allowing an amendment must be such as have nexus with the application allowed or relief granted. 

These provisos curtail absolute discretion of the Court to allow amendment at any stage of the proceedings and this will lead to multiplicity of proceedings if the Court does not exercise its discretionary power properly. Though the object for this amendment is obvious -- it is with a view to preventing frivolous applications which are filed to delay the disposal of the proceedings finally, but by adding two provisos the legislature has made confusion. 

16. At any event, on perusal of the plaint, the prayer for amendment and other materials on record, we are satisfied that the proposed amendment is necessary for the purpose of determining the real questions in controversy between the parties and though it is made at a belated stage, the High Court Division has committed no error of law in allowing the amendment. However, if ought to have afforded the defendants to file additional written statement. More so, the High Court Division ought to have awarded cost at the time of allowing the prayer. The plaintiffs have made three amendments at the trial stage and from their conduct, it is apparent that there is neglect or latches in pursuing the suit properly, and therefore, the amendment should be allowed subject to payment of costs. While we maintain the order of the High Court Division, we award a cost of Tk.50,000/- to be paid by the plaintiffs to the defendants within 4(four) weeks from the date of receipt of the order, failing which, the order shall stand vacated. The defendants can file additional written statement within four weeks of payment of cost in default they will be debarred from filing the same. 

17. The appeal is dismissed with cost as above. 

End.

full_judgment:
Mr. Soumendra Sarker, J.:- The Rule issued calling upon the Opposite Party No.1 to show cause as to why the judgment and order dated 01.12.2016 passed by the learned District Judge, Patuakhali in Civil 'Revision No.66 of 2015 allowing the same and setting aside the judgment and order dated 19.11.2015 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Patuakhali in Title Suit No.99 of 1979 allowing the application under Order VI, rule 17 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for amendment of the plaint and another application under section 151 read with section 152 of the Code of Civil Procedure for amendment of the judgment and decree passed in Title Suit No.99 of 1979 should not be set aside and/or pass such other order or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper.

2. The facts leading to the issuance of the Rule in a nutshell can be stated thus, the present petitioners as plaintiffs instituted the original Title Suit being No.99 of 1979 in the Court of learned the then Sub-ordinate Judge, Patuakhali for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession contending inter alia that the land appertaining to Mouza Dabluganj of Kolapara police station under Patuakhali District in khatian No.295 measuring an area 9.88 acres originally belonged to one Arob Ali Sarder. Arob Ali died leaving behind two sons namely Kashem Ali and Najem Ali. Najem Ali transferred his 08 annas share in favour of one Abdul Motaleb, the predecessor of the plaintiff-petitioners by a registered kabala deed dated 16.02.1940 and the possession was delivered in favour of the purchaser. The original kabala deed of the plaintiffs was lost due to devastating cyclone in the year 1943 and taking advantage of that; Kashem Ali and Najem Ali with an ill-intention managed to get their names recorded in R.S. and S.A. khatians. After the death of Abdul Motaleb, the plaintiffs being his only heirs possessing the suit land. The defendants while threatened the plaintiffs; the plaintiffs instituted the original suit.

3. The contrary case of the contesting defendants No.1-3 in short is thus, that the suit land originally belonged to Kashem Ali, who did never transfer the land in favour of the predecessor of the plaintiffs. The plaintiff's predecessor only to grab the property created a forged document. The further case of the defendants is such that the plaintiffs have no right, title, interest and possession in the suit land. The defendants alleged that the original owner Arab Ali Sarder had two sons namely Kashem Ali and Najem Ali. Kashem Ali died unmarried leaving behind his only brother Najem Ali and after the death of Najem Ali his heirs are possessing the land.

4. During trial of the original suit the learned trial court after taking evidence from the sides of the respective parties, decreed the suit on contest by his judgment and decree dated 30.11.1985 and 07.12.1985 respectively. Subsequent to that judgment and decree, while the plaintiffs have been owning and possessing the suit property; they came to learn that a mistake has been committed by their engaged the then lawyer; in the plaint of the original suit and instead of actual R.S. plot No.4893 of R.S. khatian No. 296, the learned lawyer at the time of drafting of the plaint inserted R.S. plot No.4891 wrongly. The concerned R.S. khatian No.296 has been exhibited before the learned trial court; from where it is apparent that the R.S. plot is 4893 not 4891. The plaintiffs finding necessity to correct the plot number filed an application before the learned trial court to rectify the aforesaid clerical mistake in the judgment and decree passed in Title Suit No.99 of 1979 and the learned trial court by its judgment and order dated 19.11.2015 allowed both the applications for amendment of the plaint as well as amendment of the judgment and decree.

5. Being aggrieved, the defendants preferred a civil revision under section 115(2) of the Code of Civil Procedure in the court of learned District Judge, Patuakhali being Civil Revision No.66 of 2015 which was heard and disposed of by the learned District Judge, Patuakhali and the learned District Judge by the impugned judgment and order dated 01.12.2016 allowed the civil revision and set aside the order of the learned trial court.

6. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and order, the plaintiffs have preferred 2nd Revision in this Court with leave under section 115(4) of the Code of Civil Procedure and obtained the Rule with an interim order of status quo.

7. During hearing of the Rule Mr. Probir Neogi the learned Advocate appeared on behalf of the petitioners while Mr. Abdul Quiyum, the learned Advocate appeared on behalf of the opposite parties.

8. The learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners submits that the learned 1st court of revision during passing the impugned judgment and order committed gross illegality and irregularity. The learned Advocate further submits that the learned trial court was quite justified and lawful in allowing the applications for amendment, inasmuch as; the amendment which was sought for; was bona fide and due to the inadvertent mistake of the engaged lawyer for the plaintiff-petitioners. The learned Advocate further submits that the learned District Judge, Patuakhali has committed an error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice without considering that, it is an imperative duty of the court to correct the mistake and the power of the learned court under section 152 of the Code of Civil Procedure is unlimited and as such the impugned judgment and order is liable to be set aside. The learned Advocate also submits that the learned 1g Court of revision during disposal of the civil revision was totally misconceived in holding the view that the application for amendment is barred by limitation since there was no reason to hold such a view that the relief claimed by the plaintiff-petitioners was not within time. The learned Advocate in this context referred a decision of this court reported in 56 DLR 221. The learned Advocate argued that the learned District Judge, Patuakhali at the time of passing the impugned judgment and order failed to appreciate that the plaintiff-petitioners in order to prove their case, adduced sufficient credible evidence and certified copy of the relevant R.S. khatian No.296 which was duly proved and exhibited and in that relevant khatian; there is no existence of R.S. plot No.4891. It is the mistake of the learned lawyer who was engaged on behalf of the plaintiffs and inserted the plot No.4891 instead of correct plot No.4893. Therefore, obviously; it was simply a clerical mistake which was inadvertent and bona fide. To rectify this wrong inclusion of plot number the plaintiff-petitioners while came to know about the misdeed of the lawyer, filed the application for amendment and the learned trial court rightly considering the facts and circumstances of the case along with the relevant R.S. Khatian allowed the application. The learned Advocate lastly submits that the citation of decisions given by the learned 1 g court of revision in the impugned judgment and order are not applicable in the instant case due to distinguishable facts. The learned Advocate in support of his arguments referred another two decisions reported in 29 DLR 81 and AIR (36) 1949 Madras 282.

9. As against the aforesaid submissions of the learned Advocate for the petitioners, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite parties, opposing the Rule submits that the learned District Judge, Patuakhali during disposal of the civil revision committed no illegality or irregularity, rather; he was quite justified in allowing the civil revision and thereby setting aside the judgment and order passed by the trial court. The learned Advocate further submits that in fact, the decree which was passed by the trial court was on the unspecified land as described in the schedule of the plaint. There was no specification of the suit property, and it suffers from vagueness. The learned Advocate also submits that long after 30 years the applications for amendment were filed for correction of the plaint and judgment and decree which is mala fide and not tenable in the eye of law. The learned Advocate submits that under Order VII rule 3 and 4 of the Code of Civil Procedure the suit property must be specified, but the suit land which is described in the schedule of the plaint was not specified and on that schedule of the property the learned trial court illegally passed the judgment and decree. The learned Advocate lastly submits that the applications for amendment were time barred, and the learned District Judge, Patuakhali rightly treating the applications barred by limitation, passed the impugned judgment and order; which is not bad-in-law and not deserve interference of this Court. The learned Advocate in support of his contention referred some decisions reported in 22 BLC (AD) 254, 18 BLC (AD) 139, 33 CWN 958, 36 CWN 97 and 17 BLT (AD) 51.

10. Considering submissions of the learned Advocates, having gone through the order passed by the learned trial court in Title Suit No.99 of 1979 on 19.11.2015 and the impugned judgment and order dated 01.12.2016 passed by the 1st court of revision in Civil Revision No.66 of 2015 along with the relevant R.S. and S.A. khatians with the certified copes of plaint, judgment and decree, applications for amendment of the plaint as well as the judgment and decree passed by the trial court dated 07.12.1985 in Title Suit No.99 of 1979, it transpires that after the judgment and decree passed by the trial court in the original Title Suit No.99 of 1979, the learned trial court i.e. the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Patuakhali received

two applications from the side of the plaintiffs, one for amendment of the plaint under Order VI rule 17 along with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure and the other for amendment of the decree under section 151 and 152 of the Code of Civil Procedure, and after the hearing; allowed both the two applications in holding the view that; on perusal of the record; it is evident from the face of the papers that the contested judgment and decree dated 30.11.1985 and 07.12.1985 respectively was passed on the plot No.4891 of R.S. khatian No.296 corresponding to S.A. khatian No.264, but in fact; in the relevant khatians there is no existence of plot No. 4891. The learned trial court also observed that, inasmuch as; there is a wrong insertion of the plot number in the decree; the decree has become in fructuous and therefore; relying upon a decision of this court given in the case of Chand Mia and others —vs. M.A. Rajput Ghosh Bhadur & others, 56 DLR 221, the learned Joint District Judge, l Court, Patuakhali allowed the applications for amendment. Subsequently, the learned lm Court of revision vide the impugned judgment and order dated 01.12.2016 in Civil Revision No.66 of 2015 holding the view that the proposed amendment was not sought for within the statutory period of limitation and after citation of some decisions held that the order passed by the trial court suffers from illegality, and accordingly the learned District Judge, Patuakhali allowed the revisional application filed before him and set aside the order of the learned trial court.

11. In this context; on meticulous consideration of the case records and the applications for amendment of the plaint as well as the decree passed by the trial court, I find that the plaintiffs to the suit obtained the judgment and decree from the trial court on 30.11.1985 and 07.12.1985 respectively, against which no appeal was preferred yet from the side of the defendants, and as such it stands good. Obviously it has been specifically asserted from the side of the plaintiffs that their the then engaged lawyer in advertently instead of actual plot No.4893 inserted 4891 in the plaint which have got no existence in the relevant R.S. khatian No.296 and S.A. kahtian No.264 and these khatians were produced before the learned trial court and after proof, those were marked exhibited. The learned trial court on the basis of wrong inclusion of plot number in the schedule of the plaint passed the judgment and decree which has become practically infructuous due to wrong plot number. The matter was not within the knowledge of the plaintiffs earlier, and while they came to learn about the misdeed of the then learned engaged lawyer on behalf of them, they filed the applications for amendment of the plaint and decree.

12. On perusal of the relevant papers I find that, apparently the wrong inclusion of R.S. Plot No.4891 is a bona fide mistake of the learned the then engaged lawyer of the plaintiffs, inasmuch as; in the relevant R.S. khatian No.296, there is no existence of that plot number 4891 and there exist plot No.4893. Hence, for rectification of the aforesaid inadvertent clerical mistake, which was bona fide; the application for amendment of the plaint and decree were preferred by the plaintiff-petitioners and the learned trial court was quite justified in holding the view that there is no mala fide intention or negligence on the part of the plaintiffs as because their engaged lawyer committed the misdeed in inclusion of the actual plot number in the schedule of the plaint, which is no doubt, not the latches of the plaintiff-petitioners, and it is a decided matter in our legal arena that for the latches or fault of the lawyer, the party can not suffer; as well as a decree cannot the infructuous. As soon as, the matter came into the notice of the plaintiffs, they filed the applications for amendment and as such the accidental mistake or inadvertent error, which was committed earlier deserve rectification; which is not barred by any law. In this regard, the relevant provision of law incorporated in section 152 of the Code of Civil Procedure reads as follows:

"Clerical or arithmetical mistake in judgment, decrees or orders or errors arising therein from any accidental slip or omission may at any time be corrected by the Court either of its own motion or on the application of any of the parties."

Therefore, it is evident from the relevant law that there is no limitation of time for rectification of bona fide mistake, which is clerical or arithmetical mistake or accidental slip or omission. The statute is very much clear with regard to this, and it is a legislative recognition of the courts power to correct the fault which is bonafide and unintentional.

<u>13. I find support of this, in the decisions referred to from the side of the learned counsel for the petitioners in the case of Ibrahim Sheikh and others —vs. Janab Sk. alias Janab Ali Sk. & others, 29 DLR 81, and in the case law reported in 36 AIR(1949) Madras 282. Furthermore; with regard to limitation the decision cited from 56 DLR, 221 have got every nexus in this case. On the other hand, having every regard on the decisions referred to from the side of the learned counsel for the opposite parties, I am not out of place to advert that, due to distinguishable facts, features and circumstances, those are not applicable in the instant case.</u>

14. In the foregoing narrative, before parting, I must orserve that the learned District Judge, Patuakhali, in passing the impugned Judgment and order, apparently committed an error in law, resulting in an error in the decision, occasioning failure of justice and thereby it deserve interference of this court.

15. In the result, the Rule is made absolute without any order as to costs. The impugned judgment and order dated 01.12.2016 passed by the learned District Judge, Patuakhali in Civil Revision No.66 of 2015 allowing the same and setting aside the judgment and order dated 19.11.2015 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Patuakhali in Title Suit No.99 of 1979 allowing the application under Order VI Rule 17 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for amendment of the plaint and another application under section 151 read with section 152 of the Code of Civil Procedure for amendment of the judgment and decree passed in Title Suit No.99 of 1979 is hereby set aside.

16. The order of status quo granted earlier by this court at the time of issuance of the Rule stands vacated.

17. Send down the lower court's records immediately and communicate the judgment and order at once.

End.

case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 23.03.2004 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.2581 of 1998)
full_judgment:
Syed Mahmud Hossain J. This appeal by leave by the appellant is directed against the judgment and order of 23.03.2004 passed by a Single Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.2581 of 1998 making the Rule absolute. The Rule was obtained against the judgment and decree dated 28.02.1994 of the Court of Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge), Jamalpur, in Other Appeal No.23 of 1992 allowing the appeal upon reversing the judgment and decree dated 15.03.1992 of the Court of Additional Assistant Judge, Jamalpur in Title Suit No.47 of 1991 decreeing the suit.

<u>2. The suit was filed seeking declaration that the defendant No.3 has been appointed illegally as Principal of Aram Nagar Alia Madrasha (in short, Madrasha) and the plaintiff has been illegally released from the service of the said Madrasha.</u>

3. The facts leading to the filing of this appeal, in brief, are that plaintiff-appellant joined the service of the Madrasha on December 12, 1985 as Head Mohaddes and at that time, defendant No.3 was the Second Mohaddes and he was suspended for misappropriation of money of the Madrasha but the said suspension was later on withdrawn. The Principal of the Madrasha resigned in March, 1987 and thereupon there was an advertisement for appointment of new Principal and defendant No.3 applied for the post of Principal although he did not have the requisite qualification but was appointed as Principal and thereupon post of second Mohaddes having fallen vacant Moulavi Nurul Huda was appointed as second Mohaddes on June 17, 1988. Meanwhile, the post of Vice-Principal had fallen vacant in 1989 and Moulavi Lokman Hossain was appointed as Vice-Principal although he did not have the requisite qualification and the son-in-law of defendant No.3 was appointed as lecturer. Since defendant No.3 did not have the requisite qualification and the experience he used to request the plaintiff to work on his behalf. The plaintiff had refused to accede to the said request and consequently, defendant No.3 through an illegal resolution of May 27, 1990 got the plaintiff released from his service showing the plaintiff as additional teacher. It is the case of the plaintiff that before releasing him from service no notice was served on him and he was not heard and in removing him, the rules of the Madrasha Board were not followed. The plaintiff also contended that he was removed illegally from his service and that he was entitled to get Tk.36,760/- from the Madrasha and Tk.11,130/- from the Government but the said amounts were not paid to him.

4. Defendant No.3 contested the suit by filing written statement denying all the material statements made in the plaint. His case, in short, is that there was no cause of action for filing the suit and the suit as framed was not maintainable and the suit was barred by limitation and that civil Court had no jurisdiction to entertain the suit since the subject matter of the suit was the subject matter of the Administrative Tribunal. The definite case of defendant No.3 was that he joined the Madrasha on August 1, 1964 and in 1969 he was promoted as Mohaddes and when the post of Principal of the Madrasha had fallen vacant, the Madrasha Managing Committee advertised for filling up the post of Principal. He applied and was appointed Principal by the Managing Committee. The plaintiff applied for the post of Vice Principal but he was not selected. There was an audit of the accounts of the Madrasha by the Office of the Auditor and Accountant General and in the audit report the plaintiff was shown as an additional teacher. The plaintiff was directed to return the amount drawn by him as Head Mohaddes. The plaintiff was found surplus teacher. The Managing Committee released him from service as per rules of the Madrasha Board and the release of the plaintiff was quite legal.

5. The trial Court upon hearing the parties by its judgment and order dated 15.03.1992 decreed the suit on the findings that the defendant No.3 was illegally appointed Principal of the Madrasha and that the plaintiff was illegally released from service and as such he was entitled to get the reliefs as prayed for in the suit.

6. Against the judgment and decree of the trial Court, the defendant preferred Other Appeal No.23 of 1992 before the learned District Judge, Jamalpur. On transfer the appeal was heard and disposed of by the then Subordinate Judge, Jamalpur, who by his judgment and order dated 28.02.1994 allowed the appeal and reversed the judgment and decree of the trial Court on the finding that as the plaintiff did not seek consequential relief, mere declaration that defendant No.3 was illegally appointed as Principal of the Madrasha and that plain-tiff was illegally released from the Madrasha were not available.

7. Thereafter, the plaintiff filed Review Case No.17 of 1994 for reviewing the judgment and decree of the appellate Court, which was dismissed on 20.10.1994.

8. The plaintiff-respondent then moved the High Court Division by filing revisional application and obtained Rule in Civil Revision No.2581 of 1998. The learned Single Judge of the High Court Division by his judgment and order dated 23.03.2004 made the Rule absolute and set aside the judgment and decree of the appellate Court.

9. Feeling aggrieved by and dissatisfied with judgment and order passed by the High Court Division, defendant No.3 as the leave-petitioner moved this Division by filing Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No.980 of 2004, in which, leave was granted resulting in Civil Appeal No.01 of 2005.

10. Mr. A. B. M. Baizid, learned Advocate, appearing on behalf of the appellant, submits with reference to cases reported in different law journals that it has been consistently held that a simple suit like the present one for declaration without any prayer for consequential relief is not maintainable and that in the instant case admittedly the plaintiff has not prayed for any consequential relief and as such, the impugned judgment delivered by the High Court Division should be set aside.

11. We have considered the submissions of the learned Advocate, perused the impugned judgment and the materials on record.

12. At the very outset, it is necessary to go through the grounds, on which, leave was granted, which are as under:

"In the decisions reported in 35 DLR 224, 48 DLR 330 and 49 DLR 38, it has been consistently held that a simple suit, like the present one, for declaration without further relief is not maintainable, as such the High court Division was in error in holding otherwise placing reliance on the decision reported in 55 DLR 151 and thereby upon giving go by to the established chain of decisions has arrived at an incorrect decision causing failure of justice. Plaintiff-respondent No.1 having had not applied for the post of the Principal of the Madrasha he cannot make grievance against the petitioner on his appointment as the Principal of the Madrasha, and also cannot maintain the suit against the petitioner for having no locus standi, and thus the High Court Division without taking judicial notice of the said particular aspect of the case having arrived at a wrong decision in the case caused failure of justice. The judgment of this Division in Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No.299 of 1983 (Shahjahan Mia Vs. Manager, Personnel Division, Sonali Bank disposed of on September 7, 1983) wherein it has been held "Since the plaintiffs prayer for declaration was not followed by any consequential relief the learned Judge commit-ted no illegality in holding that the omission to pray for any consequential relief for the purpose of enforcing declaratory decree was hit by the proviso to Section 42 of the Specific Relief Act".

13. Admittedly, the petitioner joined the service of the Madrasha on 12.12.1985 as Head Mohaddes. The Principal of the Madrasha resigned in March, 1987 where-upon an advertisement was made for appointment of a new Principal and defendant No.3 applied for the post of Principal although he did not have the requisite qualification. But defendant No.3 was appointed as Principal and as a result, the post of second Mohaddes having fallen vacant Moulavi Nurul Huda was appointed as second Mohaddes on 17.06.1988. Meanwhile, the post of Vice-Principal had fallen vacant and Moulavi Lokman was appointed as Vice-Principal although he did not have requisite qualification and experience. Defendant No.3 requested the plaintiff to work on his behalf and as the plaintiff refused to accede to that request, defendant No.3 through an illegal resolution dated 27.05.1990 got the plaintiff released from service showing him as an Additional Teacher. The plaintiff contended that his removal was illegal. The plain-tiff also sought declaration that defendant No.3 had been illegally appointed as Principal of the Madrasha. It is alleged by the plaintiff that before release from service he was not heard in person and no notice was served upon him before release. It was also alleged that defendant No.3 with mala fide intention got the plaintiff released from service by exhibit-2(a) which is extracted below:

‘আপনাকে এই মর্মে অবগত করানো যাইতেছে যে, বিগত ২৭/৫/৯০ইং তারিখে অত্র মাদ্রাসা গভর্নিং বডির সর্বম্মত সিদ্ধান্ত মোতাবেক এবং গণপ্রজাতন্ত্রী বাংলাদেশ সরকারের পরিশোধ এবং হিসাব নিরীক্ষণ অধিদপ্তরের শিক্ষা মন্ত্রণালয় ও মহা-পরিচালকের অধিদপ্তর, শিক্ষা ভবন, ঢাকা কর্তৃক মাদ্রাসা বোর্ডের রিপোর্ট অনুযায়ী যেহেতু আপনি একজন স্ট্যাম্পিং পার্টনার বহির্ভূত অতিরিক্ত মহাদ্দেশ হিসাবে গণ্য হইয়াছেন। বর্তমানে কামিল ও ফাজিল শ্রেণীতে অতিরিক্ত শাখা না থাকায় অত্যন্ত পরিতাপের সহিত গভর্নিং বডির সর্ব সম্মত সিদ্ধান্ত অনুযায়ী ২৬/৬/৯০ইং তারিখ হইতে আপনাকে মাদ্রাসার চাকুরী হতে অব্যাহতি দে���য়া হইল।’

14. It appears that defendant No.3 only produced one inspection report sent by the Director, Audit and Accounts, Ministry of Education, which was marked as exhibit-A. Curiously enough, it was not stated in the report that the plaintiff was an excess teacher outside the staff-pattern. Defendant No.3 showing the plaintiff as an excess teacher got him released from service. Had the plaintiff been an excess Mohaddes outside the staff-pattern, the Madrasha Education Board would have taken action against him. Admittedly, no notice was served upon the plaintiff before his release from service and that he was not given any personal hearing. Regulation 13(c) of Madrasha Education Board Governing Bodies and Managing Committees Regulations, 1979 provided as under:

১৩. গভর্নিং বডি বা ম্যানেজিং কমিটির ক্ষমতা:

এ.---------

বি.--------

সি. চাকুরিচ্যুত, অপসারণ বা শিক্ষক-দর (অধ্যক্ষ বা তত্ত্বাবধায়কসহ) নিম্নপদ নামিয়ে দেয়া, এসব শৃঙ্খলামূলক কাজ। শর্ত যে, কাউকে শুনানীর সযোগ না দিয়ে এমন কঠোর ব্যবস্থা গ্রহণ করা যাবে না।

15. Defendant No.3 admitted in his cross-examination that no approval was taken before releasing the plaintiff from service according to Rule 8 of the Rules and that no notice was served upon him to show cause as to why he should not be released and that there was no paper to show that the plaintiff was a temporary teacher.

16. Therefore, it can be easily resolved that the Managing Committee of the Madrasha without hearing the plaintiff in person ex parte decided that he was an excess Mohaddes outside the staff-pattern and as such the memo dated 26.06.1990 releasing him from service was illegal and without jurisdiction.

17. Admittedly, on the face of the record, it appears that defendant No.3 was appointed Principal of the Madrasha having no qualification. P.W.3 in cross-examination admitted that he passed in 'Kamil' examination in second class and he did not have any masters degree. The trial Court and the appellate Court having considered all aspects of the case found that defendant No.3 had been illegally appointed to the post of Principal of the Madrasha although he did not have the requisite qualification and that he in collusion with the members of the Managing Committee arranged the so-called interview and he alone appeared before the interview board and subsequently, he was selected collusively. Defendant No.3 admitted in his evidence that he alone appeared before the interview board. Defendant No.2 in his cross-examination stated that defendant No.3 is his nephew and that there were two other applicants but only defendant No.3 appeared before the interview board and that the others were not given any date to appear before the interview board. Defendant No.11 who is a member of the Managing Committee of the Madrasha deposed that the Principal did not have the requisite qualification.

18. Having considered all aspects of the case, the trial Court and the appellate Court found that defendant No.3 was illegally appointed as Principal of the Madrasha and that the plaintiff had been illegally released from service. The findings of the trial Court and the appellate Court are based on proper appreciation of the materials on record.

19. The appellate Court, however, came to the finding that without any prayer for consequential relief the present suit for declaration was not maintainable. Accordingly, the appellate Court set aside the judgment of the trail Court and dis-missed the suit.

20. The learned Advocate for the appellant cites the case of Dhunat Degree College Vs. Md. Abdus Samad and others, (1997) 49 DLR 38; Manager, Personal Division Vs. Sazahan Miah and others (1983) 35 DLR 224; and Sonali Bank and another vs. Chandan Kumar Nandi (1996) 48 DLR 330 where it has been held that in service matter a suit for simple declaration without prayer for consequential relief was not maintainable.

21. The principle of law laid down above is not disputed but the application of such principle may vary from case to case. The High Court Division relied on the case of General Manager (West Zone), Bangladesh Railway and others Vs. Din Mohammad and others (1999) 7 BLT (AD) 361. In the case referred to above, the plaintiffs only sought declaration that the plaintiffs were entitled to get appointment.

22. In the case referred to above, no con-sequential relief was prayed for according to the proviso to section 42 of the Specific Relief Act and this Division found that such a suit for mere declaration is maintainable.

<u>23. In the case in hand, admittedly, the present Madrasha is regulated by the Madrasha Education Board, a statutory body, and the Managing Committee of the Madrasha is under the legal obligation to act in accordance with the Rules and Regulations made by the Madrasha Education Board. But to our utter surprise, we find that before releasing the plaintiff from service no concurrence of the Madrasha Education Board was taken and that he was not even given a personal hearing. Surprisingly, the appointment of the Principal of the Madrasha was made contrary to the Rules and Regulations of the Madrasha Education Board. Such arbitrary and unauthorized exercise of power by the Managing Committee of the Madrasha should not go unnoticed. Since the activities of the present Madrasha is regulated by the Rules and Regulations of the Madrasha Education Board, the Managing Committee cannot do whatever it likes. Therefore, we are of the view that the present suit is maintainable even with-out prayer for consequential relief.</u>

24. The High Court Division was justified in making the Rule absolute setting aside the judgment and decree of appellate Court and affirming the judgment and decree of the trial Court.

25. In the light of the findings made before, we do not find any substance in this appeal. Accordingly, the appeal is dis-missed.

End.

full_judgment:
Mr. A.K.M. Shahidul Huq, J. :- On an application at the instance of the petitioner under Article 102 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh, a Rule Nisi was issued calling upon the respondent Nos.l-2 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 20.05.2014 passed by the learned Judge, Appellate Tribunal, অর্পিত সম্পত্তি প্রত্যার্পণ আপীল ট্রাইব্যুনাল, Sirajgonj in অর্পিত সম্পত্তি প্রত্যার্পণ আপীল মামলা নং-০৫/২০১৪ allowing the appeal and reversing those judgment and decree dated 08.09.2013 passed by the learned Judge, অর্পিত সম্পত্তি প্রত্যার্পণ অতিরিক্ত ট্রাইব্যুনাল-১, সিরাজগঞ্জ in অর্পিত সম্পত্তি প্রত্যার্পণ আপীল মামলা নং-৭৩৪/২০১২ whereby the application filed by the petitioners were allowed in part should not be declared to have been passed/made without lawful authority and is of no legal effect and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper.

2. The short facts leading to the disposal of the Rules as under –

The petitioners are law abiding permanent citizen of Bangladesh. The addresses of the petitioners are correct address for the purpose of service of notice or notices upon them. The Respondent No.1 is the Appellate Tribunal, অর্পিত সম্পত্তি প্রত্যার্পণ আপীল ট্রাইব্যুনাল, and District Judge, Sirajgonj and that the Respondent No. 2 is the Government of Bangladesh represented by its Deputy Commissioner, Sirajgonj, Collectorate Building, Sirajgonj, respondent No. 3 is the Additional Tribunal No.1, Arpito Sompotti Prottarpon, Sirajgonj and that the addresses of the respondents as mentioned in the cause title are correct addresses for the purpose of service of notice and process of the Court upon them.

The petitioners, challenging the legality of the Judgment and decree dated 20.05.2014 (decree signed on 26.05.2014) passed by the Appellate Tribunal and Court of District Judge, Sirajgonj in অর্পিত সম্পত্তি প্রত্যার্পণ আপীল মামলা নং-০৫/২০১৪ reversing those judgment and decree dated 08.09.2013 (decree signed on 15.09.2013) passed by the learned Judge, অর্পিত সম্পত্তি প্রত্যার্পণ অতিরিক্ত ট্রাইব্যুনাল-১, সিরাজগঞ্জ in অর্পিত সম্পত্তি প্রত্যার্পণ আপীল মামলা নং-৭৩৪/২০১২ whereby the application filed by the petitioners were allowed.

The petitioners filed an application as per provision of Section 9 of the অর্পিত সম্পত্তি প্রত্যার্পণ আইন-২০০১ (As amended) before the  অর্পিত সম্পত্তি প্রত্যার্পণ অতিরিক্ত ট্রাইব্যুনাল, and the Tribunal entry the application being No. অর্পিত সম্পত্তি প্রত্যার্পণ মামলা নং- ৭৩৪/২০১২. In the said application, applicant sought a decree for "নালিশী (ক) তপশিল ভূমি যাহা গত ০৩-০৪-২০১২ইং তারিখে বাংলাদেশ গেজেট অতিরিক্ত সংখ্যায় (ক) তপসিল তালিকায় ১১৩, ১৩৩ ও ১৩৪নং ক্রমিকে ভি, পি মিসকেস যথাক্রমে ৭/উল্লা/৬৫-৬৬, ১৪/উল্লা/৭৩, ২৫/উল্লা/৭৯-৮০, ৩৭/উল্লা/৬৭-৬৮, ৯১/উল্লা/৭৯-৮০, ১৮১ ও ১৮২/উল্লা/৬৬-৬৭, ১৭৯/উল্লা/৬৬-৬৭, ১৮৫/উল্লা/৬৬-৬৭, ১৯০/উল্লা/৬৬-৬৭, ১৯৫/উল্লা/৬৬-৬৭, ১৯৬/উল্লা/৬৬-৬৭, ১৯৭/উল্লা/৬৬-৬৭, ২১০/উল্লা/৬৬-৬৭, ২১১/উল্লা/৬৬-৬৭, ২১২/উল্লা/৬৬-৬৭, ২১৩/উল্লা/৬৬-৬৭, ২১৪/উল্লা/৬৬-৬৭, মূলে প্রকাশ করা হয়েছে, উহা অর্পিত সম্পত্তি প্রত্যর্পন আইন, ২০০১ (সংশোধিত ২০১১) এর ৯ ধারা বিধান মোতাবেক প্রত্যর্পনযোগ্য হেতু (ক) তপশিল সম্পত্তির তালিকা হইতে অবমুক্ত মর্মে ঘোষনা” in respect of 57.96 acres of land described in the application and alleging inter alia that the case property originally belongs to Sree Chittaranjan Sarker, Sree Nobo Kumer Sarker and Sree Ronjit Kumer Sarker and during the S.A Survey S.A. Khatian rightly published in their name and thereafter Sree Chittaranjan Sarker died leaving two sons namely Sree Asit Kumar Sarker and Sree Manik Lal Sarker and then Sree Nobo Kumer Sarker and. Sree Ronjit Kumar Sarker died on issueless in this country and they have been owning and possessing the scheduled property by way of Successor in interest in respect of 46.12 acres and Co-sharer in possession by lease in respect of 11.84 acres and then the petitioners came to know that the Nobo Kumar and Ronojit share's i.e. 2/3 declared as enemy property and for which the petitioners as plaintiffs filed partition suit being Title Suit No. 90 of 1986 in the Court of Sub-ordinate Judge, Sirajgonj impleading respondent No. 2 (herein) Deputy Custodian, vested and non-residence (land & building) property and other 28 persons as defendants, wherein Government of Bangladesh i.e. Deputy Custodian, vested and non-residence (land & building) property contested the suit by filing written statement. And then on consideration of the evidence on record and documents and also witnesses of the contesting parties, the learned Sub-ordinate Judge decreed the suit in favour of the plaintiff petitioners and accordingly the plaintiff petitioners got 12.60 acres of land by saham by judgment and decree dated 29.03.1990. More so, government did not preferred any appeal against the said judgment and decree dated 29.03.1990. And that on publication Gazette Notification dated 03.04.2012 as per provision of Section 9 of অর্পিত সম্পত্তি প্রত্যার্পণ আইন-২০০১, including the schedule land described in the application as 'Ka' schedule and for which the petitioners filed the application sought for a decree to declared that the schedule land is liable to be Prottarpon in favour to the petitioners.

3. The respondent No.2 as opposite party contested the case by filing written objection and denied the material allegation made in the case and further stated that the petitioners who tiled the case are not the heirs of the original owner and the application is liable to be dismissed.

4. The learned Judge of অর্পিত সম্পত্তি প্রত্যার্পণ ট্রাইব্যুনাল, সিরাজগঞ্জ below on considering the pleadings made in the case and in the written objection and assessed and evaluated witnesses and documents, exhibits etc. on record bad rightly held that, "দরখাস্তকারীগণ কর্তৃক সিরাজগঞ্জ সাব-জজ আদালতে বাটোয়ারা ৯০/৮৬ দায়ের করে ২১/৩/৯০ ইং তারিখে ডিক্রী পায় এবং সরকার উক্ত মামলায় বিবাদী ছিল। যেক্ষেত্রে কোন বিষয় সম্পত্তি সংক্রান্ত বিরোধ আদালতের সিদ্ধান্তে নিস্পত্তি হয়েছে সেক্ষেত্রে অনুরূপ সম্পত্তি সংক্রান্তে অর্পিত সম্পত্তি প্রত্যর্পন আইনে প্রত্যর্পন সম্পত্তি হিসাবে উক্ত আইনে ৬(ক)ধারায় গেজেট প্রকাশ বারিত করা হয়েছে।” and further held that; “অধিকন্তু তিনি তাঁর দাবীর সমর্থনে দরখাস্তকারীপক্ষ ভোটার তালিকা এবং মৃত্যু সনদপত্র এর কপি দাখিল করেছেন। যেখানে সুস্পষ্টভাবে প্রমাণিত হয় যে, এস.এ প্রজাগণের ক্রমওয়ারিশগণ এখনও বাংলাদেশে বসবাস করছেন।” and allowed the application in part vide judgment and decree dated 08.09.2013 (decree signed on 15.09.2013).

5. The provision of Section 21 of the অর্পিত সম্পত্তি প্রত্যর্পণ আইন, ২০০১ which reads as follows:

“২১।আপীল ট্রাইব্যুনালের রায়ের বিরুদ্ধে সুপ্রীম কোর্টের আপীল বিভাগে আপীল।–(১) আপীল ট্রাইব্যুনালের রায়ের বিরুদ্ধে শুধুমাত্র সুনির্দিষ্ট আইনগত প্রশ্নে, সুপ্রীমকোর্টের আপীল বিভাগে অনুমতি নিয়া উক্ত বিভাগে আপীল করা যাইবে।

(২)-------”

6. On 01.07.2012, the petitioners preferred an application as per provision of Section 9 of the অর্পিত সম্পত্তি প্রত্যর্পণ আইন, ২০০১ (As amended) before the অর্পিত সম্পত্তি প্রত্যর্পণ ট্রাইব্যুনাল, সিরাজগঞ্জ and the Tribunal entry the application being No. অর্পিত সম্পত্তি প্রত্যর্পণ মামলা নং-৭৩৪/২০১২ and the অর্পিত সম্পত্তি প্রত্যর্পণ ট্রাইব্যুনাল, সিরাজগঞ্জ allowed the case vide judgment and decree dated 08.09.2013 and being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and decree dated 08.09.2013 passed by অর্পিত সম্পত্তি প্রত্যর্পণ অতিরিক্ত ট্রাইব্যুনাল-১, সিরাজগঞ্জ in অর্পিত সম্পত্তি প্রত্যর্পন মামলা নং-৭৩৪/২০১২, respondent No.2 preferred appeal being  অর্পিত সম্পত্তি প্রত্যর্পন আপীল মামলা নং-০৫/২০১৪ and the learned Judge of the অর্পিত সম্পত্তি প্রত্যর্পন আপীল ট্রাই���্যুনাল allowed the appeal vide judgment and decree dated 20.05.2014 and being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and decree dated 20.05.2014 passed in অর্পিত সম্পত্তি প্রত্যর্পন আপীল মামলা নং-০৫/২০১৪, the petitioners preferred Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No.1699 of 2014 under provision of Section 21 of the অর্পিত সম্পত্তি প্রত্যর্পন আইন, ২০০১ before the Appellate Division, Supreme Court of Bangladesh and obtained an order of status quo in respect of possession of the suit land vide order dated 13.07.2014 passed by the learned Judge in Chamber of the Appellate Division and thereafter respondent No.2 filed an application for vacating the order of status quo on the ground that the provision of Section 21(1) of the অর্পিত সম্পত্তি প্রত্যর্পন আইন, ২০০১ has been repealed on 03.05.2013 vide Act No.20 of  2013 dated 05.03.2013 and a new provision of Section 22(3) has been inserted and as per the said amended provision the judgment and decree of the Appellate Tribunal, অর্পিত সম্পত্তি প্রত্যর্পন আপীল ট্রাইব্যুনাল is final and after hearing the parties the said Leave Petition is dismissed being not maintainable vide order dated 10.05.2015.

7. The provisions of Section 2(ড) of the অর্পিত সম্পত্তি প্রত্যর্পণ আইন, ২০০১ which is read as follows:

“২(ড). ‘মালিক’ অর্থ যে ব্যক্তির সম্পত্তি অর্পিত সম্পত্তি হিসাবে তালিকাভূক্ত হইয়াছে সেই মূল মালিক বা তাহার উত্তরাধিকারী, বা উক্ত মূল মালিক বা উত্তরাধিকারীর স্বার্থাধিকারী  (Successor in interest),  বা তাহাদের অনুপস্থিতিতে তাহাদের উত্তরাধিকার সূত্রে এমন সহ-অংশীদার যিনি বা যাহারা ইজারা গ্রহণ দ্বারা বা অন্য কোনভাবে সম্পত্তির দখলে রহিয়াছেন (co-sharer in possession by lease or in any form)  যদি উক্ত মূল মালিক বা উত্তরাধিকারী বা স্বার্থাধারী (Successor in interest)  বা উত্তরাধিকার সূত্রে সহ-অংশীদার (Co-sharer in possession by lease or in any form)  বাংলাদেশের নাগরিক ও স্থায়ী বাসিন্দা হন;”

8. The case land was rightly recorded and published in C.S. and S.A. Khatian in the name of predecessor of the petitioners and it was never included as Enemy Property and the case land was not included in the Census List. More so, on 27.03.1974 repealed the Vested Law. On 31.07.1984 the then President of Bangladesh in conference of the Hindu Community was pleased enough to declare that on and that date declaration or leasing out any further land as Enemy or Vested Property would stand stopped. Following the declaration Memo No. CST72(2)/84-81(7) dated 06.08.1984 a circular was issued to that effect from the office of the President's Secretariate. Since then there was neither any scope for the subordinate Government officials to bring any new land under the clutches of Vested Property. After came to know that the respondent No.2 tried to leased out the suit property to some unknown person and leased out some portion and then the petitioners compelled to institute Title Suit being No.90 of 1986 in the Court of Sub-ordinate Judge, Sirajgonj for partition of their share impleading respondent No.2 as defendant No.1 and on contest the suit was decree vide judgment and decree dated 21.03.1990.

9. Unless the operation of the impugned judgment and decree dated 20.05.2014 so far it relates to the case property is stayed and respondents are restrained by an order of injunction from interfering with the peaceful possession of the petitioners in the case property and/or dealing with the same in any manner whatsoever pending hearing of this writ petition, the petitioners will suffer irreparable loss and injury.

10. The learned Advocate for the petitioner further submits that the Appellate Tribunal, অর্পিত সম্পত্তি প্রত্যর্পণ আপীল ট্রাইব্যুনাল and Court of District Judge without applying mind regarding the provision of Section 6(Ka) of the অর্পিত সম্পত্তি প্রত্যর্পন আইন, ২০০১ which resulted in an error of law and facts more so learned Court of District Judge failed to consider the provision of Section 2(ড) of the অর্পিত সম্পত্তি প্রত্যর্পন আইন, ২০০১ and found to be the products of misreading and non-reading of the materials evidence and misconstruction of the important document, a case of interference is made out and as such non consideration of the evidence on record aspect of the case rendered the impugned judgment and decree as wholly illegal and bad in law and as such impugned judgment and decree dated 20.05.2014 passed by the learned Appellate Tribunal, অর্পিত সম্পত্তি প্রত্যর্পণ আপীল ট্রাইব্যুনাল below without any lawful authority and is of no legal effect.

11. Mr. S.N. Goswami with Ms. Afsana Begum, Advocates appearing on behalf of the petitioners while no one appears on behalf of the respondents.

12. Ms. Afsana Begum, the learned Advocate for the petitioners submits that the learned Appellate Tribunal, অর্পিত সম্পত্তি প্রত্যর্পণ আপীল ট্রাইব্যুনাল and Court of District Judge without assessed and evaluated the evidence on record, more so, did not advert the reasoning of the Judge  of অর্পিত সম্পত্তি প্রত্যর্পণ আপীল ট্রাইব্যুনাল-১, সিরাজগঞ্জ and also did not discussed the material evidences which were considered by the learned Judge of the অর্পিত সম্পত্তি প্রত্যর্পণ আপীল ট্রাইব্যুনাল-১, সিরাজগঞ্জ and the impugned judgment and decree 20.05.2014 (decree signed on 26.05.2014) are based on total misconception of law and contrary to the evidence brought on  record in the case and as such impugned judgment and decree dated 20.05.2014 passed by the learned Appellate Tribunal, অর্পিত সম্পত্তি প্রত্যর্পণ আপীল ট্রাইব্যুনাল below without any lawful authority and is of no legal effect.

13. The learned Advocate for the petitioners further submits that the learned Appellate Tribunal, অর্পিত সম্পত্তি প্রত্যর্পণ আপীল ট্রাইব্যুনাল and the Court of District Judge without  applying mind regarding the provision of Section 6(Ka) of the অর্পিত সম্পত্তি প্রত্যর্পণ আইন, ২০০১ which resulted in an error of law and facts more so learned Court of District Judge failed to consider the provision of Section 2(ড) of the অর্পিত সম্পত্তি প্রত্যর্পণ আইন, ২০০১ and found to he the products of misreading and non reading of the materials evidence and misconstruction of the important documents, a case of interference is made out and as such non consideration of the evidences on record aspect of the case rendered the impugned judgment and decree as wholly illegal and bad in law and as such the judgment and decree 20.05.2014 passed by the learned Appellate Tribunal, অর্পিত সম্পত্তি প্রত্যর্পণ আপীল ট্রাইব্যুনাল below without any lawful authority and is of no legal effect.

14. The learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners also submits that the decisions of the learned Judge, অর্পিত সম্পত্তি প্রত্যর্পণ অতিরিক্ত ট্রাইব্যুনাল-১, সিরাজগঞ্জ below, being based on facts and circumstances and evidence on record and there being findings over the points in issues and there being found no error of law or fact in passing the judgment and the impugned judgment and decree dated 20.05.2014 is not a proper judgment of reversal and as such fell into an error of law occasioning a failure of justice calling for interference by this Hon'ble Court and as such impugned judgment and decree dated 20.05.2014 passed by the learned Appellate Tribunal, অর্পিত সম্পত্তি প্রত্যর্পণ আপীল ট্রাইব্যুনাল below without any lawful authority and is of no legal effect.

15. The learned Advocate for the petitioners also submits that the facts and circumstances of the case the impugned judgment and decree are unsustainable in law and more for the reason that those suffers from non application of judicial mind and as such impugned judgment and decree dated 20.05.2014 passed by the learned Appellate Tribunal, অর্পিত সম্পত্তি প্রত্যর্পণ আপীল ট্রাইব্যুনাল below without any lawful authority and is of no legal effect.

16. The learned Advocate for the petitioner next submits of the learned Judge of  অর্পিত সম্পত্তি প্রত্যর্পণ আপীল ট্রাইব্যুনাল, সিরাজগঞ্জ below on considering the pleadings and evidences made in the case and in the written objection and assessed and evaluated witnesses and documents, exhibits etc. on record had rightly held that, “দরখাস্তকারীগণ কর্তৃক সিরাজগঞ্জ সাব-জজ আদালতে বাটোয়ারা ৯০/৮৬ দায়ের করে ২১/৩/৯০ ইং তারিখে ডিক্রী পায় এবং সরকার উক্ত মামলায় বিবাদী ছিল। যেক্ষেত্রে কোন বিষয় সম্পত্তি সংক্রান্ত বিরোধ আদালতের সিদ্ধান্তে নিস্পত্তি হয়েছে সেক্ষেত্রে অনুরুপ সম্পত্তি সংক্রান্তে অর্পিত সম্পত্তি প্রত্যর্পন আইনে প্রত্যর্পন সম্পত্তি হিসাবে উক্ত আইনে ৬(ক) ধারায় গেজেট প্রকাশ বারিত করা হয়েছে।--- অধিকন্ত তিনি তার দাবীর সমর্থনে দরখাস্তকারীপক্ষ ভোটার তালিকা এবং মৃত্যু সনদপত্র এর কপি দাখিল করেছেন। যেখানে সুষ্পষ্টভাবে প্রমাণিত হয় যে, এস.এ. প্রজাগণের ক্রুমওয়ারিশগণ এখনও বাংলাদেশে বসবাস করছেন।” and allowed the application vide judgment and decree dated 08.09.2013 but the learned Court of District Judge without advert the reasoning of the Judge of অর্পিত সম্পত্তি প্রত্যর্পণ অতিরিক্ত ট্রাইব্যুনাল-১ passed the impugned judgment and decree dated 20.05.2014 in অর্পিত সম্পত্তি প্রত্যর্পণ আপীল মামলা নং-০৫/২০১৪ and these hit the root of the merit of the case and as such impugned judgment and decree dated 20.05.2014 passed by the learned Appellate Tribunal, অর্পিত সম্পত্তি প্রত্যর্পণ আপীল ট্রাইব্যুনাল below without any lawful authority and is of no legal effect.

17. The learned Advocate for the petitioner lastly submits that in view of the provision of Section 6(Ka) of Act No.16 of 2001 together with the judgment and decree dated 21.03.1990 passed in Title Suit No.90 of 1986 the impugned judgment and decree passed by the learned Appellate Tribunal, অর্পিত সম্পত্তি প্রত্যর্পণ আপীল ট্রাইব্যুনাল is not only patently illegal but also malafide, arbitrarily, contemptuous and high handedness of respondents in total disregard for law and judiciary and to the utter prejudice of a citizen's fundamental and valuable right and as such impugned judgment and decree dated 20.05.2014 passed by the learned Appellate Tribunal, অর্পিত সম্পত্তি প্রত্যর্পণ আপীল ট্রাইব্যুনাল below without any lawful authority and is of no legal effect.

18. The learned Advocate for the petitioners has referred the Section 6(Ka) of the অর্পিত সম্পত্তি প্রত্যর্পণ আইন, ২০০১ in support of her contention and also referred the case of Ratan Bikash Mahajan & others Vs. Kanchan Das & others reported in 16 BLT (HCD) Page-217.

19. We have perused the writ petition, the annexures filed thereto, heard the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners, considered the submissions as advanced by the learned Advocate in support of the writ petition in order to arrive in proper finding it is very much pertinent to refer the provision of law as contained in Section 6(Ka) of the অর্পিত সম্পত্তি প্রত্যর্পণ আইন, ২০০১ where stated that:

“(ক) কোন সম্পত্তি অর্পিত নহে মর্মে এই আইন প্রবর্তনের পূর্বে যথাযথ আদালত চূড়ান্ত সিদ্ধান্ত প্রদান করিয়া থাকিলে সেই সম্পত্তি”

<u>20. We find after issuance of the rule in the instant writ petition issued usual notices upon the respondents did neither file any power in order to contest the rule nor any affidavit-in-opposition to controvert the statement as made in the writ petition on perusal of the impugned judgment and decree passed by the learned Appellate Tribunal, we find the Appellate Tribunal and the Court of District Judge without considering and evaluating the evidence on record and without adverting the reasoning of the Judge of অর্পিত সম্পত্তি প্রত্যর্পণ অতিরিক্ত ট্রাইব্যুনাল-১, সিরাজগঞ্জ and also did not discuss the material evidences which were duly considered by the learned Judge of the অর্পিত সম্পত্তি প্রত্যর্পণ অতিরিক্ত ট্রাইব্যুনাল-১, সিরাজগঞ্জ passed the  impugned judgment and decree dated 20.05.2014 which is perfunctory manner and in utter violation of the mandatory provisions of law as contain in 6(Ka) of the অর্পিত সম্পত্তি প্রত্যর্পণ আইন, ২০০১.</u>

<u>21. We also find that the learned Appellate Tribunal and the Court of District Judge without applying his mind as regard the provision of Section 6(Ka) of the ���র্পিত সম্পত্তি প্রত্যর্পণ আইন, ২০০১ which resulting in an error of law and facts more so learned Court of District Judge failed to consider the provision of Section 2(ড) of the অর্পিত সম্পত্তি প্রত্যর্পণ আইন, ২০০১ and found to be the products of misreading and non reading of the materials evidences and misconstruction of the important document, a case of</u>

<u>interference is made out and as such non consideration of the evidences on record aspect of the case rendered the impugned judgment and decree as wholly illegal and bad in law and as such the impugned judgment and decree dated 20.05.2014 passed by the learned Appellate Tribunal, অর্পিত সম্পত্তি প্রত্যর্পণ আপীল ট্রাইব্যুনাল below without any lawful authority and is of no legal effect.</u>

22. We further find that the learned Judge, অর্পিত সম্পত্তি প্রত্যর্পণ অতিরিক্ত ট্রাইব্যুনাল-১, সিরাজগঞ্জ below, being based on facts and circumstances and evidence on record and there being findings over the points in issues and there being found no error of law or fact in passing the judgment by the Tribunal as such the impugned judgment and decree dated 20.05.2014 is not a proper judgment of reversal and as such fell into an error of law occasioning failure of justice calling for interference by this Hon'ble Court and as such impugned judgment and decree dated 20.05.2014 passed by the learned Appellate Tribunal অর্পিত সম্পত্তি প্রত্যর্পণ আপীল ট্রাইব্যুনাল below without any lawful authority and is of no legal effect.

23. We further find that in view of the provision of Section 6(Ka) of the Act No.16 of 2001 together with the judgment and decree dated 21.03.1990 passed in Title Suit No.90 of 1986 the impugned judgment and decree passed by the learned Appellate Tribunal অর্পিত সম্পত্তি প্রত্যর্পণ আপীল ট্রাইব্যুনাল is not only patently illegal but also malafide, arbitrarily, contemptuous and high handedness of respondents in total disregard for law and judiciary and to the utter prejudice of a citizen's fundamental and valuable right and as such impugned judgment and decree dated 20.05.2014  passed by the learned Appellate Tribunal অর্পিত সম্পত্তি প্রত্যর্পণ আপীল ট্রাইব্যুনাল below without any lawful authority and is of no legal effect.

24. In the case of Ratan Bikash Mahajan & others Vs. Kanchan Das & others reported in 16 BLT (HCD) Page-217 where a single Judge of this Hon'ble Court held that;

"It may be mentioned here that the notice of this rule was served on the opposite parties 1-4 as appears from the office note dated 22.04.2001 and the office note dated 02.4.03 shows that a learned Advocate entered appearance on behalf of all the opposite party Nos.1-6. The learned Advocate for the opposite parties has filed a counter affidavit today during hearing of the case upon serving the copy thereof at 1.25 p.m. on the learned Advocate for the petitioners Mr. Rabi Shankar Chakraborty and filed the same before the Court 2.00 p.m. This being the position I have refused to consider the counter-affidavit during hearing of the rule and I have not read the counter affidavit as it was not filed in proper time."

The citation as referred by the learned Advocate in support of her contention is fully applicable in the facts and circumstances of the present case.

25. In view of the above facts and circumstances of the case and the submissions as advanced by the learned Advocate for the petitioner, we find merit and substance in the rule.

26. In the result the rule is made absolute without any order as to cost.

27. The order of status-quo granted at the time of issuance of the rule is hereby recalled and vacated.

28. The impugned judgment and decree dated 20.05.2014 passed by the learned Judge, Appellate Tribunal, অর্পিত সম্পত্তি প্রত্যর্পণ আপীল ট্রাইব্যুনাল, Sirajgong in অর্পিত সম্পত্তি প্রত্যর্পণ আপীল মামলা নং-০৫/২০১৪ is hereby set aside and the judgment and decree dated 08.09.2013 passed by the learned Judge, অর্পিত সম্পত্তি প্রত্যর্পণ মামলা নং-৭৩৪/২০১২ is hereby restored.

29. Communicate this judgment at once.

End.
