160. During hearing, the petitioners filed an application for issuance of Supplementary/ Additional Rule praying for direction upon the Jana Nirapatta Bighnakari Aparadh Daman Tribunal, Chittagong, to refrain him from proceeding against the petitioners in Jana Nirapatta Case No. 82 of 2001 and to quash the said proceeding as it relates to the petitioners.

161. Writ Petition No. 4430 of 2000 being filed by Mr Afzalul Abedin and 14 others, petitioners Versus Bangladesh, represented by the Secretary, Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliament Affairs and others, respondents. The petitioners' case, in short, is that on 17th July, 2000 they were arrested by police of Kotwali police station in connection with GDE No. 985, dated 18-7-2000 under section 54 of the Code of Criminal Procedure on the false allegation that they have thrown stones, cocktails, etc. at the procession of Bangladesh Chhatra League at Dinajpur town.

162. On 18th July, 2000, the petitioners were produced before the learned Magistrate, 1st Class, Court No. 2, Dinajpur whereupon they have been sent to the jail.

163. On 21st July, 2000 Syed Sohel Hossain, respondent No. 6, lodged first information report with the Kotwali police station making false allegations against the petitioners and others alleging that they have attacked a procession of Chhatra League with various weapons as a result of which a number of persons were injured. On such first information report Kotwali police started a criminal case against the petitioners and others under sections 10 and 12 of the Act.

164. In this writ petition grounds have been taken that the bill was passed as money bill by the Parliament though, in fact it, is not a money bill. The recommendation of the President was obtained on the bill as a bill which involved expenditure from public money. The bill was introduced in the Parliament on 27th January, 2000, by the Home Minister which was a private members' day and the same was passed and the bill was sent to the Parliamentary Standing Committee of the Ministry of Home Affairs. The standing committee prepared its report on Friday, the 28th January, 2000, a public holiday, with a note of dissent from two opposition MPs. The report was placed before the Parliament on 29th January, 2000 and the bill was passed by the Parliament on Sunday, 30th January, 2000.

165. Upon passing of the bill by the Parliament the Speaker certified the bill to be a money bill under Article 80(3) and sent it to the President on 31st January, 2000 for his assent under Article 80 of the Constitution.

On 14th February, 2000 President gave his assent to the bill and on the same day the Act was published in the official Gazette.

Thereafter on 10-3-2000 certain amendments were made including amendment of section 16 of the Act.

No sooner had the bill been passed as a money bill then a country-wide heated debate started as to how a bill which on the face of it deals with criminal offences could be termed as a money bill.

166. While the bill was pending before the President for his assent under Article 80(3) of the Constitution, the leader of the opposition in Parliament including all the parties of the country excepting the party in power, professional groups urged upon the President not to give assent to the bill. Senior most constitutional lawyers of the country including the then President of the Supreme Court Bar Association in a memorandum submitted to the President expressed their concern that bill was not a money bill and the President should refer the matter under section 106 of the Constitution to the Appellate Division of the Supreme Court for advisory opinion as the bill involves a question of law which is of such a nature and such public importance that it is expedient to obtain the opinion of the Supreme Court. There were remarks from various corners, published in newspapers, the Speaker stated that the bill was a money bill and he had given certificate accordingly. And the Home Minister expressed his surprise that a bill presented to the President for his recommendation; he could not have recommended it without studying it.

167. In this Writ petition these points have been assailed by the learned Counsel Mr Abdur Razzak. He has referred to some deliberation programmer of Prime Minister 'face to face with the people.' The Prime Minister categorically stated that the bill was presented to the President after the cabinet approved it. The President 'wrote that it was a money bill.' On the other hand President issued a press release and it was denied. It is further submitted that while President's recommendation was obtained on the bill as it involved expenditure from the public exchequer, by practicing fraud on the Constitution, the bill was introduced into Parliament as a money bill. 217. Colourable Legislation: The doctrine of colourable legislation is one relating to the competence of Parliament. If the Parliament has competence to pass any bill, it is irrelevant whether they have passed it fraudulently or otherwise. 218. A thing is colourable which exists in appearance and not in reality. It is 'what is purpose to be. Colourability is linked up with incompetency, that is, an authority doing a thing which he got no power to do. Colourable is not tained with bad faith; it is just lack of jurisdiction. In other words, in the case of law-making, the doctrine of colourable legislation does not involve any question of bonafide on the part of the legislature. If the legislature is competent to pass a particular law, the motives which impelled it to act are really irrelevant. As stated in Coollys' Constitutional Limitations, 'whether a statute is constitutional or not is always a question of power'. Further Ref: KCG-Narayan Deo vs State of Orissa, AIR 1953 SC 379.

239. Non-Obstante Clause

I may quote the following passage from Bindra's Interpretation of Statutes, 7th edition page 1093 :

"The non-obstante clause must be given its natural and ordinary meaning. The word 'notwithstanding' must be given its full effect, and it is not a sound principle of interpretation to brush aside words in a statute as being in apposite or surplusage. The very purpose of non-obstante clause is that provisions shall prevail over any other provision and that other provision shall not be of any consequence. In case there is any inconsistency or departure between a non-obstante clause and other provisions, one of the objects of such a clause is to indicate that it is the non-obstante clause which would prevail over other clauses. Even by the dictionary sense, the expression 'notwithstanding' implies that other provisions shall not prevail over the main provision."

But the preamble and section 3 of the Act prescribed clear guidelines where there is overriding provisions like section 3 of the Act, There is no scope of pick and choose and question of overlapping does not arise at all. All the offences prescribed in the provisions of the Act shall be tried by the tribunal established under the Act.

271. We are bound by our own decisions. We have recently passed a decision in Writ Petition No. 10 of 2001 Monowara Begum vs Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka that the Narcotics Control Act, 1990 and Drug Control Ordinance, 1982 are subsequent special laws of that of the Special Powers Act, 1974, having no specific mention of heroin in its schedule. The special enactment of 1982 has not only created a forum but having exclusive jurisdiction, it contains overriding provision as well.

272. The short fact of the aforesaid writ petition is that the accused petitioner was convicted under section 25B(2) of the Special Powers Act, 1974 but this Division Bench held the conviction and sentence of the petitioner under section 25(B)(2) of Special Powers Act was coram non judice, since the offence was made triable by the court constituted under the Drug Control Ordinance, 1982.

273. MA Aziz J held: It is found that pursuant to section 23 of the Drug Control Ordinance, 1982 by Gazette Notification dated 26-4-1988 and 17-11-88 all Sessions Judges for their respective Sessions Divisions have been empowered as Drug Court to try offenders under Drug Control Ordinance, 1982 and Dangerous Drugs Act, 1930, as such, the Special Tribunal created under Special Powers Act, 1974 had no jurisdiction to try the petitioner. The proceeding before the Special Tribunal was therefore, without jurisdiction and a nullity.

274. This view of ours finds support from the pronouncement of this court in the case of Shahidullah and another vs State reported in 1992 BLD 533.

275. In this connection I want to refer a decision reported in 44 DLR (AD) 260, Managing Director, Rupali Bank Ltd and others vs Tofazzal Hossain and others: Judgment was delivered by his Lordship Mr Justice Shahabuddin Ahmed CJ: 'Relation between general and special law—availability of remedy—if any legal remedies erroneously available under both general law and special law, the remedy prescribed by the special law must be sought in exclusion of the one available under the general law.

276. The facts of the instant cases and facts of the reported case, referred above are different but the law points decided by the Appellate Division are identical to that of the present cases. It was held by the Appellate Division, in the aforesaid reported case. 'A Labour Law, such as the Employment of Labour (Standing Orders) Act, or the Industrial Relations Ordinance, is a special law vis-a-vis the Code of Civil Procedure which is a general law. The latter affects the community at large; all people of the state are governed by it. While the former relates to and affects particular persons or things; it operates upon a selected class, rather than the public generally. Relation between a general law and a special law is governed by the principle known as Generalia Specialibus non derogant which in English means, 'general words do not derogate from the special'.

277. The above decisions of the Appellate Division is binding upon us and the Act being the special law covering a certain class of people i.e. terrorists, hijackers, mastans, miscreants, hooligans, illegal toll collectors and anti-social elements, it will prevail over the Penal Code which covers the people as a whole of the country and, in view of the above circumstances, we can safely conclude that there is no overlapping provision in the Act. Some definition of offences of Penal Code and the Act may be common but since the Act is a special and later law having overriding clause, offences coming under any definition of offences covered by the Act are absolutely triable by the Tribunal constituted under the Act not by any ordinary criminal Court.

278. Police may wrongly record first information report under the provisions of both the laws but trial begins from the date of framing charge. For the mistake or ignorance of the police, the law cannot be struck down.

279. It has been observed in many reported cases that for misuse or abuse of law by the law enforcing authorities, law itself cannot be declared ultra vires.

280. The Indian Supreme Court held in a case reported in AIR 1962 SC 361 that the possibility of abuse of a statute otherwise valid does not impart to it any aliment of invalidity. The constitutional validity of the statute would have to be determined on the basis of its provisions and on the ambit of its operation as reasonably construed. If so judged it passed the test of reasonableness, possibility of powers conferred being improperly used is no ground for pronouncing the law itself invalid (discussed earlier).

281. Having respect to all concerned I want to add that law enforcing authority of our country, mainly the police, has played the very painful role in exercising their powers and it cannot be denied that they became the party to crime. In these circumstances check and balance must be maintained to save the country as a whole and protect the people from the hands of the terrorists, criminals and also from undue harassment by the police in the name of exercise of their powers.

282. Without any hesitation I must hold that the law enforcing agencies, specially the police, must do their best to bring back confidence upon them. It is ill luck for our nation that police are placed to face trial for committing heinous criminal offences i.e. murder, rape, dacoity, looting, etc. This is a shame to the whole police community department.

283. In view of the discussion made above and foregoing reasons I hold that section 16(1), (2) and 18(Kha) of the Act are inconsistent with the provisions of the Constitution and, in the result, the aforesaid sections of the Act are struck down.

284. In my opinion, the provisions of the Act do not attract the case under challenge in Writ Petition No. 192 of 2001 Mr Nazmul Huda and others vs Government of Bangladesh and Writ Petition No. 188 of 2001 Mr Monjur Morshed vs Government of Bangladesh (arising out of the same first information report i.e. Ramna PS Case No. 38(1) 2001, dated 15-1-2001, corresponding to Jana Nirapatta Case No. 65 of 2001) as such, Public Safety Tribunal No. 1, Dhaka, constituted under the Act is not competent to try the aforesaid case and hereby directed to refrain from trying the case as mentioned above.

285. In the result, the Rules in respect of Writ Petition No. 192 of 2001 and Writ Petition No. 188 of 2001 are made absolute and the Rules in respect of other writ petitions fixed for hearing and posted in cause list dated 21-3-2001 are made absolute in part, and the order of stay and other ad-interim orders/directions in those writ petitions mentioned herein above are hereby rescinded.

High Court Division

(Special Original Jurisdiction)

Kazi AT Manowaruddin J

Afzalul Abedin and others ----- Petitioners

Vs.

Government of Bangladesh and others ----- Respondents

Judgment

Kazi AT Manowaruddin J: Upon a split decision by a Division Bench, the matter has been referred to by the learned Chief Justice for disposal by this Bench.

287. All these Rules have been taken up together for hearing and disposal.

288. Since Public Safety (Special Provision) Act, 2000 (Act VII of 2000) “জন নিরাপত্তা বিশেষ বিধান আইন, ২০০০,” which is under challenge in all the Rules, has in the meantime been repealed by “জন নিরাপত্তা (বিশেষ আইন) (রহিতকরন) আইন, ২০০২ (Act VI of 2002), I find all the above Rules have been in fructuous.

Accordingly, the Rules are disposed of as being in fructuous.

End.

parties:
SHAHIDA BEGUM AND OTHERS.
v.
SAMSUL HAQUE DEAD HIS LEGAL HEIRS 1(A) KORFULER NESSA AND OTHERS
full_judgment:
Khizir Ahmed Choudhury, J: In this revisional application rule has been issued calling upon the opposite party No.1 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and order dated 14.07.2011 passed by learned Joint District Judge, 3rd Court, Comilla in disallowing the Miscellaneous Appeal No.59 of 2010 affirming the judgment and order dated 13.7.2010 passed by learned Senior Assistant Judge, Chowddagram, Comilla in disallowing the Miscellaneous Case No.27 of 2007 should not be set aside and or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may deem fit and proper.

2. Opposite party Nos.1-4 as plaintiff instituted Title Suit No.135 of 2014 seeking partition impleading the present petitioners as defendant and the said suit was decreed ex-parte on 06.4.1998.

3. The present petitioners being defendant Nos. 2-5 filed Miscellaneous Case No.27 of 2007 under order 9 rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure contending that no notices were served upon them and the purported notice shown to have been served upon petitioner No.1 through one Ekramul Haque is concocted and collusive service and as such the petitioner No.1 had/ has no occasion to know about the filing of the suit and subsequent ex-parte decree. It is further averred that the witnesses as mentioned in the service of summons are also not the persons as shown in the purported notice.

4. Opposite party entered appearance and filed written objection contending that summons were duly served upon the defendant petitioners and they had full knowledge about the institution of the suit and subsequent passing ex-parte decree dated 13.7.2010. learned Assistant Judge disallowed the application against which Miscellaneous Appeal No. 59 of 2010 has been preferred before the District Judge, Comilla and the learned District Judge also by judgment and order dated 11.3.2013 dismissed the appeal against which the instant rule.

5. Mr. Md. Mubarak Hossain, learned advocate appearing for the petitioner submits that in the purported notice it is shown that Shahida Begum's brother son Ekramul Haque received the notice on her behalf but the said Ekramul Haque is in fact not the brother's son of petitioner No.1 Shahida Begum which has been substantiated by evidence of the petitioner but the Courts below failed to advert that vital aspect of the case and rejected the contention of the petitioner. It is further averred that the witnesses as shown in the purported service of notice by adducing evidence as plaintiffs witness also denied service of notice in their presence but the Courts also failed to advert that vital aspect and erroneously rejected the application.

6. Mr. Mubarak Hossain next submits that it is the plaintiff who is to prove that summons were served upon the defendants but in the instant case the plaintiff totally failed to prove service of summons upon the defendants but the Court below erroneously shifted the onus upon the defendant regarding service of summons which also caused failure of justice, he continued, proof of service of summons cannot be shifted to defendants but both the Courts below failed to consider that vital aspect of the case in spite of the fact that the plaintiff took no step to substantiate the claim of service of summons. Mr. Mubarak next submits that although against the decree appeal and revision were preferred but those proceedings were initiated by some other persons who are unrelated with the petitioner and his right to proceed with application under order 9 rule 13 cannot be hindered by initiation of proceeding by other defendants. Even if it is assumed that the appellate Court affirmed the judgment passed by the trial Court but since the petitioner defendant filed no appeal, he has right to initiate proceeding and if it is found that summons were not served upon the defendant as per law and if prove, the decree in question will he set aside in respect of the petitioner defendants claim and his right will not be hindered even if the decree is merged with the appellate Court's judgment and decree.

7. Mr. Mubarak Hossain referred the case of Abdur Rashid and another Vs. Abdul Batik and another reported in 35 DLR AD 162, Md. Wasiq Khan Vs. Md. Sabiq Khan and another reported in 31 DLR AD 51, Md. Eshaque Vs. Afzal Ahmed and others reported in 13 DLR 115, Wazed Ali Sander (Md) Vs. Md. Afsaruddin Sardar and others reported in I BLC AD 179 and Regent Ken International Ltd. Vs. Amanat Shah Ship Breaking Ltd. Reported in 57 DLR 234.

8. Per contra Mr. Abdul Quayum along with Mr. Ali Reja, advocates appeared for the opposite party. Mr. Abdul Quayum submits that summons upon the petitioner defendants has duly been served through Ekramul Haque who is the brother's son of the petitioner No.1 and the petitioner was all through aware about the filing of the suit and subsequent ex-parte decree. He further submits that some of the defendants preferred appeal against the impugned judgment and decree and the appellate Court also affirmed the judgment and decree of the Court of first instance and subsequent revisional application is also ended in discharging the rule and ultimately Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal has been preferred which was also dismissed and as such decree in question has been merged with the judgment and decree of the appellate Court and as such the Court of first instance has no jurisdiction to set aside the decree which has been merged with the decree of the appellate Court. He next contended that process server as O.P.W.2 affirmed his service of summons upon the defendant petitioner and the plaintiff opposite parties have discharged their responsibility regarding service of summons by producing the process server in question. In support of their contention learned advocate referred the case of Md. Wasiq Khan Vs. Md. Sabiq Khan and another reported in 31 DLR AD 51 and the case of Sajeda Khatoon Vs. Mostafa Khatoon and others reported in 28 DLR 221.

9. Learned Senior Assistant. Judge disallowed the miscellaneous case on the ground that summon has been served upon the petitioner-defendant. Ekramul Haque, the brother's son of petitioner No.1. received summon on her behalf and the contention of the petitioner-defendant that Ekramul Haque was not the brother son of Shahida Begum has not been substantiated. The appellate Court also affirmed the findings and reasonings of the Court of first instant holding that defendant No.1 is the full brother of Shahida Begum and non service of summons as alleged by the petitioner defendant has not been substantiated.

<u>10. Having gone through the judgment of the Courts below and other materials, it appears that specific contention of the petitioner was that summons was not served upon the petitioner No.1 and Ekramul Haque is not the brother's son of petitioner No.1 and as such purported service of summons upon Ekramul Haque on behalf of the petitioner No.1 is not service of summons in the eye of law. Further contention of the petitioner was that Abul Khair P.W.2 by giving evidence stated that he was not present at the purported service of summons. P.W.3 also stated that other 2 witnesses are not resident of village Vashanda and as such service of summons upon the petitioner is not valid service of summons. On the other hand O.P. W.2 who served the summons upon the petitioner No. 1 through his brother's son stated that he served summons upon the petitioner. The O. P.W.2 made declaration in his summons that summons was duly served upon the defendant which is presumption of due service and it has got evidentially value, although it is rebutable but such presumption is to be rebutted by cogent evidence. Another aspect of the case is that defendant No.1 who is the full brother of the petitioner has preferred appeal against the ex-parte judgment and decree, so, from that point also a presumption may be taken that since defendant No.1 and petitioner are full brother and sister there is no reason that the petitioner was not aware about the institution and disposal of the suit, appeal and other proceeding. So far onus regarding service of summons, initial onus rested upon the plaintiff so, that such summons was duly served upon the defendant, if the initial onus is discharged it is upon the defendant petitioner that summons was not duly served upon him but this particular case is rested on other vital aspects also. Admittedly the ex-parte decree has been challenged by filing appeal and the appellate Court also affirmed the judgment and decree of the trial Court, the revisional Court also affirmed discharged the rule by affirming the judgment and decree of the appellate Court and Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal has been dismissed. On perusal of the case of Sajeda Khatun Vs. Mostafa Khatun reported in 28 DLR 221 it appears that when an ex-parte decree passed by the trial Court is it merged in the decree of the appellate court, the formar has no jurisdiction to amend the ex-parte decree. In the case of Md. Wasiq Khan Vs. Md. Sabiq Khan and another reported in in 31 DLR AD 51. similar view has been reiterated in paragraph No.18 which is hereunder: "On a review of the decisions and the discussion on the question set out, the following propositions seem to be well settled: Where a defendant against whom an ex-parte decree is passed applies under Order 9, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure to set it aside and at the same time prefers an appeal from it, the Calcutta High Court has held that notwithstanding the pendency of appeal the original Court may proceed with the application.</u>

<u>Where the ex-parte decree has been confirmed or otherwise disposed of on appeal the Court which passed the ex-parte decree has no longer any power to entertain an application to set it aside, even though the application was made before the appeal was filed.</u>

<u>The same principle will hold good even if the appeal has been preferred by a party other than the defendant against whom the decree was passed ex-parte provided the decree was one and indivisible.</u>

<u>But it will not affect the case of the defendant against whom ex-parte decree was passed and whose claim was not subject matter of appeal although he might be made party as respondent in the appeal.</u>

11. In the case of Sajeda Khatoon Vs Mostafa Khatoon and others 28 DLR 221 it is held that,

"we are definitely of the view that after the merger of the trial Court's decree in the decree of the appellate Court the trial Court's decree case to exist for the purpose of a proceeding under Order 9 of the Code and as such there cannot be any exercise of the power under the said Order by the trial Court for setting aside such a decree which has already been superseded. In the instant case the entire decree of the trial Court was brought before the High Court in the First Appeal which was preferred to it and in which all the defendants were made parties and as such when the High Court dismissed the appeal and affirmed the decree of the trial Court, there is no room for doubt that the entire decree of the trial had merged in the decree of the Court of appeal made in F.A. No.33 of 1962"

12. Mr. Mubarak Hassan) also referred the case of Md. Wasiq Khan Vs Md. Sabiq Khan and others 31 DI,R AD 51 as referred by the opposite parties to show that mere pendency of the appeal will not be bar for filing case under order 9 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure but in the instant case not only appeal has been disposed of rather revisional application and civil petition for leave to appeal have also been disposed of and as such the preposition as advanced by Mr. Mubarak Hossain is not hold good.

13. In this respect the contention of Mr. Md. Mubarak Hossain that since the petitioner-defendant did not prefer appeal against the ex-parte decree the appellate Court decree is not bound upon him and if it is proved that summons was not served upon him, the ex-parte decree even can be set aside in respect of his share or claim in the suit. Such contention is not supportable as because ex-parte decree cannot be set aside in respect of particular portion of any subject matter of the suit, in that event there will arise multiplicity of suit and proceeding. The decision referred by Mr. Mubarak relying in the case of Regent Ken Vs Amanath Shah Ship Breaking 57 DLR 234 is regarding service of summons is not applicable to the present case because in the instant case the decree has been merged with the decree of the appellate Court. In 31 DLR AD 51 as referred by Mr. Mubarak. Hossain, the proposition has been discussed and settled conveniently as mentioned above. In the instant case it is found that judgment and decree of the Court of first instance has been challenged as a whole and the appellate Court affirmed the judgment and decree of the trial Court which signifies that the cause regarding entire suit land has been disposed of so, although the petitioner did not prefer appeal but as the entire cause has been disposed of by the appellate Court his claim regarding his purported share cannot be adjudicated as the appeal has been disposed by the appellate Court having affirmed by the highest Court of the Country.

14. However the petitioner is not remediless if he can prove that fraud and collusion has been perpetrated in obtaining judgment and decree and there is separate forum for ventilating grievances.

15. In the above context, the Courts below did not commit any error in disallowing the miscellaneous case and accordingly, the rule is discharged without any order as to cost.

16. The order of stay granted at the time of issuance of the rule is hereby re-called and vacated.

17. Send down the lower Courts records.

18. Communicate the order.

End.

parties:
AGRANI BANK LIMITED REPRESENTED BY ITS MANAGER, SHYAMNAGAR BRANCH, POLICE STATION-SHYAMNAGA2R, DISTRICT-SATKIHRA. 
Vs. 
THE JUDGE, ARTHA RIN ADALAT NO. 2, SATKHIRA AND ANOTHER.
full_judgment:
A.K.M. Zahirul Hoque, J. This Rule Nisi was issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the impugned order No. 70, dated 24.11.2014 passed by the respondent No. 1, learned Joint District Judge and Artha Rin Adalat No. 2, Satkhira in Artha Jail No. 07 of 2008 allowing the application to pay the principal loan amount with cost complying the BRDP circular No. 7, dated June, 2013 (Annexure-D) should not be declared to have been made without lawful authority and is of no legal effect and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper.

2. Facts, relevant for the purpose of disposal of the Rule, in short are as under: Upon application of the respondent No. 2 the petitioner Bank sanctioned credit facilities total amounting to Tk. 63,71,000/- only in favour of the respondent No. 2 vide its Sanction Letter No. (i) IDFD/H0/1 DA/ 152 dated 18.09.1986, (ii) শিউঋবি/ওয়েজ/২১৬, তারিখ-৩০/০৭/১৯৮৯, iii) শিউঋবি/ওয়েজ/২৭১, তারিখ-১৭/০২/১৯৯২, (iv) শিউঋবি/বাস্ত/ওয়েজ/১৯০৯, তারিখ-০৮/১২/১৯৯৪, The respondent No. 2 duly accepted all terms and conditions of the said sanction letter and availed and enjoyed the aforesaid credit facilities. As securities against the said credit facilities the respondent No. 2 executed all usual charge documents in favour of the petitioner Bank. Moreover, respondent No. 2 mortgaged his property in favour of the petitioner Bank by executing registered deed of mortgage as well as executed registered deed of power of attorney authorizing the petitioner Bank to sell the schedule property in case the respondent No. 2 borrower failed to repay outstanding dues of credit facilities within the time stipulated. Having availed the credit facilities the respondent No. 2 defaulted to liquidate the outstanding dues to the petitioner Bank when the stipulated time to repay the outstanding dues of the credit facilities expired as per the terms and conditions of the sanction letter.

The petitioner Bank on several times dispatched warning letters to the respondent No. 2 to adjust the outstanding dues of the credit facilities but they did not come forward to repay the same, as such a legal notice was served upon the respondent No. 2 claiming to repay the outstanding dues of the credit facilities whereby it was warned that in failure of repayment of the outstanding dues the petitioner bank shall take legal action against them and/or shall sell the mortgaged property to realize the outstanding dues but they completely failed to repay the outstanding dues of the credit facilities or pay any heed of the request of the petitioner bank.

To realize the outstanding dues the petitioner bank published auction notice to sell, the schedule property but failed to sell the same for want of proper bid amount covering the outstanding dues of the petitioner Bank.

Finding no other alternative the petitioner Bank filed Artha Rin Suit No. 4 of 2002 against the respondent No. 2 before the Artha Rin Adalat No. 2, Satkhira the respondent No. 1 for realization of the outstanding dues of the credit facilities and the Court was decreed the said on  17.02.2008 (decree signed on 24.02.2008) in favour of the petitioner Bank for an amount of Tk. 2,12,55,796/-

Thereafter, the petitioner filed the Artha Execution Case No. 07 of 2008 to execute the said judgment and decree to realize the decreetal amount of Tk. 2,12,55,796/-.

It is stated that after hearing of both the parties the learned Artha Rin Adalat No. 2 allowed the application of the respondent No. 2 to pay the principal loan amount with cost complying the BRPD circular No. 7, vide Order No. 70, dated 24.11.2014.

3. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the impugned order 24.11.2014 passed by the respondent No. 1, the petitioner preferred this application under Article 102 of the Constitution and obtained the present Rule.

4. The Rule was contested by respondent No. 2 by filing an affidavit-in-opposition denying all the material allegations and contending inter alia that after sanctioning the loan in favour of the respondent No. 2 though the M/S. Uttaron Ice and Cold Storage was started but due to natural disturbance, load shading and a long time law voltage of the electricity the said cold storage was already ruined off and ultimately it was closed in a position of a sick industry and then the said position of the said industry was informed to the Ministry of Industry and also higher authority of the Agrani Bank by this respondent No. 2 and thereafter the industry of this respondent was listed as sick industry after having an inquiry about this matter locally by the higher authority of the Ministry of Industry and also by the concerned Agrani Bank.

5. It is further stated that the Bangladesh Bank made a circular on 20th June, 2013 with respect of disposing the account of loan case of the said industries which have been listed as sick industries with certain procedure so as that in case of sick industries all the applied interest and unapplied interest will be exempted in disposing the loan case of such industries and in complying the said circular of Bangladesh Bank, the industrial credit division-2 Agrani Bank Ltd. Head Office, Dhaka also issued a circular on 20th August 2013.

6. It is further stated that in pursuance of the said two circulars the present respondent No. 2 filed an application before the Managing Director, Agrani Bank Ltd. Head Office, Dhaka on 10.07.2013 and subsequently this petitioner deposited 13,68,000 as down payment along with legal expense in connection with such application and the copy of the said application was also sent to the Governor, Bangladesh Bank; Managing Director, Agrani Bank, Head Office, Dhaka; Deputy General Manager, Khulna Circle, Agrani Bank, Khulna, Assistant General Manager, Regional Office, Agrani Bank, Satihira and Manager Agrani Bani, Shaymnagor Branch, Satkhira for excepting the all kinds of interest with respect of loan account of this respondent in respect of the Uttoron Ice and Cold Storage.

7. Thereafter, the Managing Director and Deputy General Manager called a report on 03.12.2013 from the Assistant General Manager, Agrani Bank Ltd. Satkhira and in complying the same the Assistant General Manager sent a report to its Head Office, but as Head Office of the Agrani Bank and DGM, Khulna Circle, Khulna were not satisfied by the said report and as such they again called a report with an opinion in detailed mainly the limit of the cost of fund and the moment of deposition of down payment and accordingly the Regional Officer, Agrani Bank, Satkhira sent a report on 22.10.2013 with a forwarding letter dated 26.12.2013 to its Head Office and also to the office of DGM, Agrani Bank, Khulna Circle, Khulna with an opinion for approval of payment of capital loan money of this respondent an amount of Tk. 43,47,727/75 and miscellaneous cost of Tk. 3,79,2436/0 with a period of one year exempting 100% applied interest and unapplied interest an amount of Tk. 1,52,70,431/95 and Tk. 3,02,67,153/-respectively. That the respondent No. 2 also filed a supplementary affidavit-in-opposition and stated that section 44(1) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 provides that the Artha Rin Adalat may for accurate and full trial of the suit and for ends of justice and to prevent the misuse of the judicial process, pass such ad-interim order as it may deem fit to pass. Section 44(2) of the said Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 provides that subject to the provisions of sub-section 3 no, ad-interim order passed by any Court under this Act shall be questioned in the form of an appeal or revision in any higher Court. The ad-interim order i. e. interlocutory order as used in section 44(2) of the said Ain refers to an order passed by the Adalat before pronouncement of the decree of an Artha Rin Suit and against the said order no appeal or revision is maintainable that means any party of the suit may challenge the said ad-interim order only by filling writ petition but when a decree was pronounced and any order was passed after the decree was drawn then the only remedy of the party of the Artha Rin Suit is to file appeal as per provision of the Code of Civil Procedure if he wants to challenge the said decree or order passed at the stage of post-decree. In that case no writ petition lies for challenging the said order and as such the impugned order of the instant writ petition was passed in Artha Rin Execution Case No. 07 of 2008 i. e. at the stage of post decree as because here the alternative remedy is efficacious and adequate for the decree holder bank to file appeal against the impugned order as per provision of the Code of Civil Procedure.

8. Mr. Md. Kamruzzaman, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner takes us into the application, annexures as appended by the parties including the impugned order and other materials-on-record and submits that he filed the Artha Rin Suit for realization of Tk. 2,12,55,796/- and got decree on contest in respect of said amount thereby he filed the decree execution case under Order 21 Rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure with an intention to realize the decree amount from the decree debtor respondent No. 2 but the learned Judge of the Artha Rin Adalat passed the impugned order on the application filed by the respondent No. 2 in pursuance of BRPD circular which is totally without jurisdiction in the part of the decree execution court. He further submits that the decree execution court cannot go beyond the decree which is totally contrary with the power and function as well as with the provision of section 50(1) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 and therefore the impugned order has been passed without lawful authority and is of no legal effect. He further submits that the respondent No. 2 contested the suit as principal defendant and decree was passed in his presence and against the said judgment and decree the respondent No. 2 did not file any appeal under the force of section 41 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 but in the decree execution case the defendant respondent No. 2 filed the application for implementation of the BRDP circular which was neither a part of the decree nor any part of the proceeding of the decree execution case and as such the application filed by the respondent No. 2 itself was not maintainable but the learned Judge of the Executing Court without considering these legal aspect has passed the impugned order which is totally illegal, malafide and liable to be declared without lawful authority and is of no legal effect. In support of his submissions the learned Advocate for the petitioner has referred a decision the case of Sheikh Sekander Ali and others Vs. Agrani Bank Limited and others, reported in 68 DLR (AD) 113, and the case of Janata Bank Vs. Mohiuddin Specialized Textile, reported 62 DLR 501 and the case of Elite Lamps Ltd. Vs. Secretary, Ministry of Industries and others, reported in 61 DLR 641.

9. Md. Ruhul Quddus Kajol, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of respondent No. 2 takes us into the contention of the affidavit-in-opposition and different annexures supplementary affidavit-in-opposition including the impugned order and submits that the impugned order is not an ad-interim/interlocutory order before pre-decree rather it is the final order of the Artha Rin Execution Case No. 07 of 2008 and as such the legality or illegality of the said order can be challenged by any party by filling an appeal as per provision of section 96, 104 and relevant rule of order 41 of the Code of Civil Procedure and therefore the writ petition filed by the petitioner under Article 102 of the Constitution is not maintainable. He further submits that the Executing Court under the force of sections 44(1) and 57 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 and considering the facts and circumstance along with. the materials on record being satisfied has passed the impugned order for ends of justice as a final order of the Executing Court and Therefore the writ petitioner would to file revision or appeal against the said order but the petitioner instead to file the appeal or revision has filed the instant writ petition which is not maintainable as such the Rule is liable to be discharged. In support of the submissions of the learned Advocate for the respondents No. 2 has referred same decisions in the case of Sonali Bank Limited Vs. Asha Tex International and others, reported in 20 BLC 185; the case of Jahangir Kabir Chowdhury Vs. Bangladesh Government, represented by the Secretary, Ministry of Law Justice and Parliamentary Affairs, Bangladesh and others, reported in 22 BLC (AD) 139 and the case of Golzar Hossain (Md.) Vs. Janata Bank, reported in 65 DLR (AD) 101.

10. Mr. Arobinda Kumar Roy (Ananda), the learned Deputy Attorney General appearing on behalf of the respondent No. 1 opposes the Rule and also adopted the submissions of the learned Advocate for respondent No. 2.

11. Heard the learned Advocates for both the sides, the learned Deputy Attorney General for the respondent No. 1, perused the application, affidavit-in-opposition annexures as appended therewith and other materials-on-record including the impugned order.

12. It appears from the record that the petitioner has been challenged the legality and property of the impugned order passed by the learned Judge of the Artha Rin Adalat dated 24.11.2014 in the execution case mainly on the ground by the petitioner that whether the Executing Court had the jurisdiction to entertain and allowed such application of the defendant No. 2 decree debtor in the proceeding of execution case under Order 21 Rule II of the Code of Civil Procedure to give exemption from the loan liabilities by modifying the decreetal amount.

13. Before considering this material aspect we would like to study what is meaning of Decree? It appears that the definitions of the Decree has been given in section 2(2) of the Code of Civil Procedure which runs as follows;

"(2) "decree" means the formal expression of an adjudication which, so far as regards the Court expressing it, " conclusively determines the rights of the parties with regard to all or any of the matters in controversy in the suit and may be either preliminary or final. It shall be deemed to include the rejection of a plaint and the determination of any question within section 144, but shall not include-

(a) any adjudication from which an appeal lies as an appeal from an order, or

(b) any order of dismissal 'for default."

14. So, it is admitted fact that the petitioner got the contested decree in a Artha Rin Suit against the defendant respondent No. 2 of the writ petition. It is also admitted that the decree debtor did not prefer any appeal against the said decree till date. Therefore, as per the definition of decree the expression of the Court was conclusive determination of the right of the parties of the Artha Rin Suit has been made in the decree by the Adalat in the concern Artha Rin Suit of the petitioner within the meaning of section 2(2) of the Code of Civil Procedure. Thereby in pursuance of the said decree the plaintiff as petitioner filed the Decree Execution Case No. 7 of 2008 under Order 21 Rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure before the respondent No. 1 to get the decreetal amount from the respondent No. 2.

15. We have gone through the Order XXI of the Code of Civil Procedure wherein the heading of the said Order categorically expressed to the effect that; "Execution of Decrees and orders"

16. But in the particular case though the appeal lies against the judgment and decree of Artha Rin Suit of the petitioner but the aggrieved party i. e. defendant respondent No. 2 did not prefer any appeal against the said judgment and decree of the Court of first instance. Therefore the Order 21 does not permit the executing Court to act on the decree to modify the decreetal amount neither in the name of BRPD circular nor any report or opinion of the concern authority in any manner. Thereby, the executing court has only the authority and empowered to execute the decree in pursuance of the decree of the Artha Rin Suit and to recovery the decreetal amount from the respondent No. 2 as decree debtor in accordance with the provisions of Order 21 Rules 11-23 along with other provisions of the Code of Civil Procedure.

17. On perusal of the application of the decree execution case filed by the decree holder petitioner before the learned Judge of the Executing Court which is Annexure-13 to the Writ Petition wherein the said application contained all the particulars as required under the said sub-rule 2 of Rule 11 of Order 21 of the Code of Civil Procedure and as such the decree holder petitioner duly filed the execution case in accordance with the law before the executing court wherein the petitioner decree holder mentioned the decreetal amount as of Tk. 2,13,81799/-

18. We have gone through the preamble of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 wherein the legislature has created the said law with an object for realization of loan money along with its interest from the borrower. The provision of order 21 relates for decree execution. The said provision spelt out that the object of the said order is only for the execution the decree as defined in section 2(2) of the Code of Civil Procedure by observing the different rules and procedure of relevant law.

19. We have gone through the impugned order wherein the operating portion of the said order is as under:

“উভয়পক্ষের আইনজীবী বক্তব্য বিবেচনায় নেয়া হল। সে সাথে অত্র মামলা সংশ্লিষ্ট মূল অর্থঋন মামলার রায়, অত্র ডিক্রি জারীর দরখাস্ত, বাংলাদেশ ব্যাংকের সংশ্লিষ্ট সার্কুলার, রুগ্ন শিল্প হিসাবে এ দেনাদারের প্রতিষ্ঠানের অন্তর্ভুক্তিরকরণ তালিকা, দ্যা ব্যাংক কোম্পানীজ এ্যাক্ট,১৯৯১ এর ৪৫ ধারা, অগ্রনী ব্যাংক আঞ্চলিক কার্যালয়, সাতক্ষীরা কর্তৃক প্রেরিত ২৭/১২/৯৩ তারিখের সুপারিশ পত্র, অর্থঋন আদালত আইন এর বিধানাবলী বিশেষ করে উক্ত আইনের ৫৭ ধারায় বর্ণিত বিধান আইনানুগভাবে বিচার বিশ্লেষন করে দেখা হল। অত্র মামলার ঘটনা সহ নথি ও পর্যালোচনা করা হল।

সবকিছু বিচার-বিবেচনা অন্তে অত্র আদালতের কাছে মনে হল-১নং দেনাদার পক্ষের আনীত অত্র দরখাস্তখানি ন্যায়নুগ যুক্তির আলোকে আইন সন্মতভাবেই বিবেচনার যোগ্য। তাই ন্যায় বিচারের স্বার্থেই উহা মঞ্জুর করার সিদ্ধান্ত নেয়া হল। আর এ সিদ্ধান্তের আলোকে ১নং দেনাদারকে ডিক্রিদার ব্যাংক বরাবর আসল টাকা হিসাবে ৪৩,৪৭,৬২৬.২৫ টাকা এবং অন্যান্য খরচ বাবদ ৩,৬৯,২৩৬/- টাকা একুনে ৪৭,২৬,৯৭৩.৭৫/-( সাত চল্লিশ লক্ষ ছাব্বিশ হাজার নয়শত তেষট্রি টাকা পঁচাত্তর পয়সা) অত্র আদেশ প্রাপ্তির ১(এক) বছরের মধ্যে সমান ৪(চার) কিস্তিতে প্রতি কিস্তিতে ১১,৮৯,৭৪৯.৯৪/-(এগার লক্ষ একাশি হাজার সাতশত চল্লিশ টাকা চুরানব্বই পয়সা) হিসাবে পরিশোধ করে দেয়ার জন্য নির্দেশ দেয়া হল।”

20. On plan reading the above order it appears that the executing Court after considering the judgment of the Artha Rin Suit, application for waiver of the respondent No. 2, circular of the Bangladesh Bank and different correspondence of the authority of the Bank then in pursuance of the provision of section 57 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 has reduced the decreetal amount to at Tk. 47,26,973.75/- like as a Court of first instance. The said order of the Executing Court is contrary to the definition of decree as defined in the Code of Civil Procedure.

21. We have also gone through the section 50(1) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 which runs as follows:

“(১) ধারা ৪৭ এর বিধান সাপেক্ষে, এই আইনের অধীন কোন আদালত, ঋন প্রদানের দিবস হইতে মামলা দায়েরের দিবস পর্যন্ত সময়কালে কোন ঋনের উপর আর্থিক প্রতিষ্ঠান কর্তৃক আইনানুগ ধার্যকৃত সুদ বা ক্ষেত্রমত, মুনাফা বা ভাড়া হ্রাস, মাফ বা নামঞ্জুর করিতে পারিবে না।”

22. If we consider the impugned order along with the above mentioned mandatory provision of law then it appears that the impugned order is totally inconsistence with the said provision. Furthermore, the matters which have been considered by the executing court as mentioned above are disputed question of facts. The above mentioned letters, opinion of the authority concern and BRPD circular etc. are not law at all thereby the respondent No. 2 was require to prove the said allegation in accordance with law before the Court of first instance or before the appellate Court in accordance with law. Therefore, the consideration of the above mentioned document along with the application by the respondent no. 1 in passing the impugned order had no legal jurisdiction as Executing Court. Rather, it appears that the impugned order has been passed to the contrary of the application filed by the petitioner under Order 21 Rule 11(2) of the Code of Civil Procedure for execution of the decree. In such view of the matter, the provision of section 57 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 has no manner application in passing the impugned order.

23. However, for proper consideration of this aspect we would like to study the same decision of the High Court Division passed in the case of Janata Bank Vs. Mohiuddin Specialised Textile, reported in 62 DLR 501, wherein the questions has arisen for consideration:

(i) Whether the Court is empowered to refuse interest pendent lite while decreeing the suit.

(ii) Whether is a suit filed under Artha Rin Adalat Ain, Government recommendation for exemption of payment of interest pendent lite is applicable or not.

24.To decide the said aspect their lordship's after referring as many as 11 reported judgment including the judgment of the Hon'ble Appellate Division wherein it has been decided that the recommendation of the Government cannot be enforced through a writ for the simple reason that it is not a law therefore it is the settled established principle of law the policy guide lines including the BRPD circular etc. are not law and cannot be enforced to through Court and same has already been decided in the case reported in 61 DLR 641 wherein their lordship's held that:

"The question as to whether the petitioner became a sick industry due to its own fault or for the fault of the Bank being a disputed question of fact it cannot be decided in summary writ jurisdiction."

6.Their lordship's also observed to the effect that:

"Since the recommendations cannot be legally enforced by the Court and it is not legally binding upon the Bank, no direction can he given for withdrawing a suit for non-implementation of those recommendation."

<u>25. In such view of the matter since BRPD circular relating with the government circular is a government policy guidelines for the sick industry and since the said guideline is not a law within the meaning of Article 152 of the Constitution. Therefore the implementation of said BRPD circular cannot be considered as a matter of enforcement by any Court of law; Moreover, the decree execution Court is also a Court with the meaning of section 50 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 which is being a special law and thereby the learned Judge of the Adalat being the Executing Court had no such jurisdiction to reduce or to waive the interest of loan in favour of the respondent and thereby decreed the suit for a specific amount as mentioned in the decree as well as in the application for decree. In this regard, we have also gone through the decision in the case of Sheikh Sekander Ali and others Vs. Agrani Bank Limited and others, reported in 68 DLR (AD) 112 wherein their lordship's held that:</u>

<u>"The executing court cannot go beyond the decree. The decree was passed against the writ-respondent and therefore, the executing court had no jurisdiction to strike out their names from the execution case."</u>

26. The above principle also shows that the Executing Court has debarred to do any act beyond the decree by the Hon'ble Appellate Division.

27. We have gone through the judgment passed in the case of Sonali Bank Limited Vs. Asha Tex International and others, reported in 20 BLC 185 wherein the High Court Division observed on an application filed under Article 102 of the Constitution at the instant of Sonali Bank against the order passed under section 33(5) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 in course of execution of the decree by the same Adalat itself and wherein their lordship's observed that sometime revision or appeal also can be preferred by the Bank if he is aggrieved by any order in course of execution of the decree under Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 specially under the provision of sections 33(1) to 33(7) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003. But the instant decree execution case has been started under Order 21 Rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure wherein the manner of execution and its procedure are not same with the said provision of Artha Rin Adalat. Moreover, in course of execution of the decree if any acts are omitted and any provision of the said Act is not properly follow in that case revision or appeal required to be preferred by an aggrieved party,.

28. In the particular case the respondent being the decree debtor filed the application for waiving of the interest as sick industry in pursuance of BRPD circular and other transaction between the Bangladesh Bank and the Government in the decree execution case of the petitioner. But under what provision of law has filed the said application by the respondent did not mention in his application. Though the executing court himself mentioned the section 57 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 in the impugned order. But it appears which inconsistent with the provision and procedure of the present execution case under Order 21 and its Rules of the Code of Civil Procedure. Such acts in the part of the learned Judge of the Executing Court is very much unfortunate being a judicial officer. Therefore, the decision cited by the learned Advocate for the respondent are not applicable under the facts and circumstances of the present case rather the decisions cited by the learned Advocate for the petitioner are applicable under the facts and circumstances of the present case of the petitioner.

29. Considering the facts, circumstances and discussion made above along with the principle decided in 68 DLR (AD) 192, 62 DLR 501 and 61 DLR 641, we find substance in the submissions of the learned Advocate for the petitioner. Thus, we do not find substance in the submissions of the learned Advocate for respondent No.2.

30. In the result, the Rule is made absolute.

31. The impugned order No. 70, dated 24.11.2014 passed by the respondent No. 1, learned Joint District Judge and Artha Rin Adalat No. 2, Satkhira in Artha Jari No. 07 of 2008 allowing the application to pay the principal loan amount with cost complying the I3RDP circular No. 7, dated June, 2013 (Annexure-D) is hereby declared to have been made without lawful authority and is of no legal effect.

32. The order of stay stands vacated.

33. The Executing Court is directed to proceed with the Execution Case in accordance with law and to dispose the same expeditiously.

34. No costs.

End.

full_judgment:
A.K.M. Shahidul Huq: This Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party no. 1 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment " and decree dated 27.04.1998 and 30.04.1998 respectively passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, and Artho Rin Adalat Patuakhali, in Title Appeal no. 145 of 1996 allowing the appeal and reversing the Judgment and decree dated 14.10.1996 and 20.10.1996 respectively passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, in-charge Additional court, Patuakhali in Title Suit no. 18 of 1996 should not be set aside and/or to pass such other or further order or orders as to this court may seem fit and proper.

2. The short facts leading to the disposal of the rule are that on 11.01.1992 the petitioner as plaintiff instituted a suit being Title suit no. 3 of 1992 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Patuakhali for declaration that—

a) The selection of defendant no. 1 as a Assistant Teacher of Purba Chandkhali non Government Primary School dated 11.12.1991 by the District Selection Committee for Registered Non-Government Primary School is illegal, void, without jurisdiction

b) For declaration that the plaintiff is the regular of the School

c) For declaration that the plaintiff is entitled to go the Government grant. Subsequently the suit was transferred in the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Additional Court and tenumbered as Title Suit no. 18 of 1996.

3. The plaintiffs case in short is that the plaintiff passed the S.S.C (Science) examination in the year 1985 and lie joined as an Assistant Teacher of Tuba Chandkhali Non-Government Primary School on 01.01.1987 and performing his duties regularly. He paid Taka 5000/- for repairing the school in 1990. Though the other teacher were not regular to their duties yet he was regular.

4. The defendant no. 1 is a businessman of Patuakhali new Market but he entries his name as a teacher of the said School. The executive committee of the School on 25.01.1984 released him. Thereafter he was not a teacher of the School. On the other hand Shalia Khatun (Added Defendant no. 12) entires her name as a teacher for a few days and went to her service in "ASUA". In the meantime the defendant no. 1 came to know about the grant for the teacher of Non-government Primary School and he influenced the selection committee and defendant nos. 2 and 3 through Honourable State Minister  and on 11.12. 1991obtained decision in his favour that the government grant be given to him instead of the plaintiff illegally. It caused loss to this plaintiff and deprive the plaintiff from his right. The defendant no. 3 on 09.09.1991 submitted a report which supported the plaintiff's claim but the selection committee did not consider the same. So, the selection of this defendant no. 1 as a teacher was illegal, void and malafide, hence the plaintiff instituted the suit.

5. The defendant no. 1 and added defendant no. 12 appeared in the suit by filing written objection denying all the statement embodied in the plaintiff. The defendant no.1 was appointed as Assistant Teacher in the said School on 25.05.1976 and joined on 01.06.1976 and till today he is performing his duties regularly as teacher. When the government in 1991 took the decision that the teachers of the Non-government Primary Schools shall be given grant the plaintiff inclusion with the members of the Managing Committee of the School entired his name instead of this defendant no. 1, changed all the registers of the School and created new documents to this effect. The defendant no. 1 filed petition to the than State Minister for Education for those illegal activities of the plaintiff and the Managing Committee. The Honourable Minister directed the Chairman of the District Selection Committee into the matter and to take proper action. The then Chairman of the District Selection Committee, Principal, Patuakhali Government College along with Secretary of the committee on 09.10.1991 went to the locality and made investigation in presence of the teachers. Members of the committee and local elites regarding the allegations raised by the defendant no.1 found genuine. The plaintiff never appointed as Assistant Teacher of the said School and he never performed his duties as teacher. The plaintiff after passing S.S.C examination appeared in the H.S.C examination in 1987 from the Subidkjali College as a regular student but could not successes. So, he went to Dhaka and served in a garments name `Maraka' the plaintiff never donated the School financially and he had got no contribution for this School. This defendant being the regular teacher the District Selection Committee on 11.12.1991 Selection the defendant no. 1 as Second teacher of the School legally and properly. So the government grant in the name of the defendant no. 1 available, yet for this suit the same can not be drawned since there is the dispute with the head Master and the member of the Managing Committee, hence they did not allowed this defendant to put his signature in the Daily attendance register. So, he is bound to maintain separate attendance register. The plaintiff has got no cause of action, so the suit is liable to be dismissed with cost.

6. The case of the added defendant no. 12 is that she was appointed as Assistant Teacher on 06.03.1984 and joined on 11.03.1984 an performing her duties regularly from the date of her join in the service. The plaintiff raised an illegal and false allegation that this defendant no. 22 was the staff of ASHA but in fact though for a short period. She was in service of "ASHA" but immediate after appointment as Assistant Teacher in the said School, she did never went to the ASI1A. The defendant no. 1 illegally claimed himself as Fourth Teacher of the said School and arrange for stray of grant in favour of this defendant and she also claimed that the plaintiff and the defendant no. 1 are not the teacher or not working in the said school.

7. During trial the plaintiffs examined 4 witnesses and defendant no.1 examined 4 witnesses and added defendant no. 12 examined 2 witnesses in support of their respective claim and after concluding trial the learned trial court by the judgment and decree dated 14.10.1996 and 20.10.1996 respectively decreed the suit on the ground that the plaintiff was found a regular teacher and selection of defendant no. 1 dated 11.12.1991 was not legal.

8. Against the judgment and decree the opposite party no:1 as appellant fled Title Appeal no. 145 of 1996 in the Court of District Judge, Patuakhali which was ultimately heard by the learned Sub-Ordinate Judge, Artha Rin Adalat, Patuakhali who by the judgment and decree dated 27.04.1998 and 30.04.1998 respectively allowed the appeal and send back the suit on remand to the learned trial court for retrial on the round that the circular no.  সাঃ ৭/৩ পি-২৭/৯০/৮২ শিক্ষা তারিখ ১৩.২.৯১ ইং/৩০.১০.৯৭ বাংলা Was not properly considered.

9. Mr. Md. Mostafa, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner while Mr. Md. Abdur Rahman Howlader, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite parties.

10. Mr. Md. Mostafa, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that the Purba Chand Khali Non-government Primary School was functioning since 1974 and got it registration on 04.03.1980 and the plaintiff was appointed as Assistant Teacher on 24.12.1986 and Joint on 1.1.1987 since then he has been functioning as a regular teacher. The defendant no. I was appointed as Assistant Teacher on 25.05.1976 and joined on 1.06.1976, but in the hazira boo his appearance was noted since 1974 the learned trial court upon considering all the hazira book as well as the inspection report came to a conclusion that the defendant no. 1 is not a regular teacher.

11 . He next submits that the added defendant no. 12 was appointed on 11.03.1984 and she was also included in the grant list from the period of 1.1.1991 to 30.6.1991, but the learned trial court found from exhibit IV i.e. Inspection report submitted to the then state Minister, Ministry of Education to the effect that during the aforesaid period the defendant no. 12 served in "ASHA". so she could not be treated as regular teacher. Considering the evidence on record the learned trial court found the plaintiff as regular teacher since 1.1.1987 and as such selection of defendant no. 1 dated 11.12.1991 as Assistant teacher is illegal and the plaintiff is also entitled to get the substantive all benefit. .

12. He also submits that the learned Appellate Court without reversing the finding of facts arrived by the learned trial court most erroneous held that the circular issued by the Ministry of Education bearing no. শা-৭/৩ পি-২৭/৯০/৮২ তারিখ ১৩.২.৯১ ইং/৩০.১০.৯৭ বাংলা Was not ‘Do/so/N)a followed, but it is not the case either of the plaintiff or the defendant. The aforesaid circular runs in the following manner :-

গণপ্রজাতন্ত্রী বাংলাদেশ সরকার,

শিক্ষা মন্ত্রণালয়,

সারকনং-শা-৭/৩পি-২৭/৯০/৮২ 			তারিখ -১৩.২.৯১ইং/৩০.১০.৯৭ বাংলা

বিষয়- বাধ্যতামূলক প্রাথমিক শিক্ষা বাস্তবায়ন কার্যক্রমের অধিনে রেজিষ্রিকৃত বেসরকারী প্রাথমিক বিদ্যালয়ের শিক্ষকগণের জন্য বেতন বাবদ অনুদান মঞ্জুরীর নীতিমালা।

বাধাতামূলক প্রাথমিক শিক্ষা বাস্তবায়ন কার্যক্রমের অধিনে রেজিষ্রিকৃত বেসরকারী প্রাথমিক বিদ্যালয়ের শিক্ষকগণের জন্য সরকার বেতন খাবদ অনুদান মঞ্জুরীর ব্যবস্থা করিয়াছেন। এই অনুদান প্রাথমিক পর্যায়ে নিম্নোক্ত নীতিমালা অনুযায়ী প্রদান করা হইবে বলিয়া সিদ্ধান্ত গৃহিত হইয়াছে।

১। ১৯৯১ শিক্ষা বর্ষের জন্য ৩১/১২/১৯৯০ ইং তারিখের মধ্যে রেজিষ্টরিকত সকল বেসরকারী প্রাথমিক বিদ্যালয়

২। তালিকাভুক্ত বিদ্যালয়ের ছাত্র সংখ্যা ২৫০ জ্নে উন্নীত না হওয়া পর্যন্ত অনুদান স্থগিত থাকিবে।

IV) it is stated that,  বিশ্ববিদ্যালয়ের যেসকল মন্তব্য বই পাওয়া গিয়াছে তাহাতে জনাব মোঃ শাহ আলম খানের বিরুদ্ধে বিদ্যালয়ে অননুমোদিতভাবে অনুপস্থিত থাকা অথবা অন্য কোন কারণে কখনও কোন কৈফিয়ত তলব অথবা কোন বিধিগত ব্যবস্থা গ্রহনের কোন রেকর্ড নাই। এই বিষয়ে বিদ্যালয়ের প্রধান শিক্ষক এবং কমিটির সভাপতি ও অন্যান্য সদস্যবৃন্দকে জিজ্ঞাসাবাদ করিয়া জানা গেল যে, তাঁহার বিরুদ্ধে কখনও ঐ ধরনের ব্যবস্থা গ্রহণ করা হয় নাই। and as such the suit of the plaintiff respondent petitioner is not maintainable and the same should be dismissed and the rule of the civil revision is liable to be discharged with modification of the impugned judgment and decree of the appellate court not sending the same on remand.

21. Mr. Md. Abdur Rahman Howlader, the learned Advocate for the opposite party no.1 in support of his contention has referred the case of Uttara Bank Limited Vs. Shahabuddin Khan and others reported in 59 DLR page 166 para 9, He next referred the case of M/S Eastern Mercabtile Bank Ltd. Vs. Mohammad Shamsuddin reported in 21 DLR (SC) page 365 para 7.

22. I have perused the impugned judgment and decree of the last court of fact passed in title appeal no. 145 of 1996 perused the revisional application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure also considered the submissions as advanced by the learned Advocate of both sides in support of their respective case.

23. In order to arrive at a proper finding it is very much pertinent to refer the case of Begum Lutfunnessa Vs. Md. Shafiullah and others reported in 12 BLT (AD) page 66 where out Apex court held that:-

<u>24. It is now settled principle of law that order of remand should not be made lightly by the superior court and that if materials on record are sufficient for the disposal of the suit in the case instead of sending the suit back on remand the superior court should dispose of the same. The above is the general as well as broad principle of law. But there may be case (s) as the instant one even though there is no prayer from the parties in the proceeding for sending the suit back to the trial court or to the lower appellate court for disposal where right of the parties to the proceeding so send back on remand is dependent on the result of a suit filed earlier still remand pending the order of remand by the appellate/higher court made in such a situated cannot he considered unjustified.</u>

25. From the defence taken by the defendant no. 1 in title suit no. 50 of 1984 as it is quire evident that right claimed by the plaintiffs under the agreement between the defendant no. 1 and plaintiffs is depended in the result of title Suit no. 360 of 1979. It is further seen that an order of injunction in Title suit no. 360 of 1979 is in force restraining the defendant no. 1 from dealing with the property in any manner and consequently if a decreed the affirmative is passed in title suit no. 50 of 1984 that would not become effective in disposal of the title suit no. 360 of 1979. In the background of the said undisputed facts the order of the High Court Division sending back the case on remand for trial of title suit no 50 of 1984 analogously with title suit no. 360 of 1979 can all together be not said justified even though has been made in the absence of prayed from the parties. It is now the settled principle of law that order of remand should not be made lightly by the superior court and that if materials on record are sufficient for the disposal of the suit in that case instead of sending of the suit back on remand the superior court should dispose of the same. The above is the general as well as broad principle of law but there may be case (s0 as the instant one, even though there is no prayer from the parties in the proceeding for sending the suit back to the trial court or to the lower appellate court for disposal where right of the parties to the proceeding so send back on remand is depended on the result of a suit filed earlier still remands pending the order of remand by the appellate/higher court made in such a situation cannot he considered unjustified.

26. I find that the case of Hosna Ara Begum and others Vs. Montaj Ali and others reported in 55 DLR (AD) page 20 where our Apex Court held that:-

27. Where the trial court has decided the suit on merit the revisional court has no power to remand by shirking its duty of writing the judgment afresh.

"Though the learned Judge of the High Court Division quoted the relevant portion of the deposition of D.W. 1 as noticed by us, but he failed to consider the same properly resulting in error in his finding. Further, the legal position is that where evidence has been duly placed before the trial court and it has decided the suit on merit the revisional court has not power to remand by shirking its duty, particularly solely for the purpose of writing the judgment afresh. This appeal, therefore, must succeed."

29. 1 find that in the case of Akitullah and others Vs. Zafala Begum and others reported in 54 DLR (AD) page 74 where out Apex Court held that:-

Remand as contemplated under Order 41 rule 23 of the Code of civil procedure was not of matter of course or to fill in. the lacuna in any party's pleading.

"Remand as contemplated under Order 41 rule 23 of the Code of civil procedure was not of matter of course or to fill in the lacuna in any party's pleading. In the instant case the plaintiff having led evidence to show that the Hiba-bil-Ewaj allegedly executed by Wazeuddin in favour of Abdul Majid being a forged and concocted one, there was no reason to send back the suit on remand to the trial court for fresh decision after making necessary amendment of the plaint with opportunity to the contesting parties to adduce fresh evidence."

30. In view of the clear finding of the trial court regarding Hiba-bil-Ewaz as aforesaid we are of the view that this open remand order for a fresh decision in the suit allowing parties to adduce fresh evidence is designed to fill in the lacuna of the pleadings of the parties, which is not the intent and object of the order of remand contemplated under Order XLI rule 23 of the Code of Civil Procedure. In the case of Dr. Razia Khatun Vs. Bhanu Guha and others 1986 BLD (AD) 135 it has been observed that "the long line of judicial decision is to the effect that the remand order should be avoided as far as possible and even the Privy Council in some cases observed that indiscriminate order of remand tantamount to shirking the responsibility."

31. In view of the submissions as advanced by the learned Advocate appearing on both sides and on due proper consideration of the submissions of the learned Advocate for the petitioner. I find substance in the rule and the citations as referred by the learned Advocate for the petitioner in support of his contentions are fully applicable in the facts and circumstances of the present case. On the other hand I find no merit of the opposite party submissions of the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite party and the citations as referred by the learned Advocate for the opposite party have no manner of application in the facts and circumstances of the Present case.

32. In that view of the matter I find merit in the rule.

33. In the result, the rule is made absolute, there will be no order as to cost. The impugned judgment and decree dated 27.4.1998 and 30.04.1998 respectively passed Subordinate Judge, and Artho Rin Adalat Patuakhali, in title appeal no. 145 of 1996 allowing the appeal and remanding the case to the learned trial court for re-trial by reversing the judgment and decree dated 14.10.1998 and 20.10.1996 respectively passed by learned Senior Assistant Judge, in charge Additional Court, Patuakhali in Title Suit no. 18 of 1996 is herby restored.

34. The order of stay as granted at the time of issuance of the rule is hereby re-called and vacated.

35. Send down the lower Court records along with a copy of this judgment to the concerned court forthwith for information and necessary action.

End.

Abdul Quayum with Md Mozibur Rahman, Advocates ------ For the Petitioner. 
Mohammed Eunus, Advocate ------ For the Opposite Parties.
parties:
Easin Fakir (Md) -------  Petitioner
