full_judgment:
This rule has been issued calling upon opposite party No.1 to show cause as to why the judgment and decree passed by learned District Judge, Patuakhali in Title Appeal No.30 of 1989 affirming the judgment and decree dated 29-1-1989 and 7-2-1989 respectively passed by learned Assistant Judge, Bauphal should not be set aside.

2. The opposite party No.1 as plaintiff instituted Title Suit No.118 of 1984 for declaration of title in the suit land. The case of the plaintiff in brief is that, the suit land belonged to Md Easin Fakir having 8 anna shares and Md Gayazaddin remaining 8 anna shares. During survey and settlement operation record of right has been prepared in their names. Gayazaddin became aged and having no heirs, he bequeathed the suit land to his wife Kulsum Bibi Abdus Salem, the plaintiff and Abul Kalam by a will dated 5-6-1957 and made over possession to them. After executing Osiatnama Abul Kalam died and after having discussion with his well wishers, he came to know that more than 1/31d of the bequeathed property will not be effective and, as such, Gayazaddin executed a deed of gift on 14-1-1962 in favour of the plaintiff and made over possession to him in presence of witnesses and since then the plaintiff continued to hold and possess the suit land residing in the homestead portion and cultivating the agricultural land. After Gayazaddin's death, the plaintiff continued to hold and possess the suit land as before. Although the defendant had/has no title and possession over the suit land, he raised claim therein which clouded the clean title of the plaintiff and hence the suit for declaration of title.

3. The defendant No.1 contested the suit by filing written statement contending inter alia that the suit land along with other land belonged to Gayazaddin and defendant No.1 who is the cousin of Gayazaddin and the said Gayazaddin died without any children whereby defendant No.1 got 12 anna shares in the suit land and Gayazaddin's wife Kulsum Bibi got 4 anna shares therein and since then defendant No.1 has been holding and possessing the suit land beyond statutory period of limitation within the knowledge of all concerned and, as such, he prayed for dismissal of the suit.

4. The plaintiff examined 3 witnesses and submitted papers in support of his claim while the defendant No.1 also examined 3 witnesses in support of his claim. The trial Court found that the plaintiff got the suit land by virtue of deed of gift from Gayazaddin and since then he has been holding and possessing the same. The trial Court further held that the deed of gift executed by Gayazaddin has been proved by its scribe PW 2. The trial Court also relied upon the document submitted by the plaintiff to the effect that he secured loan from the bank by producing the documents executed by Gayazaddin to him.

5. The appellate Court concurred with the findings of the trial Court and dismissed the appeal finding no tangible ground therein.

6. Mr Abdul Quayum, learned advocate appearing for the petitioner, submits that admittedly the suit land belonged to defendant No.1 Mr Easin and Gayazaddin and as Gayazaddin died issueless, the defendant No.1 being his cousin inherited 12 annas shares therein and Gayzaddin's wife Kulsum Bibi inherited remaining 4 annas share and since then defendant No.1 has been holding and possessing the suit land. He next submits that Osiatnama dated 5-6-1957 purported to have been executed and registered by Gayazaddin is not a valid document and more importantly the original document was not produced by the plaintiff; so by virtue of Osiatnama the plaintiff in fact inherited nothing from Gayazaddin as because the purported will has been cancelled by Gayazaddin himself. He next submits that the deed of gift dated 24-1-1962 is not a valid document because of its lack of registration as per section 123 of the Transfer of Property Act. He further averred that if any deed of gift is written one, it must be registered for its validity and there must be three elements to be fulfilled namely declaration by donor, acceptance by the donee and consequent delivery of possession which are clearly absent in the purported transaction. He next submits that any property can be transferred by oral gift subject to fulfillment of three condition as stated above, but if any document is written it must be registered, otherwise it will not be a valid deed of gift. He next submits that the suit is not maintainable also on the ground that simple declaration has been sought for without making any consequential relief namely, prayer for partition because admittedly the suit land is owned and possessed by Md Easin and Gayazaddin and so claiming Gayazaddin's share, prayer for partition is necessary. He further submits that the deed of gift was not proved by its attesting witnesses and, as such, the deed of gift has got no evidentiary value. The trial Court as well as the appellate Court without adverting those vital aspects of the case decreed the suit which cannot be sustained. In support of his contention he referred the cases of Jabed Ali vs Abu Shaikh being dead his heirs Md Naimuddin, 35 DLR (AD) 31, Salma Khatun, vs Zilla Parishad, Chittagong 51 DLR (AD) 257, Amirunnessa vs Abdul Mannan Howlader 17 BLD 251 = 1 BLC 183, National Bank Lid. vs Habib Bank Ltd 56 DLR (AD) 1,5, Said Ali vs Soleman Bibi, BCR 1982 140, Tayeb Ali vs Abdul Khaleque, 42 DLR (AD) 87 and Mst Sardar Bibi vs Abdul Latif, PLR 1308.

7. Conversely, Mr Mohammed Eunus, learned advocate appearing for the opposite parties, submits that admitted owner Goyazaddin earlier transferred the suit land to the present petitioner, his brother Abul Kalarn and his wife Kulsum Bibi by virtue of a will dated 5-6-1957 and as it is found that transfer of more than 1/3rd  of the whole property through will not be valid, he again executed deed of gift in favour of the present plaintiff on 24-1-1962, mentioning the legal proposition regarding will, he submits that Gayazaddin consciously transferred the property in favour of the plaintiff in presence of witnesses and he performed all formalities namely proposal for gift, acceptance by the plaintiff and delivery of possession of the suit land, He averred that since transfer by Gayazaddin, the plaintiff, has been holding and possessing the suit land and both the Courts below found the deed of gift as valid and genuine one. He next submits that the scribe of the deed of gift dated 24-1-1962 gave evidence as PW 2 stating that he wrote the deed of gift having executed by Goyazuddin in favour of plaintiff, where Easin Fakir and others were witnesses and Easin Fakir himself put his signature in the deed of gift knowing fully well about the contents and averments of the deed in question. He submits that since the deed of gift has been acted upon and the plaintiff has been possessing the suit land till date, the infirmity in the deed of gift for its lack of registration, if any, has been cured by long-standing possession and occupation by the plaintiff. He further submits that the witnesses of the plaintiffs have proved continuous possession of the plaintiff over the suit land which both the Courts below found to be consistent and consequently the judgment and decree cannot be assailed in the revisional forum. He next submits that both the Courts below found plaintiff's title and possession over the suit land and this concurrent finding of fact cannot be reversed in the revisional forum unless misreading, non-reading and non-consideration of material evidence are shc4n which the defendant could not detect. He further submits that the age of PW 2 as mentioned in the evidence is misinterpreted as because in the school record and other papers sometimes actual date of birth is not recorded and, as such, PW 2 Abdul Khalik was major at the relevant time when he composed the deed of gift in question. In support of his contentions Mr Eunus referred the cases of Abul Hashem (Bulbul) vs Mubarak Uddin Mahamud, 38 DLR 145, Haji Aklema Khatun vs Shah Alam, 33 DLR 62, Mahajak Shipping Co. Ltd. vs MV Sagar at present berthed at Chittagong Port 39 DLR 425, Jabed Ali vs Abu Shaikh being dead his heirs 35 DLR (AD) 31, Enjaheruddin Mia alias Md Enjaheruddin Mia vs Mohammad Hossain, 50 DLR (AD) 84, KZ Alam vs Secretary Ministry of Housing and Public Works, 54 DLR 451 and Amirunnessa vs Abdul Mannan Howlader, 17 BLD 251 = 1 BLC 183.

8. Mr Mohammed Eunus, by filing another application under Order VI, rule 17 of the Code of Civil Procedure, prayed for inserting prayer for partition for passing a preliminary decree in favour of the plaintiff in respect of his title having declared by the Courts below contending that the suit land along with other lands are ejmaly property of Gayazaddin and Md Easin and the plaintiff being co-sharer of Gayazaddin, it should be partitioned with other co-sharer namely the heirs of Md Easin who was defendant No. 1 . The merit of the said application will be dealt with later.

9. Firstly, I shall deal with osiatnama dated 5-6-1957 executed by Gayazaddin in favour of the plaintiff, Abul Kalam and Goyazaddin's wife Kulsum Bibi whereby Gayazaddin bequeathed 6+6 annas share to plaintiff and Abul Kalam and 4 annas to his wife Kulsum Bibi. As per Muslim law, a will can be executed by any Muslim regarding his property which may be effective after his death, provided no other heirs raise any objection thereto and in case of any objection 1/3RI of the bequeath property will be valid. It appears from the deed of gift that subsequently Gayazuddin executed a deed of gift in favour of the plaintiff Abdus Salam on 24-1-1962 whereby he gifted his property in favour of the plaintiff Abdus Salam wherein it is stated that the will be effective in respect of 1/3rd share and Abdus Salam will get 2/3rd of the property by gift. One thing is apparent from the contents of the deed of gift is that the donor apprehended that 2/3rd property of the will may not be conveyed but it is not comprehensible because Abdus Salam and Abul Kalam being his niece through sister are not sharers and so restriction of will is not applicable to them which remained unexplained. Now if I turn to the question of gift dated 24-1-1962, the established principle of Mohammedan Law is that there may be gift by a Muslim orally or by a written instrument subject to the provision of section 123 of the Transfer of the Property Act. As per section 123, any deed of gift, if written, it must be registered under provision of Mohammedan Law. So far ingredients of gift is concerned, three elements must be present, namely the donor's intention to make gift, acceptance by donee, and delivery of possession.

If these three elements are fulfilled, then a deed of gift is completed, even if it is oral gift, but for written document is concerned, it is to be registered. Besides if any property is donated by oral gift, by fulfilling all the ingredients of the gift, it can be written in a subsequent document evidencing oral gift with particular dates, witnesses and other elements of oral gift, but in the present deed of gift, there is no such assertion that the gift is made earlier in presence of witnesses and effected by delivery of possession, rather by the very instrument the property is being transferred to the donee i.e. the plaintiff without having any oral gift and, as such, the deed of gift is not valid one for want of registration. This question has been nicely expounded in BCR 1982 140 in following way,

"According to Muhamadan Law gift of immovable property may be made orally. When such a gift is made, followed by a deed, the deed of gift is nothing but a mere piece of evidence of the transaction. It does not, therefore, require registration."

10. But here the unregistered deed of gift is not preceded by any oral gift, rather there was a will which has been cancelled by the doner with flimsy ground. In the said decision, it has been further held that, in such situation the said document will be treated simply as a collateral evidence of making gift. The same question came before the court in the case of Jabed Ali vs Abu Shaikh, being dead his heirs Md Naimuddin, 35 DLR (AD) 31 wherein same facts has also been reiterated that if there is a oral gift and all component of the gift is fulfilled i.e. proposal, acceptance and delivery of possession, in that case the oral gift can be considered as a valid gift, but if the document is a written text, it must be registered. In the said decision it is held in the following way: "On the other hand if there is no oral gift, but by an unregistered instrument, a person seeks to make a gift of immoveable property, it must be registered."

11. In the instant case, it is not the contention of the plaintiff that the suit property has been made over by an oral gift effecting delivery of possession, as such this instrument is to be registered for effective completion of the gift. In 54 DLR 451 it is held that under the Transfer of the Property Act, a Muslim gift is not required to be registered but factual aspect is quite different here. In that case, allottee of RAJUK transferred the property in favour of someone, authorizing him to mutate the property in his name in the record of right. The transferee made application to the authority for mutating his name in the record of right, but the authority declined to mutate the name of the donee who filed writ petition wherein it has been held that since allottee has transferred the property in favour of someone else, the authority is bound to effect mutation. So the factual aspect of that case is different from the facts and circumstances of the present case.

12. On the other hand Mr Abdul Quayum submits that section 129 of the Transfer of Property Act is relating to movable property which has no relation regarding any immovable property and, as such, as per section 123 of the Transfer of Property Act if a deed of gift is written one without mention of oral gift it must be registered and this aspect was not specifically dealt with in the said decision.

13. Regarding the decision referred by learned advocate for the opposite party reported in 17 BLD 251 = 1 BLC 183, it appears that there was a unregistered deed of gift which was a basic title deed of the plaintiff and the plaintiff successfully proved his possession beyond 12 years where the learned Court held that since the plaintiff proved his possession beyond 12 years, so inspite of being an unregistered deed of gift, his title is perfected by adverse possession. In the present case, no adverse possession has been pleaded specifically in the plaint and no evidence has been led for adverse possession, rather the plea of the plaintiff was that by virtue of deed of gift, he is possessing the suit land claiming the deed of gift as a valid document and there is no claim that his possession is perfected by adverse possession. So in absence of any factual context, the ratio enunciated in 17 BLD 251 = 1 BLC 183 cannot be relied upon. Moreover in 35 DLR (AD) 31, the appellate division held in clearest terms that, if there is a written instrument not preceded with oral gift, it must be registered. The ratio declared by our apex Court must have primacy over other decisions.

14. In the case of Mst. Sardar Bibi vs Abdul Latif PLR 1308 it is held that if a will is made by any Muslim and subsequently a gift is also made in respect of self same property the validity of the will be revoked automatically and so far gift is concern it is to be decided as per law and reversionary heirs right's will not be curtailed in any way inspite of making gift.

15. Mr Mohammed Eunus relied upon the principal of 35 DLR (AD) 31 that an oral gift of the immoveable property made according to Muslim Law would be valid but such ratio is not applicable here because in the instant case a written gift has been made without registering it and, as such, it is to be registered as per Section 123 of the Transfer of Property Act. In 33 DLR the ingredients and gift has been reiterated and further their lordship held that if a written deed is executed and registered subsequent to the oral gift it is valid but here registration is lacking and, as such, this principal is not applicable here. In 50 DLR (AD) 84 it is held that plaintiff could have asked for ether joint possession or partition as a co-sharer of the defendants in the disputal land but if no such prayer is made in the lower Court it can be sought even in the High Court division.

16. Now, turning to the evidence of the witnesses, the trial Court found the evidence of PW 1 regarding the age of the plaintiff and other aspect is inconsistent, but even then, the trial Court relied upon her evidence. PW 1 while depositing in the year 1989 stated that she was 35 years old but in cross examination she stated her age 25 years. She further stated that Goyazaddin died 50/60 years back and she was present when deed of gift is written. According to plaint deed of gift was executed on 14-1-1962, before she was born and, as such, it is clear that her purported knowledge regarding the deed of gift is totally untrue and naturally she had no knowledge about Osiatnama and deed of gift but both the Courts below without adverting the vital fact believed the story of Osiatnama and deed of gift. She further asserted that the suit land is being possessed by bargader, but no such credible witness is produced in support of such contention. So far the evidence of PW 2 Abdul Khalek who is the scribe of the deed of gift, stated during cross examination that his date of birth as per school certificate is 31-12-1953 and he further stated that his actual date of birth is in the year of 1944. He stated that in 1970 he passed SSC examination and in 1962 he was a student of class Eight or Nine. So according to his discloser two facts emerged that his actual date of birth is 1944, but as per the school certificate, he was born on 31-12-1953. So far the purported date of birth as disclosed, no certificate has been submitted before this Court to substantiate such claim. Regarding the school certificate as mentioned, if the date of birth be taken as correct, his age would be eight years when the document in question is written. So it is not provable or believable that a boy of eight years can compose a deed of gift.

17. Mr Mohammed Eunus in this connection submits that in fact in a school register the actual date of birth is not revealed always, rather it is being furnished upon assumption and in support of his contention he referred the case of Abul Hashem (Bulbul) vs Mobarak Uddin Mahmud 38 DLR 145. It has been mentioned in the said decision that:

"The legal position with regard to on entry in School Register. Admit Cards and Board's Certificate is that such Registers, Cards and Certificates are public documents and are admissible in evidence under section 35 of the Evidence Act, but the evidentiary value to be attached to the entries will vary from case to case. With regard to the School Register it has long been held that it is very common to understate the age when entering a school in order that the boy may not be too old for government service."

18. So far the proposition is concerned, there is no doubt that such thing happens in our socio-economic context, but so far this particular aspect is concerned, it is incumbent upon the plaintiff to substantiate the claim that actually he was not of eight years old, rather he was above eight years old and he was mature enough to compose a deed of gift or instrument, but so far the PW 2 is concerned, no such attempt has been made to substantiate such claim. PW 3 Abul Hasem Howlader stated that Yeasin Fakir put Signature in his presence and he showed Yeasin Fakir's signature in the deed of gift. He also stated that the certificate issued by the Chairman regarding osiatnama is written by him. He also admitted that he heard that Moslem procured a pattanama from plaintiff in advance. The said Moslem is his brother's son. He also disclosed in cross examination that Salam and Abdul Khalik are friends. He stated that he does not know who wrote the deed of gift and what is the contents of the deed of gift. He disclosed that Goyazaddin died after seven/eight days of execution of deed of gift. From his evidence it appears that he was not particularly aware when the property was actually gifted to the plaintiff. He stated that Yeasin Fakir put down his signature in the deed of gift in his presence, but on comparing the signature in the deed of gift and other signatures put in vokalatnama, affidavit and other documents, the signature seems not to be identical with the signature made in the deed of gift. It is not the assertion of the plaintiff that Yeasin Fakir with a view to derive illegal gain consciously put signature in other papers which is quite dissimilar with the signature of the deed of gift.

19. Now if I turn to the evidence of the DW's it is revealed that DW 1 Yeasin Fakir stated that he is not aware about the registered Osiatnama which is frivolous. He also stated that deed of gift is fraudulent and no possession is delivered to plaintiff and on the death of Goyazuddin he got twelve annas share and Kulsum got four annas share. DW 2 Ismail Howlader stated in deposition that Yeasin Fakir is the cousin of Goyazuddin whose death Yeasin Fakir and Goyazuddin's wife got the suit land. DW 3 Abdul Kader stated examination-in-chief and cross-examination that defendant No.1 possessed the suit land. Now, so far the findings of the trial Court is concerned, PW 2 and PW 3 disclosed that the plaintiff withdrawn loan by virtue of osiatnama being exhibit 1 and 1(ka), but it is revealed subsequently that Gyazaddin purportedly executed deed of gift and, as such, the conferment of title by will is not to be relied upon. It is not the case of the plaintiff that by depositing '/31`t share of the will, loan has been procured, rather it is the case of the plaintiff that by depositing the deed of Osiatnama loan has been procured but Gayazuddin himself nullified the will. So, that vita] point has been overlooked by the trial Court. The trial Court held that a deed of gift can be effected both by oral and documentary evidence. There is no dispute regarding such contention, but there are certain situation where oral gift can be made and it is to be made by fulfilling certain specific condition and so far documentary gift is concerned if it is written, it must be registered, but that point was also overlooked by the trial Court. Besides almost all the witnesses disclosed that after 7/8 days of execution of deed of gift Gayazuddin died, which also shaken the veracity of the deed of gift. Apart from this it is stated in the deed of gift that osiatnama will not be valid beyond 1/3K1 share, but the plaintiff not being heir, the principle is not applicable to him and, as such, it is apparent that deed of gift has been created with a view get illegal gain. The trial Court stated that the defendant failed to produce any evidence that he got the property from Gayazuddin save and except producing two witnesses. This portion of the findings is also not altogether correct as because the defendant produced evidence in support of acquisition of title and possession in the suit land.

<u>20. Apart from this, it is the plaintiff who is required to prove his title and possession by proving his claim which is not done here. So far the findings of the trial Court is concerned, the wife of Gayazuddin filed solenama admitting the title of the plaintiff over the suit land although PW 1 stated that she is not aware about the contents of solenama. However, mere filing of solenama regarding any property, title cannot be conferred in favour of the recipient of the Solenama as the plaintiff is to get title by his own account. The findings and reasonings regarding mode of possession of the plaintiff in the suit land is not substantiated by the evidence on record.</u>

21. The appellate Court concurred with the findings of the trial without adverting the factual aspects. The appellate Court erroneously held that the will dated 5-6-1957 being registered document is believable and further made a hypothetical comments that if the deed of gift, is forged, criminal case could have been lodged. So far the signature put down by Yeasin Fakir is concerned, it is discussed earlier that the signatures of Yeasin Fakir is not identical with his other signatures and, as such, this finding is also not based on record. So far the registered will is concerned the original will is not produced before the Court, mere photostat copy has been exhibited, so no finding should have been given regarding a document which has not been produced before the Court. From the above discussion, it is apparent that the findings of both the Courts below is based on misreading, non-reading and non-consideration of the evidence on record and, as such, the revisional Court can rightly and validly interfere with such finding.

22. The plaintiff by filing application for amendment of plaint intended to insert prayer for partition but since it is found that the plaintiff has got no title in the suit land, his prayer for partition is not sustainable at this stage.

23. In the above facts and circumstances, I am of the view that the gift in question has not been proved. Both the Courts below misconstrued the deed of gift and without considering the legal aspects and facts and circumstances decreed the suit in favour of the plaintiff.

24. In the above context, I find merit in the rule and accordingly the rule is made absolute without any order as to cost.

Let copies of the judgments along with the Lower Court Records be sent to the concern Courts.

End.

case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 15-5-2014 passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition Nos.1755, 1756, 1758, 1759, 1760, 1763, 1764, 1765, 1766, 1767, 1768, 1769, 1770, 1771, 1797, 1798 of 2008).
full_judgment: Syed Mahmud Hossain CJ: All the appeals, by leave, are directed against the judgment and order dated 15-5-2014 passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition Nos.1755, 1756, 1758, 1759, 1760, 1763, 1764, 1765, 1766. 1767. 1768. 1769,1770, 1771, 1797, 1798 of 2008 making all the Rules absolute with direction. 2. All the civil appeals have been heard together and are being disposed of by this common judgment as they do involve common questions of laws and facts. 3. The facts, leading to the filing of all the appeals, in a nutshell, are: All the writ-petitioners were serving in different clerical posts as Senior Clerk, MLSS, LDA-cum-Typist, Bearer, Typist, Assistant Clerk, Office Assistant etc. At the Zia Fertilizer Company Limited (hereinafter referred to as ZFCL) for several years on daily basis. The writ-petitioners applied to the ZFCL authority to appoint them permanently in the vacant posts. On consideration of their quality of service and sound performance, the authority by Memo No. ZFCL/Proshason/ LSA/7(a)/1607 dated 9-10-2006 sent a proposal to the Chief of Bangladesh Chemical industries Corporation (BC1C), which is the controlling authority of ZFCL seeking approval under Article 13(5) of the Bangladesh Chemical Industries Enterprise (Nationalization) Order, 1972 (PO 27 of 1972) for the permanent appointment of the writ-petitioners against vacant posts at ZFCL. It has been further stated in the said letter that “তারা নিজ নিজ কর্মক্ষেত্রে উল্লেখযোগ্য অবদান রেখেছেন। কিন্তু বছরের পর বছর কাজ করার পরও তাদেরকে স্থায়ীভাবে চাকুরীতে নিয়োগ না করায় তাদের মধ্যে অনিশ্চয়তা ও হতাশা বিরাজ করছে। তাদেরকে স্থায়ীভাবে নিয়োগ দেয়া হলে তাদের কর্মস্পৃহা বৃদ্ধি পাবে।” It is further stated that as a regular practice vacant posts at the ZFCL are generally filled in by regular appointment from daily basis workers, who possess required qualifications. 4. In response to the aforesaid letter dated 9-10-2006 seeking approval under Article 13(5) of the Bangladesh Chemical Industries Enterprise (Nationalization) Order, 1972 (PO 27 of 1972) for permanent appointment of the writ-petitioners, the Deputy Employee Chief on behalf of the Employee Chief vide Memo No. BCIC/Niog-3/ZFCL-6145 dated 5-2-2007 intimated the Managing Director of ZFCL about the approval of BCIC for permanent appointment of the writ-petitioners at ZFCL subject to approval of the ZFCL. In the letter it was clearly stated that “আপনাদের ৯.১০.২০০৬ ইং তারিখের সূত্র নং-জেডএফসিএল/প্রশা/এলএসএ/৭/১৬০৭ এবং ৩১.১.২০০৭ ইং তারিখের সূত্র নং জেডএফসিএল/প্রশা/এলএসএ/১১৯/৪৯৯৫/৩০১৩ পত্রের প্রেক্ষিতে জানানো যাচ্ছে যে, নিম্নে উল্লেখিত ১৮(আঠার) জনকে শুন্য পদের বিপরীতে তাদের নামের পার্শ্বে উল্লেখিত পদ বেতনক্রম/ মঞ্জুরীক্রম সম্পূর্ন অস্থায়ী ও এডহক ভিত্তিতে নিয়োগদানের জন্য কর্তৃপক্ষ অনুমোদন করেছেন।” 5. After getting formal approval from the Bangladesh Chemical Industries Corporation, ZFCL Authority vide Memo dated 06.02.2007 issued appointment letter to the writ-petitioners and after getting the said appointment letters the writ-petitioners joined in their posts and started serving the authority to the satisfaction of all concerned. It is stated that there is no allegation from any quarter against the writ-petitioners' service or their efficiency. Thereafter, suddenly by letter dated 29-11-2007, the Senior Assistant Secretary of the Ministry of Industries, informed the Chairman of the Bangladesh Chemical Industries Corporation that a newspaper article showed that there were certain irregularities in the appointment of 19 employees at ZFCL and that the writ-petitioners having been found unsuitable for the post, their services should be terminated. On receipt of the aforesaid Memo dated 29-11-2007, Bangladesh Chemical Industries Corporation by letter dated 05.12.2007 informed ZFCL to terminate the Service of the writ-petitioners at once. The ZFCL Authority as per direction of writ-respondent No.2, thereafter, by the impugned letter dated 11.12.2007 informed the writ-petitioners that their services were terminated and they would be entitled to one month's pay in lieu of any prior notice. 6. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the impugned letters dated 11-12-2007 (Annexure-B) issued by writ-respondent No.3 under the signature of writ-respondent No.5, the writ-petitioners filed the writ petitions before the High Court Division and obtained Rules Nisi in the above writ petitions. 7. Writ-respondent Nos. 2 and 5 contested the Rules by filing affidavit-in-opposition controverting the material statements made in the writ petitions. Their case, in short, is that the writ-petitioners were appointed on purely temporary and ad-hoc basis and the same was mentioned in their appointment letters. The petitioners joined their services accepting the said terms and conditions as stated in the appointment letters and the employer had every right to terminate their services without assigning any reason and this is also the case as per provision of Bangladesh Labour Law,2006. It has been further stated that since the appointment of the writ-petitioners were irregular, they were legally terminated as per instruction made by the Ministry of Industry in terms of clause-3 of the appointment letter and that the writ-petitioners cannot have any grievance against the same. It has been further stated that as per PO 27 of 1972, the concerned Ministry has supervisory and controlling authority over BCIC and ZFCL and, as such, ZFCL is bound to carry out the instructions of the Ministry as well as Bangladesh Chemical Industries Corporation. It has been further stated that the writ-petitioners' services have been terminated in accordance with the provision of law and that the impugned orders of termination are nothing but termination simpliciter and hence the writ-petitioners cannot have any grievance against the same and that the Rules are liable to be discharged. 8. The learned Judges of the High Court Division, upon hearing the Rules, by the impugned judgment and order dated 15-5-2014, made the Rules absolute with direction. 9. Feeling aggrieved by and dissatisfied with judgment and order passed by the High Court Division, the writ-respondents as the leave-petitioners have filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal Nos.3028-3043 of 2014 before this Division, in which, leave was granted on 19-2-2015, resulting in Civil Appeal Nos.96-111 of 2015. 10. Mr Tofailure Rahman, learned Senior Advocate, appearing on behalf of the appellants in all the civil appeals, submits that according to term and condition No.3 of the appointment letter, the writ-petitioner-respondents were terminated from service and, as such, the termination in question is mere termination simpliciter and not a stigma and that the High Court Division taking into consideration some extraneous matter held that the orders of termination were arbitrary and malafide and, as such, the impugned judgment should be set aside. He further submits that according to clause (2) of Article 11 of PO No.27 of 1972, the Board shall be subject to the superintendence and control of the Government and shall be guided, in discharge of its functions, by such general or special instruction as may, from time to time, be given to it by the Government and. as such, the writ-petitioner-respondents were rightly terminated as per instruction of the concerned Ministry and. as such, no interference is called for. 11. In support of his submissions, the learned Senior Advocate relied on the case of Secretary EPIDC vs Md Serajul Haque, 22 DLR (SC) 284. 12. Mr AF Hassan Ariff, learned Senior Advocate, appearing on behalf of the respondents of all the civil appeals, on the other hand, submits that the instant orders of terminations were not termination simpliciter and in fact, the writ-petitioner-respondents had been dismissed from their service in the garb of termination and, as such, the High Court Division was justified in making the Rules absolute. 13. We have considered the submissions of the learned Counsel of both the sides, perused the impugned judgment and the materials on record. 14. Admittedly, the writ-petitioners were appointed to the vacant posts at Zia Fertilizer Company Limited (ZFCL) as per recommendation of ZFCL authority. On consideration of their long standing service, the Bangladesh Chemical Industries Corporation at its discretion considered the recommendation of ZFCL and approved the appointment of the writ-petitioners to the respective posts. The writ-petitioners joined those posts and continued to work without any complaint from any quarter. It appears that suddenly the Ministry of Industries by its letter dated 29-11-2007 issued by the Senior Assistant Secretary informed the Bangladesh Chemical Industries Corporation that the writ-petitioners were not fit for the job against which, they were appointed and consequently, they were liable to be terminated. 15. For better appreciation, the letter dated 29-11-2007 is produced below: গণপ্রজাতন্ত্রী বাংলাদেশ সরকার শিল্প মন্ত্রণালয় স্বস-বিসিআইসি শাখা ৯১ মতিঝিল বাণিজ্যিক এলাকা, ঢাকা। নং-শিম/স্বস (বিসিআইসি)বিবিধ-১/২০০৭/১০৪১ তারিখ: ২৯ নভেম্বর, ২০০৭ বিষয়ঃ আশুগঞ্জের সার কারখানায় গোপনে নিয়োগ,আড়াইশ জন বঞ্চিত সংবাদ পত্রিকায় প্রকাশিত হওয়ার প্রেক্ষিতে ইতোপূর্বে তদন্ত কমিটির দাখিলকৃত প্রতিবেদন উল্লেখিত নিয়োগপ্রাপ্ত ১৯(ঊনিশ) জন কর্মচারী ও শ্রমিক নিয়োগ যাচাই বিষয়ে দায়ী কর্মকর্তা/কর্মচারীদের দায়-দায়িত্ব নিরুপনের তদন্ত প্রতিবেদন। উপযুক্ত বিষয়ের আলোকে বিসিআইসির তৎকালীন কর্মচারী প্রধান আব্দুর রহমান, জিয়া সার কারখানার তৎকালীন ব্যবস্থাপনা পরিচালক জনাব গোলাম কিবরিয়া তৎকালীন মহাব্যবস্থাপক(ভারপ্রাপ্ত) জনাব এম এ আক্কাস তৎকালীন ব্যবস্থাপক(প্রশাসন) সৈয়দ আইনুল হক এবং সিবি এর প্রাক্তন ও বর্তমান নেতৃবৃন্দ যথাক্রমে সর্বজনাব মোজাম্মেল হক খন্দকার, ফরিদউদ্দিন আহমেদ, মোঃ গাউছুর রহমান ও আমিন খন্দকার এর বিরুদ্ধে বিধি মোতাবেক ব্যবস্থা গ্রহণ এবং তদন্ত প্রতিবেদনে উল্লেখিত নিয়োগপ্রাপ্ত ১৯(ঊনিশ) জন শ্রমিক কর্মচারী যাচাই অন্তে অযোগ্য বিবেচিত হওয়ার নিয়োগপত্রের শর্ত মোতাবেক তাদেরকে অপসারন করার জন্য অনুরোধ করা হলো। স্বাক্ষর অস্পষ্ট ২৯.১১.২০০৭ (এ,কে, এম সামসুল আরফীন) সিনিয়র সহকারী সচিব ফোনঃ-৯৫৫১৪৩৫। 16. The aforesaid letter reveals that inquiries against some other officers of Bangladesh Chemical Industries Corporation indicated that the writ-petitioners were not fit for the job and, as such, they should be terminated. There is nothing on record to show that during the course of inquiry held at the instance of the Ministry, the writ-petitioners were heard and they were allowed to defend their case. There is no doubt that the Government in the Ministry of Industries is the controlling authority of ZFCL but it cannot direct BCIC to remove employees of ZFCL, who were appointed by the proper authority. 17. In this connection, clause (1) and (2) of Article 11 of the Bangladesh Industrial Enterprises (Nationalisation) Order, 1972 is quoted below: "11.(l) The general direction and administration of the affairs and business of a corporation shall vest in a Board of Directors which may exercise all powers and do all acts and things which may be exercised or done by the Corporation. (2) The Board shall be subject to the superintendence and control of the Government and shall be guided, in the discharge of its functions, by such general or special instruction as may, from time to time, be given to it by the Government." 18. Clause (1) of Article 11 provides that general direction and administration of the affairs of the business of a corporation shall vest in a Board of Directors, which may exercise all powers and do all acts and things, which may be exercised or done by the Corporation. 19. Clause (2) of Article II provides that the Board shall be subject to the superintendence and control of the Government and shall be guided, in the discharge of its functions, by such general or special instruction as may, from time to time, be given to it by the Government. 20. For harmonious construction, both clause (1) and (2) must be read together. Consideration of clause (2) in isolation without considering the other clause cannot give a harmonious interpretation. If the Ministry dictates the Corporation in all matters then the purpose of clause (1) of Article 11 will become nugatory. There is, of course, no doubt that the Ministry has the control and superintendence over the Corporation but the Ministry cannot interfere in its internal management without concurrence of the Board of Directors. Therefore, the letter dated 29-11-2007 issued by the Senior Assistant Secretary of the Ministry of Industry was malafide exercise of power. The concerned authority of ZFCL recommended the appointment of the writ-petitioners to Bangladesh Chemical Industries Corporation which after considering everything recommended the absorption of the writ-petitioners against the vacant posts. After that, the writ-petitioners were appointed to the said posts and no complaint was made by the Company about their performance. For the reasons best known to the Ministry, it instructed the Corporation to terminate the writ-petitioners' job. Therefore, the orders of termination were not termination simpliciter. Consequently, this is the outcome of arbitrary exercise of power in a malafide way and, as such, the High Court Division was justified in making the Rule absolute declaring the orders of termination to have been passed without lawful authority and to be of no legal effect. 21. Mr Tofailur Rahman, learned Senior Advocate, appearing on behalf of the appellants of all the civil appeals, relied on the case of Secretary, EPIDC vs Md Serajul Haque 22 DLR (SC) 284 where the orders of termination do not at all contain any charge or stigma against the respondents. By these orders, their services were terminated with an offer of 1 month's pay in lieu of notice on the sole ground that their services were no longer required by the Corporation. These orders cannot, therefore, be regarded as orders terminating the services of the respondents by way of penalty. 22. In the case in hand, at the instruction of the Ministry of Industries, the Corporation initiated inquiry against some officials of the Corporation and subsequently pursuant to the letter dated 29-11-2007 of the Ministry, the services of the writ-petitioners were terminated. Therefore, the termination in the instant case is not a termination simpliciter and, as such, the case cited by the learned Senior Advocate for the respondents has no manner of application. 23. In the case of The Chartered Bank, Mombay, vs The Chartered Bank Employees' Union AIR 1960 SC 919, it has been held as under: “..........The form of the order of termination is not conclusive of the true nature of the order, for it is possible that the form may be merely a camouflage for an order of dismissal for misconduct. It is therefore always open to the tribunal to go behind the form and look at the substance; and if it comes to the conclusion, for example, that though in form the order amounts to termination simpliciter it in reality cloaks a dismissal for misconduct it will be open to it to set it aside as a colourable exercise of the power." 24. In order to arrive at a correct decision, the Court has the power to go behind order of termination and may look to the cause underlining the dismissal. 25. Reliance may be placed on the case of Bangladesh Road Transport Corporation vs Md Shahidullah 54 DLR (AD) 124, it has been held as under: "It appears that the Corporation initially wanted to remove the respondent through a proceeding and that having failed, they wanted to take action for compulsory retirement under Regulation 55(2) of Service Regulations,1990 and that also having failed his service was terminated. As a matter of fact from the materials on record, the learned Judges of the High Court Division correctly held that in the present case, it was punishment/dismissal in the garb of termination and consequently set aside the order of termination." 26. Reliance may be placed on the case of Parjatan Corporation vs Md Ali Hossain, 65 DLR (AD) 158 wherein it has been held that the impugned letter of termination passed against the petitioner of this case though appears to be a termination simpliciter, but in fact, it is not. The petitioner was dismissed from his service in the garb of termination by resorting to regulation 50(2) of the Employees Service Regulations, 1990. 27. The principle expounded in the case referred to above also applies to the facts and circumstances of the present case as the letter dated 29-11-2007 reveals that there was an inquiry about the appointment of the writ-petitioner-respondents and pursuant to the said inquiry, the writ-petitioner-respondents were terminated from service by the letter dated 11-12-2007. Therefore, it cannot be said that the writ-petitioner-respondents were terminated from service and in fact, they were dismissed from service in the garb of termination. In the light of the findings made before, we do not find any substance in these appeals. Accordingly, all the appeals are dismissed without any order as to costs. End.

lawyer:
ABM Waliur Rahman Khan, Advocate--For the Petitioner 

AHM Ziauddin, AAG—For Respondent No. 1.
parties:
SM Abdus Salam ----- Petitioner
Vs
Joint Commissioner and Chairman Licensing Authority Customs, Excise and VAT and others …. Respondents
full_judgment:
Zinat Ara J: In this Rule Nisi, the petitioner has challenged the legality of the order under Nothi No. নথি নং ৫/২০(২৫) এলসি-সিত্র/ভোমরা/৯৮/২৬৬৮ (১-২৩) dated 9-8-2016 (Annexure-H to the writ petition) passed by respondent No. 1, the Joint Commissioner and Chairman, Licensing Authority, Customs, Excise & VAT Commissionerate, Khulna, suspending operation of the petitioner's Customs House Agent License No. 03/Lc-ca/98 dated 8-7-1998.

Petitioner's Case

2. The petitioner's case as narrated in the writ petition as well as in the reply to the affidavit-in-opposition is as follows:—

Petitioner, SM Abdus Salam, is the Proprietor of M/s Shawon Enterprise. He is engaged in the business as Overseas Bank) exported commodities to Bangladeshi Importer, namely, M/s Seven Trade International (briefly stated as Seven Trade) and that on examination of the documents of Bhomra Customs Station, it was found that Indian Exporter BR International and Bangladeshi Importer MP International through L/C No. 0120915010312 dated 6-10-2015 issued by Social Islami Bank Limited (shortly, Social Bank) had released the aforesaid imported goods through petitioner as C&F Agent with false statement collusively and fraudulently. The petitioner gave reply to the said show cause notice on 12-5-2016 stating that he was engaged to release the imported goods of MP International of Bogra exported from BR International, West Bengal, India through L/C No. 0120915010312 dated 6-10-2015 issued by Social Bank, Bogra Branch, Bogra. But, the petitioner had no knowledge about the exporter Sheikh Saria or the importer Seven Trade. The Joint Com-missioner then heard the petitioner in-person. At the time of hearing, the petitioner submitted written statements on 3-8-2016 stating that he through proper documents released the raw cotton as' an authorized C&F Agent. Thereafter, the petitioner received the impugned order signed by the Joint Commissioner by suspending the petitioner's License allegedly for violating the provisions of section 2(ka) read with section 207 of the Customs Act, 1969 (shortly, the Customs Act) and rules 20 and 21 of the Rules. Prior to this incident, Bhuiyan Mafizur Rahman, a Customs Officer of Customs Station, Bhomra lodged a First Information Report with Satkhira Police Station on 18-8-2015 being Satkhira Police Station Case No. 25 dated 18-8-2016 under sections 420/406/467/468/471 of the Penal Code. Whereupon, a criminal case was started against the petitioner and the importer, which is still under investigation. The petitioner was enlarged on ad-interim bail in the said criminal case on 3-4-2017 by the High Court Division vide Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 13333 of 2017. In connection with the said criminal case, the show cause notice was issued by the Joint Commissioner to the petitioner. The impugned suspension order was passed on 9-8-2016 and till date, no departmental proceeding has been drawn up against the petitioner and therefore, the order of suspension for an indefinite period is malafide, arbitrary and liable to be struck down.

Respondent No. 1’s Case

3. Respondent No. 1, the Joint Commissioner, contested the Rule by filing an affidavit-in-opposition controverting the statements made in the writ petition and supporting the impugned order. It has been stated that on the basis of a complain from Indian Exporter Sheikh Saria, an Inquiry Committee was duly formed by the customs authority for investigation into the allegations made by the said Indian Exporter. After investigation, the Inquiry Committee submitted a report. From the report, it was Found that the Exporter Sheikh Saria exported goods against five L/Cs being L/C Nos. 071603 31510160 dated 1-11-2015, 120915010312, 120915010312 and 120915010312 all dated 6-11-2015 and 0716033 15101 76 dated 19-11-2015 issued by Indian Overseas Bank, Hongkong to Bangladeshi Importer, Seven Trade. The Joint Commissioner, on the basis of secret information, came to know that the said goods were released through tempered and forged shipping documents, etc. by the petitioner. After scrutiny/verification of the register/information of Bhomra Customs Station ASYCUDA World along with other related documents, the Joint Commissioner also found that Indian Exporter, BR International, Kolkata, exported the goods through L/C No. 120915010312 dated 6-11-2015 issued by Social Bank to Bangladeshi Importer, MP International, Bogra. The petitioner was appointed by MP International for release of the goods. But the petitioner allegedly released the goods of another exporter and importer by tempering and forging the shipping documents. Thus, it is found that the petitioner has violated the provisions of rule 21 of the Rules. The License of the petitioner has been provisionally suspended under rule 20 of the Rules. Suspension of a license is not a punishment and it has been passed for completion of investigation of the criminal case by the police. In the circumstances, the rule is liable to be discharged.

Arguments as Advanced by the Contending Parties

4. Mr ABM Waliur Rahman Khan, the learned Advocate for the petitioner, takes us through the writ petition, the reply to the affidavit-in-opposition, the connected materials on record and submits that an Officer of Customs, Customs Station, Bhomra lodged a first information report being Satkhira Police Station Case No. 25 dated 18-8-2017 against the petitioner and an importer, which is under investigation. He next submits that meanwhile, over the same subject matter, the Joint Commissioner issued a show cause notice upon the petitioner, the petitioner gave reply to the show cause notice and then the Joint Commissioner, upon hearing the petitioner, passed the impugned order of suspension of the License on 9-8-2016. He further submits that although suspension order was passed on 9-8-2016, but till date no proceeding has been drawn up by the customs authority against the petitioner relating to the License. He finally submits that the suspension order of the License for an indefinite period without drawing up any departmental proceeding relating to License is malafide, arbitrary and, as such, liable to be struck down.

5. In support of his submissions, Mr Khan has relied on the decision in the case of Bangladesh Livestock Research Institute vs Dr Md Jahangir Alam Khan, reported in 20 BLT (AD) 239.

6. In reply, Mr AHM Ziauddin, the learned Assistant Attorney-General appearing for the Joint Commissioner (respondent No. 1), takes us through the affidavit-in-opposition and contends that the petitioner'' Customs House Agent License was suspended for violation of the provisions of rule 21 of the Rules. He next contends that there is no provision in the Rules within which an investigation has to be completed or the period for which a Customs House Agent License may remain suspended. He finally contends that the police has not completed the investigation of the case filed against the petitioner and therefore, the order of suspension cannot be said to be unlawful and the Rule is liable to be discharged.

Point for Determination

7. The only question to be decided in this Rule is the legality of the suspension order of the petitioner's Customs House Agent License under Nothi No. 5/20(25)Lc-ca/Bhomra/98/2668(1-23) dated 9-8-2016 (Annexure-H to the writ petition) for an indefinite period.

Examination of the Records

8. We have examined the writ petition, the affidavit-in-opposition filed by the Joint Commissioner (respondent No. 1), the reply of the petitioner to the affidavit-in-opposition and the connected materials on record. We have also carefully studied the relevant provisions of the Customs Act, 1969 and the কাস্টমস এজেন্ট লাইসেন্সিং বিধিমালা, ২০১৬ and the decision as reported in 20 BLT (AD) 239.

Deliberation of the Court

9. There is no dispute that a Customs Officer of Customs Station, Bhomra lodged Satkhira Police Station Case No. 25 dated 18-8-2016 against the petitioner and an importer under sections 420/406/467/468 and 471 of the Penal Code and that the said case is still under investigation it is not disputed that after filing of the aforesaid criminal case against the petitioner and another, the Joint Commissioner issued a show cause notice upon the petitioner for violating certain provisions of the Customs Act and the Rules made thereunder and that the petitioner gave reply to the said show cause notice. It is also admitted that upon hearing, the impugned order has been passed by the Joint Commissioner by suspending of the petitioner's Customs House Agent License on 9-8-2016 i.e. about one and half years back. Admittedly, till date, the Joint Commissioner failed to bring any departmental proceeding against the petitioner. The suspension order of the petitioner's license has not also been withdrawn by the authority concerned.

10. From the impugned order of suspension (Annexure-H to the writ petition), it transpires that the petitioner's Customs House Agent License was suspended under rule 20 for violating the provisions of rule 21 of the Rules. For better understanding, the relevant provisions of rules 20 and 21 of the Rules are quoted below:

“২০ । লাইসেন্স সাময়িক স্থগিতকরণ। -লাইসেন্সিং কর্তৃপক্ষের নিকট যদি প্রতীয়মান হয় যে, কোন কাস্টমস এজেন্ট এর অনুকূলে প্রদত্ত লাইসেন্স অবিলম্বে স্থগিত করা আবশ্যক, তাহা হইলে বিধি ২১.এর অধীন লাইসেন্স বাতিল করিবার পূর্বে লাইসেন্সের কাযকারিতা সময়িকভাবে স্থগিত রাখিতে পারিবে।

২১। লাইসেন্স বাতিল এবং অর্থদণ্ড আরোপ ।-(১) লাইসেন্গিং কর্তৃপক্ষ নিন্বর্ণিত যে কোন কারণে কাস্টমস

এজেন্টকে ১৫ (পনের) দিনের মধ্যে কারণ দর্শাইবার সুযোগ প্রদান করিয়া তাহ্র লাইসেন্স বাঁতিলসহ উপ-বিধি (২) এর অধীন ক্ষেত্রমত অর্থদণ্ড আরোপ করিতে পারিবে, যথাঃ__

(১) এই বিধিমালার কোন বিধান বা লাইসেনে উন্মেখিত কোন শর্ত ভন করা হইলে;

(৯) প্রযোজ্য কোন শুল্ক-কর ফাঁকি বা প্রচলিত আইনের অধীনে আরোপিত শর্ত বা নিষেধাজ্ঞা এড়াইয়া

যাই���ার উদ্দেশ্যে কোন জাল দলিল প্রস্তুত করিয়া কাস্টমস কর্মকর্তার নিকট দাখিল করিলে;

(Underlined by us)

11. Thus, it appears that the provision relating to suspension order of Customs House Agent License is provided in rule 20 of the Rules. There is no provision in this rule or in any other rule of the Rules providing the period for which a license may remain suspended.

12. However, we are of the considered view that a license ought not remain suspended for an indefinite period. After suspension of a license, the concerned authority must bring and complete departmental proceeding within a reasonable period.

13. In the case repotted in 20 BLT (AD) 239, their lordships of the Appellate Division, in case of an order of suspension for an indefinite period, decided as under:—

"Respondent No. 1 moved the above writ petition in the High Court Division challenging the order of his suspension dated 7 December, 2009 on the ground that it was issued arbitrarily with ulterior motive, while he was awaiting an order of appointment to the post of Managing Director of the Bangladesh Livestock Research Institute he was suddenly placed under suspension by order under memo dated 7th December, 2009 and that no departmental proceeding was drawn up within 5 months till he filed the writ petition on 30th May. 2010 despite issuance of suspension order.

The High Court Division upon consideration of the materials on record noticed that during the long period of 5 months 23 days no formal charge was framed against the writ petitioner and that he was supposed to go on LPR on 30th December, 2009. ne claimed that with a view to circumvent his appointment to the post of Director General, he was suspended from the service. He was a veteran freedom fighter and there was no stigma in his service record. The High Court Division also noticed that even during the pendency of the writ petition no formal proceeding was drawn up against him and the petitioner was totally kept in dark as to the cause for issuance of the order of suspension. In view of the above, the High Court Division made the rule absolute and declared the order of suspension as has been issued without lawful authority and is of no legal effect.

We have perused the materials on record and heard the learned Counsel for the petitioner. In course of hearing, learned Counsel has conceded that no formal charge was brought against him as yet. Learned Counsel failed to satisfy us the procedure for placing an officer under suspension for an indefinite period. On consideration of the materials on record we find no cogent ground to place the respondent under suspension. It is true that an order of suspension is not a punishment but from the admitted facts, we find it difficult to come to the conclusion that the High Court Division has wrongly exercised its discretionary powers. What is more, as noticed by the High Court Division, the petitioner failed to bring any departmental proceeding against the petitioner within 5 months from the date of order of suspension. In view of the above, we find no merit in this petition. Accordingly, the petition is dismissed."

14. In the instant case also, it transpires that though the License of the petitioner was suspended about one and half years back but, till date, the Customs Department after preliminary enquiry, failed to bring any departmental proceeding against the petitioner within the aforesaid period of about one and half years from the date of order of suspension of the License. Therefore, we are of the view that the principle set out in the above case is squarely applicable in this ease.

15. The learned Assistant Attorney-General fails to show us any prevision of law either in the Customs Act, 1969 or in the Rules that due to investigation of a criminal case, a license may remain suspended for an indefinite period.

<u>16. In the facts and circumstances of the case, we are of the opinion that the suspension order relating to the petitioner's Customs House Agent License for an indefinite period without bringing any departmental proceeding against the petitioner within about one and hall years is arbitrary and malafide.</u>

17. In view of the discussions made in the foregoing paragraphs, vis-a-vis the law, we find merit and force in the submissions of Mr ABM Waliur Rahman Khan, the learned Advocate for the petitioner and we find no merit in the submissions of Mr AHM Ziauddin, the learned Assistant Attorney-General.

18. In such view of the matter, we find that the impugned order of suspension of the License suffers from legal infirmity.

19. Accordingly, the Rule is made absolute.

20. The impugned order under Nothi No. নথি নং ৫/২০(২৫) এলসি-সিত্র/ভোমরা/৯৮/২৬৬৮ (১-২৩) dated 9-8-2016 (Annexure-H to the writ petition) passed by respondent No. 1, the Joint Commissioner and Chairman, Licensing Authority, Customs, Excise & VAT Commissionerate, Khulna, suspending operation of the petitioner's Customs House Agent License No. 03/Lc-ca/98 dated 8-7-1998 is, hereby, declared to have been passed without lawful authority and be of no legal effect.

21. However, the concerned Customs Authority is at liberty to draw up departmental proceeding against the petitioner in accordance with law.

22. No costs.

Communicate the judgment to the respondents at once.

End.
