full_judgment:
AKM Abdul Hakim J: This First Miscellaneous Appeal has been preferred by the sole plaintiff-appellant against the judgment and order No. 113 dated 8-5-2016 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, Second Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 336 of 2014 rejecting an application for temporary injunction under Order XXXIX, rule 1 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure.

2. After admitting the appeal an application for temporary injunction was filed by the plaintiff-appellant accordingly a rule was issued on 19-5-2016 calling upon the respondent-opposite-parties Nos. 1-6 to show cause as to why the impugned order No. 113 dated 8-5-2016 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, Second Court, Dhaka. Pending hearing of the rule the parties are directed to maintain status-quo in respect of mutating 'ka' schedule property in the office of the defendant-opposite parties Nos. 9-10 and also for transferring and changing the nature and character of the schedule 'ka' land also possession and position of the suit land for a period of three months from date.

3. The appellant-petitioner as plaintiff instituted Title Suit No. 336 of 2014 on 8-5-2014 in the Second Court of Joint District Judge, Dhaka impleading the respondent Nos. 1-6 as defendant Nos. 1-6 and present pro forma defendant Nos. 7-10 for partition of ejamali properties described in 'Ka' and `Kha' schedule to the plaint, cancelling of sale deeds and Wasiatnama more fully described in 'Ca' and 'Gha' schedule to the plaint and also distribute the share of the bank money described in schedule 'Uma' to the plaint. Subsequently, the pro forma respondent Nos. 9-10 impleaded in the suit by order dated 3-4-2016.

4. The plaintiff case, in short, are that Father of the plaintiff, late Faiz Ahmed divorced his first wife Selima Ahmed, mother of the plaintiff in 1984 when he was 2 (two) years old, then he obtained the guardianship and custodian of the plaintiff through court; that thereafter his father took Helena Khatun, defendant No. 1 as second wife in the year 1988 and through his second wife defendant Nos. 2-3 was born; that the plaintiffs father died on 27-12-2013 after long suffering from chronic disease for long 2 years; that at the time of death he left plaintiff as one son by first wife, second wife, Helena Faiz, daughter Farhin Faiz, son Tanjim Faiz by second wife; that plaintiff owing to his job staying at Canada due to which he appointed his maternal uncle, Mr Alhaj Khondakar Musle Uddin as his attorney on 17-4-2014; that the father of the plaintiff got allotment a plot of land measuring an area of 7.104 decimal of from Government Housing Settlement Department, now under National Housing Authority (shortly, NHA) at Mirpur Road No. 1, Block-B, section-1, being commercial plot building No. 6/A, same was allotted to him by allotment letter dated 07.07.1981 and said plot of 'Ka' schedule land was delivered to him physically; that thereafter Housing Settlement Department executed registered lease agreement being Lease Deed No. 2214 dated 10-6-1982, accordingly his name was recorded in the city Jarip by filing Mutation Case No. 127-47(S)/82 dated 21-10-1982; that father of the plaintiff constructed 8 storied building by approval of the plan from RAJUK; that his father inherited 1570 sft of flat of 7th floor of 9 storied building known as "Tower Hamlet", situated in "Kha" schedule land of plot No. 4/8, Block- F under Lalmatia Housing Estate which was developed by a Developer Company, after his demise, the said property should be partitioned amongst his heirs; that the plaintiff after coming back to Bangladesh on 6-3-2014 came to know that the defendants in collusion with each other made a sale deed No.12061 dated 15-10-2012 in respect of 3rd and 4th floor against minimum consideration of money which is a forged deed and another transfer deed No. 10400 dated 23-9-2013 which was got by defendant Nos. 9 and 10 due to which they have submitted an amended deed No. 2903 dated 12-3-2014 and 13-3-2014; thereafter the attorney of the plaintiff in response to the request of defendant No. 1 sat together on 24-4-2014 for amicable settlement, he informed that no money was left in the account; that the Fourth floor of 'ka' schedule building is transferred to defendant Nos. 4-6 and rest 4 floors were distributed equally by Faiz Ahmed to his heirs by executing Wasiatnama; that the attorney of the plaintiff by obtaining the certified copy found that all deeds are found to be irregular and unethical and consideration money were not properly shown and further found that defendant No. 7 being a brother of defendant No. 1 manipulated everything to manufacture sale deeds and Wasiatnama without obtaining any consent from the plaintiff's father; that it further appears that the plaintiff's father died on 27-12-2013 and Wasiatnama deed is shown to be executed two months before his death; that the plaintiff inherited 35% share in all schedule properties and money; that defendant Nos. 1-3 by taking the advantage of joint account with the father of the plaintiff they have withdrawn the money according to their sweet will and spoiled the money and at last on 30-4-2014 the plaintiff through his attorney gave a proposal to settle amicably for partitioning the properties but the defendant refused to do so.

5. It appears that primarily the plaintiff filed the suit on 8-5-2014 through his attorney and subsequently the suit was withdrawn by order dated 18-10-2015. Thereafter, on the prayer of the plaintiff the instant suit was restored on 20-3-2016. After restoration of the suit on 20-3-2016, the plaintiff filed an application on 24-3-2016 under Order XXXIX, rules 1 and 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure praying for injunction restraining the defendants from mutating their names in the office of defendant Nos. 9-10 as well as from transferring, changing the nature and character of the suit properties as described in the schedules 'ka' and 'kha' to the plaint and also restraining them from creating obstruction or hindrances against the tenants of the ground floor of the `ka' schedule, who purchased the possession of the said ground floor and also restraining them from withdrawing and encashing the money lying with the bank described in 'Uma' schedule to the plaint. The trial court by order dated 24-3-2016 issued show cause notice. After show cause notice none of the defendant appeared and filed written objection against the show cause notice. Thereafter, the plaintiff-appellant filed an application on 13-4-2016 under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure praying for ad-interim injunction and the learned Joint District Judge by order No. 109 dated 17-4-2016 passed an order to maintain status-quo till filing of the written objection in respect of possession and transfer of the suit property. In due course the matter of temporary injunction was fixed for hearing.

6. Defendant Nos. 4-6 filed written objection on 27-4-2016 and Defendant No. 1 also contested the injunction application by filing separate written objection on 3-5-2016. That the case of the defendant Nos. 1, 4-6 are that father of the plaintiff during his lifetime executed bainanama with the defendant Nos. 4-6 for sale of 1st, 2nd and 3rd floor more or less 12,000 sft as specifically mentioned in schedule 'Ica' to the plaint for a total consideration of Taka 4,60,00,000 out of which Taka 30,00,000 was paid as advanced and bainanama was registered being No. 15083 dated 13-12-2011. It was further stated that the plaintiff during his lifetime filed an application for sale permission before the Lessor National Housing Authority-defendant No. 9 to transfer the properties mentioned in the bainanama and defendant Nos. 9-10 accordingly issued sale permission dated 11-10-2012 in favour of the lessee, Faiz Ahmed. Subsequently, predecessor of the plaintiff, Faiz Ahmed executed two sale deeds being registered sale deed Nos. 12060 dated 15-10-2012 showing transfer of 3rd and 4th floor measuring 3,075 sft. and another sale deed being No. 10400 dated 23-9-2013 showing transfer of Ground and 2nd floor each for an area of 3075 sft. Then the defendant Nos.4-6 filed an application before the office of defendant Nos. 9-10 for mutating their names by memo dated 28-4-2016. It may be noted that Faiz Ahmed, the original allottee/lessee of the suit schedule 'ka' and `kha' property died on 27-12-2013.

7. The injunction matter was heard by the learned Joint District Judge on 8-5-2016. After contesting hearing the learned Joint District Judge rejected the injunction application on the finding that when the co-sharer is in exclusive possession of any land of schedule property and part from the other land he can get protection of the court from the other co-sharer who got no possession, but in the present case said principle is not at all applicable. In respect of the 'ka' schedule property admittedly the plaintiff is not in possession of the said schedule property which is 9 storied building out of which only 6th floor for an area of 146 square meter are to be partitioned by meets and bound. In this respect the plaintiff-appellant referred to a decision reported in 10 BCR (AD) 124 = 42 DLR (AD) 3. But the facts and circumstances of cited case and the present case are totally different. So the trial court categorically finds that the decision is not applicable in the instant case.

8. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the impugned order No. 113 dated 8-5-2016, the plaintiff-appellant preferred the present appeal and obtained the order of status-quo in Civil Rule No. 396 (FM) of 2016 on 19-5-2016.

9. It appears that during pendency of this rule the present appellant filed an application for staying operation of the mutation order passed by the office of the defendant-respondent-opposite-parties Nos. 9-10 and also prayed to call for the record of নথি নং জাগৃক/ভূসব্য/সিপি/১৬/৮০ lying in the office of defendant-respondent-opposite-party Nos. 9-10. After hearing, this court by order dated 2-8-2016 allowed the said application in part and the defendant-respondent-opposite-parties No. 9-10 are directed to transmit the record নথি নং জাগৃক/ভূসব্য/সিপি/১৬/৮০ to this court within three weeks. Although the said application was not opposed from any corner.

10. Mr Kamal-ul-Alam, the learned Advocate with Mr JK Paul, Advocate appearing on behalf of the plaintiff-appellant. Mr Kamal-ul-Alam, the learned Advocate at the very outset submits that the National Housing Authority mutated the names of the defendant Nos. 4-6 during subsistence   of the order of injunction against them. He further submits that the trial court was wrong in law in finding that the plaintiff did not specify his share in the schedule land and, as such, he is not entitled to get an order of injunction. He further submits that the trial court did not at all consider the specific allegation of the plaintiff that the alleged acquisition of right and title of the defendants on the basis of Wasiatnama and the sale deeds are tamed with fraud. He next submits that the trial court was wrong in law in holding that section 134 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act barred the jurisdiction of the civil court with regard to mutation. He categorically submits that the said section has no manner of application in the case of mutation by the National Housing Authority with regard to leasehold land owned by it. He finally submits that the petitioner did not seek any injunction against the National Housing Authority but sought injunction against the defendant Nos. 4-6 from mutating their names in the office of National Housing Authority. In support of his submissions learned Advocate has cited the following decisions namely 14 MLR (AD) 111 and 24 BLD (AD) 282 = 9 BLC (AD) 272.

11. On the other hand, Mr M Nurul Amin, the learned Advocate for the defendant-respondent-opposite-parties Nos. 1-6 submits that the courts below after considering the papers, documents and materials on record rightly rejected the prayer for temporary injunction and correctly found that the plaintiff has failed to prove his prima-facie title and exclusive possession on the suit schedule 'ka' land. He further submits that no strong prima-facie case is available in this case and balance of convenience and inconvenience is not in favour of the plaintiff but in favour of the defendants. He vehemently submits that admittedly the plaintiff is out of possession of the suit 'ka' schedule land. He finally submits that the original lessee, Faiz Ahmed during his lifetime transferred the schedule 'ka' property to defendant Nos. 4-6 by registered kabalas dated 15-10-2012 and 23-9-2013 in respect of 'ka' schedule for sale of the 1st, 2nd, 3rd, and 4th floor of the schedule 8th storied building which admittedly situated in the land of the National Housing Authority and predecessor of the plaintiff was original lessee under the National Housing Authority. In support of his contentions, he referred decisions of our apex court reported in 33 DLR (AD) 298, 14 MLR (AD) 111 and 49 DLR 260. Thus the court below rightly found that the plaintiff has failed to prove the prima-facie title and exclusive possession over the schedule property.

12. Ms Nasrin Hena, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of National Housing Authority defendant Nos. 9-10 submits that Title Suit No. 336 of 2014 filed by the plaintiff-appellant on 8-5-2014 without impleading the National Housing Authority as defendants who is admittedly the lessor of the suit schedule 'ka' and 'kha' property. She further submits that the title suit was withdrawn by the plaintiff by order No. 102 dated 18-2-2015 and subsequently suit was restored by order No. 105 dated 20-3-2016. She next submits that Faiz Ahmed, the original lessee of the suit property applied for sale permission on 18-7-2012 and accordingly National Housing Authority issued sale permission on 11-10-2012. Thereafter Faiz Ahmed died on 27-12-2013. She also submits that defendant Nos. 4-6 applied for mutation before the National Housing Authority on 23-3-2014 and plaintiff, Tanvir Faiz filed written objection in said mutation case on 30-3-2016 annexing the application for injunction filed in Title Suit No. 336 of 2014. She vehemently submits that National Housing Authority passed the mutation order on 28-4-2016, long before passing of the status-quo order passed by High Court Division on 19-5-2016 and no order of injunction was subsisting against defendant nos. 9-10 when mutation order passed by the authority on 28-4-2016. Moreover, the trial by order No. 109 dated 17-4-2016 passed status-quo order against the defendant Nos. 4-6 in respect of 'ka' schedule with regard to possession and transfer but not for mutation of schedule 'Ka' property. She finally submits that the trial court after considering the materials on record rightly rejected the plaintiff's application for temporary injunction.

13. Heard the learned Advocates and perused the memo of appeal, application for injunction dated 16-5-2016, application for staying operation of the mutation order dated 24-7-2016 and নথি নং জাগৃক/ভূসব্য/সিপি/১৬/৮০ transmitted by the National Housing Authority in compliance of the order dated 2-8-2016 passed by this court.

14. It appears that in respect of mutation of the schedule 'ka' property no order of status-quo was passed by the learned Joint District Judge on 17-4-2016. It further appears that in four corners of plaint no averments were made by the plaintiff-appellant in this respect. Although the plaintiff in his application for temporary injunction sought injunction in respect of mutation of the suit property in favour of the defendant Nos. 4-6 by the National Housing Authority, defendant Nos. 9-10. It also appears that admittedly the plaintiffs are not in possession of the suit properties. It further appears that after filing of the present appeal, on the prayer of the appellant this court by order dated 19-5-2016 passed an order of status-quo in respect of mutating 'ka' schedule property in the office of the defendant respondent Nos. 9-10.

15. It is evident from the record of the National Housing Authority that defendant Nos. 9-10 mutated the names of defendant Nos. 4-6 on 28-4-2016 long before passing of the status-quo order passed by this court. It also appears that the plaintiff-appellant realising the fact of mutating the names of defendant Nos. 4-6 subsequently filed an application before this court on 24-7-2016 for staying operation of the mutation order without mentioning the date. High Court Division by order dated 2-8-2016 did not pass order of status-quo in respect of mutating `Ka' schedule property but allowed the application in part directed the defendant-respondent-opposite-parties Nos.9-10 to transmit its case record that is নথি নং জাগৃক/ভূসব্য/সিপি/১৬/৮০ to this court within three weeks from date.

16. Thus the main submission advanced by the learned Advocate for the appellant that during subsistence of the status-quo order/ injunction order, the National Housing Authority mutated the names of the defendant Nos. 4-6 does not consider any merit because of the fact that the order of status-quo was passed in this appeal on 19-5-2016 in respect of mutating 'Ka' schedule property in the office of the defendants respondent Nos. 9-10, although respondent Nos. 9-10 on 28-4-2016 mutated the names of the defendants Nos. 4-6.

17. It is pertinent in this case to emphasize a point that the order No. 1u9 dated 17-4-2016 of the learned Joint District Judge directing the defendant Nos. 4-6 to maintain status-quo in respect of 'Ka' schedule property with regard to possession and transfer but in that order the learned Joint District Judge did not pass order of status-quo in respect of mutation of 'Ka' schedule property.

18. It further appears that the plaintiff filed the suit for partition and cancellation of some deeds and it is admitted by the plaintiff that he claimed partition for allotting him 35% share in the schedule' ka' and 'kha' land and building and the amount lying in the bank.

19. Thus it is apparent that the trial court has rightly found that the plaintiff failed to show exclusive possession of a specific and separate share thereof, well demarcated by boundaries in the schedule 'ka' land, as such, the trial court by referring 10 BCR (AD) 124 rightly found that the plaintiff is not entitled to get injunction. Since the plaintiff failed to show exclusive possession in any specific share of the ejmali property seeking injunction against the other co-sharer from disturbing his possession. It further appears that admittedly the plaintiff is out of possession, thus the question of disturbing plaintiff's possession does not arise at all. Thus the principle of law enunciated in 10 BCR (AD) 124 = 42 DLR (AD) 3 is not applicable to the present case.

<u>20. Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case, we find that the plaintiff has failed to make out any good arguable prima-facie case. It further appears that in the plaint as well as in the application for temporary injunction plaintiff failed to show any prima-facie title and exclusive possession of a specific and well defined portion in the suit property and the balance of convenience and inconvenience is not in favour of the plaintiff but in favour of the defendants. In a suit for partition when a co-sharer of a ejmali/joint property is in exclusive possession of a specific and well defined portion is entitled to retain his possession till legal partition, by an order of injunction against another co-sharer who threatens him with dispossession. In granting injunction it is not required by the court to decide the title of the respective parties. But in the present case admittedly plaintiff is not in exclusive possession of the suit property in assertion of his own right, so he can not claim for injunction and in case of injunction it is only look into factum of possession in the case property.</u>

<u>21. We have already found that admittedly the plaintiff is not in possession of the suit property and the trial court on consideration of the materials on record rightly rejected the prayer for temporary injunction. Since the plaintiff has failed to prove his exclusive possession in the suit property, he is not entitled to get the order of temporary injunction. Moreover, it is well settled that there can be no injunction for actionable wrongs for which damages are proper remedy.</u>

22. Learned Advocate for the appellant refers the cases reported in 14 MLR (AD) 111 and 24 BLD (AD) 282 = 9 BLC (AD) 272. We have carefully gone through the decisions but the citations as referred by the learned Advocate for the appellants have no manner of application so far the points involved in the present case and those decisions will not any way help the learned Advocate for the appellant.

23. Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case we find no merit in this appeal.

24. In the result, the appeal is dismissed without any order as to cost and the order of the trial court dated 8-5-2016 is affirmed. The connected rule being Civil Rule No. 396 (FM) 2016 is discharged and the order of status-quo granted at the time of admission of the appeal is hereby vacated.

Let a copy of the judgment be sent to the concerned court expeditiously.

End.

full_judgment:
Md Nazrul Islam Talukder J: This is an application under Article 102(2)(a) (ii) of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh filed by the petitioner challenging impugned Notices contained in Memo being স্মারক নং-০০.০১.০০০০.৫০১.০১.০৯৫.১৮.২৫৫৯০ dated 16-8-2018 and Memo being স্মারক নং-০০.০১.০০০০.৫০১.০১.০৯৫.১৮.২৫৫৯৪ dated 28-8-2018 both issued under sections 19 of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004 and Rule 20 of the Anti-Corruption Commission Rules, 2007 read with section 160 of the Code of Criminal Procedure issued by Respondent No. 2 (Annexure-A and C).

2. The fact of the writ petition as stated in the application runs as follows:—

The petitioner is an established businessman and a regular tax payer. He is a renowned and respectable politician of the country. At present, he is a member of the Standing Committee of the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP). He was a former Minister, Ministry of Commerce. It is alleged in the application that the Respondent No.2 at the instance of the government in order to harass and humiliate the petitioner issued a notice contained in Memo being স্মারক নং-০০.০১.০০০০.৫০১.০১.০৯৫.১৮.২৫৫৯৪ dated 16-8-2018 under sections 19 of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004 and Rule 20 of the Anti-Corruption Commission Rules, 2007 read with section 160 of the Code of Criminal Procedure upon the petitioner for holding a hearing in respect of some false and fictitious allegations against him such as doing business of five star hotel in another's name, money laundering, purchasing share in the name of his wife and family members and acquiring wealth beyond the known source of income. Having received the notice, the petitioner by a letter dated 28-8-2018 expressed his inability to appear before the Respondent No.2 on 28-8-2018 and sought for one month time for the reasons mentioning that he needed some papers and preparations to give reply to the allegations properly and accurately. It is alleged in the application that Respondent No.2 without considering the aforesaid letter of the petitioner arbitrarily issued the second notice contained in Memo being স্মারক নং-০০.০১.০০০০.৫০১.০১.০৯৫.১৮.২৫৫৯৪ dated 28-8-2018 similar to the earlier one asking the petitioner to appear before him at 10-00 am on 10-9-2018.

3. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid notices dated 16-8-2018 and 28-8-2018 issued by Respondent No. 2, the petitioner has filed this writ petition before this court.

4. At the very outset, Mr Moudud Ahmed, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner, submits that the impugned notices dated 16-8-2018 and 28-8-2018 issued by Respondent No. 2 are illegal, unlawful and of no legal effect as Respondent No. 2 has no jurisdiction and authority to issue such notices upon the petitioner under section 19 of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004 and Rule 20 of the Anti-Corruption Commission Rules, 2007. He next submits that the petitioner has been shown as an accused in the so-called enquiry as has been started against the petitioner by Respondent No.2 and for this reason, section 19 of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004 and Rule 20 of the Anti-Corruption Rules, 2007 are not applicable in this case as the petitioner is not an accused as yet and as such, the impugned notices dated 16-8-2018 and 28-8-2018 are not tenable in the eye of law and the same are liable to be knocked down for ends of justice.

5. He then submits that since the respondents have decided to hold an enquiry upon hearing the petitioner showing him as an accused section 22 of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004 read with Rule 8 of the Anti-Corruption Rules, 2007 are very much applicable to the case of the petitioner and as the respondents have failed to comply with the provisions of law, the impugned notices are malafide and of without jurisdiction. He further submits that as per sections 19(2) of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004, the Anti-Corruption Commission can ask for document or information from the witness or from the third party because the word 'any person' in section 19(2) of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004 is only applicable for the witnesses/third parties, not for the accused person and as such, the issuance of notices upon the petitioner is not legal and to no legal effect. In support of his submissions, Mr Ahmed has referred to a decision taken in the case of Moudud Ahmed vs Anti-Corruption Commission passed in Writ Petition No. 8668 of 2012 wherein it was held that 'any person' in section 19(2) of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004 does not include an accused.

6. He lastly submits that since a Rule Nisi on the similar, subject-matter issued in Writ Petition No. 8668 of 2012 was made absolute by a Division Bench on 14-3-2016, this court being not deviated from the views taken in that writ petition should issue Rule and stay the impugned notices.

7. Mr Moudud Ahmed, the learned Advocate in support of his contentions has referred to a photocopy of the judgment passed in Writ Petition No.8668 of 2012 along with the Rule issuing orders passed in Writ Petition No. 3207 of 2018 and Writ Petition No. 11335 of 2018 and the order dated 17-5-2018 passed in Civil Petition for Leave To Appeal No.1653 of 2018 preferred against the order dated 5-3-2018 passed by High Court Division in Writ Petition No. 3207 of 2018.

8. On the other hand, Mr Khurshid Alam Khan, the learned Advocate appearing for the Anti-Corruption Commission, submits that the Anti-Corruption Commission has right, authority and jurisdiction to issue and serve notice upon any person under the provisions of section 19 of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004 read with section 160 of the Code of Criminal Procedure directing him/her to furnish information relevant to enquiry or investigation as the case may be and as such, the notices issued by Respondents No.2 on behalf of the Anti-Corruption Commission are not illegal, malafide, motivated and unconstitutional in nature and as such, the writ petition should be rejected. He further submits that the words "any person" in section 19(2) of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004 clearly indicate that it does not only refer to the witness/third party rather includes witness/ third party/accused against whom the allegations of the schedule offences have been brought.

9. He next submits that in the instant case, the notices were issued and served upon the petitioner not showing him as an accused but as a person against whom allegations of the schedule offences have been brought and even the notices have been issued upon the petitioner under section 19 of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004 read with Rule 20 of the Anti-Corruption Commission Rules, 2007, there is no bar to proceeding of enquiry against the petitioner initiated by the Anti-Corruption Commission and for this reason, the writ petition is liable to be rejected. He then submits that even if the petitioner is not an accused at this stage, the provision of section 22 of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004 and Rule 8 of the Anti-Corruption Commission Rules, 2007, in addition, are also applicable to the case of the petitioner in the instant case and considering the aforesaid aspects of the matter, the writ petition should be rejected.

10. He categorically submits that the judgment in Writ Petition No.8668 of 2012 were pronounced by the High Court Division on 14-3-2016 but the judgment on the similar subject matter in the case of Sonali Jute Mills Limited vs Anti-Corruption Commission, reported in 22 BLC (AD) 147 was delivered by the Appellate Division on 29-5-2016, wherein it was decided that "sub-sections (1) and (2) of section 19 have given wide jurisdiction to the Commission to enquire into and investigate any allegations whatsoever as covered in its schedule and in doing so may direct any authority, public or private to produce relevant documents. The person concerned shall be bound to comply with the said direction. The power contained in section 19 of the Ain can exercise both at inquiry as well as investigation stage."

11. Mr Md Khurshid Alam Khan, the learned Advocate appearing for the Anti-Corruption Commission, in support of his submissions, has placed before us another decision passed by High Court Division in the case of Sonali Jute Mills Limited vs Anti-Corruption Commission, reported in 18 BLC 723. Mr Khan further on the similar matter and similar legal point has mentioned about a decision taken in the case of Shahidullah Minh (Md) vs Government of Bangladesh reported in 66 DLR 444, Where in it was held that "on the allegation of corruption on any subject matter as well as on the allegation of commission of schedule offences, the Commissioner or the officers of the Commission entrusted with the power to enquire is empowered under section 19 of the Ain, 2004 read with Rules 8 and 20 of the Anti-Corruption Rules, 2007 to direct the person, against whom a complaint is made, to appear before the Commission to give explanation either orally or in writing, with a view to find out the correctness of the allegation issuance of the order directing the petitioner and 4 others to appear before the Commission to record their statements does not suffer from any illegality requiring interference by this court." Mr Khan lastly submits that the purpose of the notice is to ask the petitioner to appear before the commission to have a hearing in respect of the allegations brought against him and under the appropriate circumstances, the notices under section 19 and Rule 20 of the Act/Rules or under section 22 or Rule 8 of the Act/Rules may be issued as per requirement and necessity of the Anti-Corruption Commission and there is no illegality in it because such notices may be issued upon an accused or any person against whom allegations have been brought for the purpose of enquiry and investigation but the petitioner in order to avoid the inquiry with Malafide intention has filed the instant writ petition and on the aforesaid landscapes, the writ petition may be rejected.

12. In view of the submissions and counter-submissions advanced by the learned Advocate for the respective parties, we want to come a decision whether the notices were served upon the petitioner lawfully or not. In order to appreciate the same, we want to reproduce the notice dated 28-8-2018 verbatim:-

দুর্নীতি দমন কমিশন

প্রধান কার্যালয়

১, সেগুন বাগিচা, ঢাকা।

স্মারক নং-০০.০১.০০০০.৫০১.০১.০৯৫.১৮.২৫৯৯০

তারিখঃ ১৬-৮-২০১৮ইং

বিষয়ঃ অভিযোগ সংশ্লিষ্ট ব্যক্তির বক্তব্য শ্রবণ ও গ্রহণ প্রসংগে নোটিশ (কমিশন আইনের ১৯ ধারা ও কমিশন বিধিমালার ২০ বিধিসহ ফৌজদারী কার্যবিধির ১৬০ ধারা দ্রষ্টব্য)।

সূত্রঃ দুর্নীতি দমন কমিশন, প্রধান কার্যালয়, ঢাকার নথি নং ০০.০১.০০০০.৫০১.০১.০৯৫.১৮-২৫১৯৩

তারিখঃ ১৩-৮-২০১৮ইং

এতদ্বারা জানানো যাচ্ছে যে, নিম্নলিখিত অভিযোগের অনুসন্ধানপূর্বক প্রতিবেদন দাখিলের জন্য নিম্নস্বাক্ষরকারীকে অনুসন্ধানকারী কর্মকর্তা নিয়োগ করা হয়েছে।

অভিযোগের সংক্ষিপ্ত বিবরণঃ

জনাব আমির খসরু মাহমুদ চৌধুরী, সাবেক মন্ত্রী ও সভাপতি, চট্টগ্রাম চেম্বার অব কমার্স এর বিরুদ্ধে বেনামে পাঁচ তারকা হোটেল ব্যবসা, ব্যাংকে কোটি কোটি টাকা অবৈধ লেনদেনসহ মানিলন্ডারিং করে বিভিন্ন দেশে অর্থ পাচার এবং নিজ, স্ত্রী ও পরিবারের অন্যান্য সদস্যদের নামে শেয়ার ক্রয়সহ জ্ঞাত আয় বহির্ভূত সম্পদ অর্জনের অভিযোগ ।

সুষ্ঠু অনুসন্ধানের স্বার্থে আপনার বক্তব্য শ্রবণ ও গ্রহণ করা একান্ত প্রয়োজন।

বিধায়, উল্লিখিত অভিযোগের বিষয়ে আগামী ২৮-৮-২০১৮ খ্রিঃ তারিখ বেলা ১০ ঘটিকায় নিম্নস্বাক্ষরকারীর

কার্যালয়ে উপস্থিত হয়ে বক্তব্য প্রদানের জন্য আপনাকে বিনীত অনুরোধ করা হল।

প্রাপক

জনাব আমির খসরু মাহমুদ চৌধুরী

৩৩, মেহেদীবাগ, থানাঃ চক বাজার

জেলাঃ চট্টগ্রাম ।

কাজী শফিকুল আলম

পরিচালক

দুনীতি দমন কমিশন

প্রধান কার্যালয়, ঢাকা।

13. On the prayer of the petitioner, one month time was allowed and the petitioner was further directed to appear before the commission by a second notice issued by the commission which runs as follows:—

দ্বিতীয়

নোটিশ

দুর্নীতি দমন কমিশন

প্রধান কার্যালয়

১, সেগুন বাগিচা, ঢাকা ।

স্মারক নং: ০০.০১.০০০০.৫০১.০১.০৯৫.১৮.২৫৯৯৪

তারিখঃ ২৮-৮-২০১৮ইং

বিষয়ঃ অভিযোগ সংশ্লিষ্ট ব্যক্তির বক্তব্য শ্রবণ ও গ্রহণ প্রসংগে নোটিশ (কমিশন আইনের ১৯ ধারা ও কমিশন

বিধিমালার ২০ বিধিসহ ফৌজদারী কার্যবিধির ১৬০ ধারা দ্রষ্টব্য)।

সূত্রঃ দুর্নীতি দমন কমিশন, প্রধান কার্যালয়, ঢাকার নথি নং ০০.০১.০০০০.৫০১.০১.০৯৫.১৮-২৫১৯৩

তারিখঃ ১৩-৮-২০১৮ইৎ।

এতদ্বারা জানানো যাচ্ছে যে, নিম্নলিখিত অভিযোগের বিষয়ে অনুসন্ধানপূর্বক প্রতিবেদন দাখিলের জন্য নিম্নস্বাক্ষরকারীকে অনুসন্ধানকারী কর্মকর্তা নিয়োগ করা হয়েছে।

অভিযোগের সংক্ষিপ্ত বিবরণঃ

জনাব আমির খসরু মাহমুদ চৌধুরী, সাবেক মন্ত্রী ও সভাপতি, চট্টগ্রাম চেম্বার অব কমার্স এর বিরুদ্ধে বেনামে পাচ তারকা হোটেল ব্যবসা, ব্যাংকে কোটি কোটি টাকা অবৈধ লেনদেনসহ মামিলন্ডারিং করে বিভিন্ন দেশে অর্থ পাচার এবং নিজ, স্ত্রী ও পরিবারের অন্যান্য সদস্যদের নামে শেয়ার ক্রয়সহ জ্ঞাত আয় বহির্ভূত সম্পদ অর্জনের অভিযোগ ।

সুষ্ঠ অনুসন্ধানের স্বার্থে আপনার বক্তব্য শ্রবণ ও গ্রহণ করা একান্ত প্রয়োজন । বিধায়, উল্লিখিত অভিযোগের বিষয়ে স্মারক নং: ০০.০১.০০০০.৫০১.০১.০৯৫.১৮-২৫৯৯০, তারিখঃ ১৬-৮-২০১৮ইং মূলে ২৮-৮-২০১৮ খ্রিঃ তারিখ বেলা ১০ ঘটিকায় নিমস্বাক্ষরকারীর কার্যালয়ে উপস্থিত হয়ে বক্তব্য প্রদানের জন্য আপনাকে বিনীত অনুরোধ করে নোটিশ প্রদান করা হয়েছিল; কিন্তু আপনি নোটিশ মোতাবেক দুদকে উপস্থিত হয়ে বক্তব্য প্রদান করেননি ।

এমতাবস্থায়, আগামী ১০-৯-২০১৮ খিঃ তারিখে বেলা ১০ ঘটিকায় নিন্নস্বাক্ষরক��রীর কার্যালয়ে উপস্থিত হয়ে বক্তব্য প্রদানের জন্য আপনাকে পুনরায় অনুরোধ করা হল। নির্ধারিত সময়ে উপস্থিত হতে ব্যর্থ হলে আপনার বিরদ্ধে দুর্নীতি দমন কমিশন আইন, ২০০৪ এর ১৯৩) ধারা মোতাবেক ব্যবস্থা গ্রহণ করা হবে।

প্রাপক

জনাব আমির খসরু মাহমুদ চৌধুরী

পিতাঃ মাহমুদুন্নবী চৌধুরী,

৩৩, মেহেদীবাগ, থানাঃ চক বাজার

জেলাঃ চট্টগ্রাম ।	কাজী শফিকুল আলম

পরিচালক

দুর্নীতি দমন কমিশন

প্রধান কার্যালয়, ঢাকা ।

14. One of the arguments of the learned Advocate for the petitioner is that the notices should have been served upon the petitioner under section 22 of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004 and Rule 8 of the Anti-Corruption Commission Rules, 2007 instead of section 19 of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004 and Rule 20 of the Anti-Corruption Commission Rules, 2007 read with section 160 of the Code of Criminal Procedure.

Section 19 of the Anti-Corruption Commission, 2004 runs as follows:—

১৭। অনুসন্ধান বা তদন্তকার্যে কমিশনের বিশেষ ক্ষমতা।-(১) দুনীতি সম্পর্কিত কোন অভিযোগের অনুসন্ধান বা তদন্তের ক্ষেত্রে, কমিশনের নিম্নরূপ ক্ষমতা থাকিবে, যথাঃ-

(ক) সাক্ষীর প্রতি নোটিশ জারী ও উপস্থিত নিশ্চিতকরণ এবং স্বাক্ষীকে জিজ্ঞাসাবাদ করা;

(খ) কোন দলিল উদঘাটন এবং উপস্থাপন করা;

(গ) সাক্ষ্য গ্রহণ;

(ঘ) কোন আদালত বা অফিস হইতে পাবলিক রেকর্ড বা উহার অনুলিপি তলব করা;

(ঙ) সাক্ষীর জিজ্ঞাসাবাদ এবং দলিল পরীক্ষা করার জন্য পরোয়ানা জারি করা; এবং

(চ) এই আইনের উদ্দেশ্য পূরণকল্পে, নির্ধারিত অন্য যে কোন বিষয়।

So, for the convenience of discussions, we want to quote all the relevant laws asunder:—

(২) কমিশন, যে কোন ব্যক্তিকে অনুসন্ধান বা তদন্ত সংশ্লিষ্ট বিষয়ে কোন তথ্য সরবরাহ করিবার জন্য নির্দেশ দিতে পারিবে এবং অনুরূপভাবে নির্দেশিত ব্যক্তি তাহার হেফাজতে রক্ষিত উক্ত তথ্য সরবরাহ করিতে বাধ্য থাকিবেন।

15. We have gone through the application under Article 102 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh and the materials annexed therewith. We have also heard the learned Advocates for the respective parties and considered their submissions to the best of our wit and wisdom. Ongoing through the application, we find that Respondent No.2 issued a notice upon the petitioner in order to hear him in respect of the allegations. It is evident from the application that the petitioner having received the notice submitted an application before Respondent No.2 seeking one month time for collecting necessary materials. Upon receiving the application, Respondent No.2 allowed the same giving one month time and directed him to appear before Respondent No.2, on 10-9-2018. However, instead of appearing before Respondent No.2, the petitioner feeling aggrieved by the impugned notices approached this court with an application challenging the impugned notices directing him to appear before Respondent No.2. As per submission of the learned Advocate for the petitioner, Respondent No.2 is not authorized by section 19(2) to issue any notice upon the petitioner directing him to appear before Respondent No.2. From the decision in the case, of Moudud Ahmed vs Anti-Corruption Commission passed in Writ Petition No. 8668 of 2012 referred to by the learned Advocate for the petitioner, it appears that the words "any person" means the person other than the accused and in other words, the same includes only the witness or other persons save and except the accused.

16. It is pertinent to note that the aforesaid judgment cited by the learned Advocate for the petitioner was delivered by High Court Division on 14-3-2016 but on 29-5-2016 that is immediately after the judgment of High Court Division, Appellate Division in the case of Sonali Jute Mills Limited vs Anti-Corruption Commission and others reported in 22 BLC (AD) 147 pronounced the judgment affirming the judgment of High Court Division in the case of Sonali Jute Mills Limited vs Anti-Corruption Commission reported in 18 BLC 723. In the case of Sonali Jute Mills Limited vs Anti-Corruption Commission reported in 22 BLC (AD) 147, it was held as under:—

"Sub-section (1) and (2) of section 19 have given wide jurisdiction to the Commission to enquire into and investigate any allegations whatsoever as covered in its schedule and in doing so may direct any authority, public or private to produce relevant documents. The person concerned shall be bound to comply with the said direction. The power contained in section 19 of the Ain can exercise both at inquiry as well as investigation stage."

17. Apart from this, The High Court Division pronounced a judgment on the similar legal points in the case of Shahidullah Miah (Md) vs Government of Bangladesh reported in 66 DLR 444 wherein it was held as under:—

"On the allegation of corruption on any subject matter as well as on the allegation of commission of schedule offences, the Commissioner or the officers of the Commission entrusted with the power to enquire is empowered under section 19 of the Ain, 2004 read with rules 8 and 20 of the Rules, 2007 to direct the person, against whom a complaint is made, to appear before the Commission to give explanation either orally or in writing, with a view to find out the correctness of the allegation. Issuance of the order directing the petitioner and 4 others to appear before the Commission to record their statements does not suffer from any illegality requiring interference by this court."

<u>18. We have meticulously examined sections 19/20/22 of the Anti- Corruption Commission Act, 2004 as well as Rules 8/20 of the Anti-Corruption Commission Rules, 2007 along with section 160 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. It may be mentioned that the Rules are framed in order to implement the purpose and intent of the Act. On a close perusal of the provisions of section 19 of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004, it appears that the purpose of this section so far relating to issuance of notice are twofold-one is to issue notice upon the witness/third parties for interrogation, examination and production of documents if required and the other is to issue notice upon "any person" under sub-section 2 of section 19 of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004, which includes an accused against whom an FIR has been lodged disclosing his involvement and a person against whom allegations of the schedule offences of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004 have been primarily brought.</u>

<u>19. It may be noted that the rights of an accused or a person against whom allegations have been brought, of being heard before proceeding against them in any manner are statutory rights which have been given to them under section 22 of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004. In view of the above provision of laws, the reasonable opportunity of being heard as a course of statutory rights under section 22 of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004 may be given to an accused and to a person during the proceeding of enquiry or investigation against whom allegations have been brought for their safeguard so that none can be implicated and harassed in any case in any manner before starting any legal proceeding. If upon hearing the accused or any person against whom allegations have been brought, the Anti-Corruption Commission becomes satisfied that the allegations so brought are false vague, frivolous and preposterous, the said accused or any person so framed may be not sent up/discharged from the proceeding of enquiry or investigation.</u>

20. Accordingly, we are of the view that the purpose of section 19 of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004 is not one fold and the provisions of section 19 of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004 are not only applicable to the witness rather those are equally, practically and reasonably applicable to witness/accused/third parties/any person against whom allegations have been brought.

<u>21. Upon perusal and examination of the provisions of law, we are of the opinion that the notices upon the accused or any person may be served under section 19 of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004 read with Rule 8 of the Anti-Corruption Commission Rules, 2007 as well as under section 22 of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004 read with Rule 8 of the Anti-Corruption Commission Rules, 2007 if the Anti-Corruption Commission thinks necessary to hear any person connected with the allegations. And the notices upon the witnesses may be served under section 19 of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004 read with Rule 20 of the Anti-Corruption Commission Rules, 2007. Here, in the instant case, the notices have been served upon the petitioner under section 19 of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004 along with Rule 20 of the Anti-Corruption Commission Rules, 2007 though the said Rule 20 is practically applicable to calling the witness but in spite of adding Rule 20 of the Anti-Corruption Commission Rules, 2007 with section 19 of the Anti-Corruption Act, 2004 on the top of notices does not affect the legality and propriety of the notices served upon the petitioner because the substantive section 19 of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004 is there on the notices. Therefore, it may be said that not-mentioning of relevant Rules in the notice/s will not affect the validity of notice/s if the substantive section/s of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004 is/are mentioned in the notice/s.</u>

22. Before parting with the matter, we want to address another aspect of the case which has emerged before this court during hearing of this application and the submissions made by the learned Advocate for the petitioner. The definite and specific argument of the learned Advocate for the petitioner is that the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004 should have issued notices upon the petitioner under section 22 of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004 read with Rule 8 of the Anti-Corruption Commission Rule, 2007 instead of section 19 of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004 read with Rule 20 of the Anti-Corruption Commission Rules, 2007.

23. It is an undisputed fact that the Anti-Corruption Commission has right and authority to call upon any witness or any person against whom allegations of the schedule offences have been brought in order to have hearing from them as a recourse of fact finding proceedings. Furthermore, it is not the case of the petitioner that the subject-matter of the notice does not fall within the scope and ambit of the provisions of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004. As per submission of the learned Advocate for the petitioner, if we, for the sake of argument, hold mat Anti-Corruption Commission issued the notice upon the petitioner under the wrong sections and rules, the question arises whether notices can be treated as invalid by reason of mistake, defect or omission of laws/rules in the notice/s.

24. In view of the above discussions, our considered view is that if the notices, in substance and effect, are in conformity with or according to the intent and purpose of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004, the notices cannot be invalidated by the reason of any mistake of section/rule whatsoever in the notice. If there is any mistake of section /rule in the notices, those may be allowed to be cured, otherwise the very purpose and object of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004 would be frustrated and defeated. The purpose of issuing notice is to call upon the petitioner to submit information disclosing whether he is involved in that regard or not. Here, what we want to say is that even if a wrong provision of law/rule is mentioned in the notice or notices, the same does not invalidate the proceeding of enquiry or investigation. It may be concluded saying that by mentioning of a wrong provision of law or non-mentioning of a provision of law on the application/order/notice does not invalidate the same if the court and /or statutory authority had the requisite jurisdiction there for.

25. In view of aforesaid elaborate discussions, the case laws cited on behalf of petitioner being distinguishable from the point of law at hand as settled by the Appellate Division do not help the petitioner anyway.

26. Having heard the learned Advocates for the respective parties, keeping in view the arguments made by them and carefully going through the materials placed on the record along with impugned notices and the propositions of law cited and discussed above, we do not find any illegality in the notices as served upon the petitioner under section 19 of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004 and Rule 20 of the Anti-Corruption Commissions Rules 2007 rather those were issued as a safeguard to protect the interest of the petitioner against whom allegations have been brought so that he could defend false, vague, frivolous and preposterous allegations during the proceeding of enquiry or investigation.

27. Accordingly, we do not find any merit in this application.

Consequently, the application under Article 102 of Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh filed by the petitioner is summarily rejected.
